title: Calls grow for audit of Labor finances
summary: Economists including Saul Eslake, Shane Oliver and Cherelle Murphy are calling for an independent review of federal spending, after figures showed government spending reached 26.9% of GDP and recent budget decisions delivered no net savings. Assistant Treasurer Daniel Mulino rejected a formal audit, saying the government’s budget processes are enough, while critics say a review could identify waste and help ease pressure on inflation, debt and household budgets.
ticker_line: Economists call for review of federal spending
author: MATTHEW CRANSTON
heading: Economy

title: Banks sitting on billions in customer savings that do not grow with interest rate hikes
summary: The big four banks raised some savings rates after the latest Reserve Bank increase, but many customers may miss out because bonus rates have strict conditions, while billions of dollars remain in accounts earning no interest. Consumer advocates say banks should better alert customers when they are at risk of missing bonus interest, and urge savers to check whether their accounts still suit them.
ticker_line: Strict conditions leave savers missing out on rate rises
author: reporters Adelaide Miller
heading: Banking

title: Exclusive: PM attacks RBA use of 'blunt instrument'
summary: Anthony Albanese called interest rate rises a “blunt instrument” that hurts mortgage holders as the Reserve Bank prepares for a possible fifth increase this year. He defended government spending, promised savings in December’s budget update and promoted a growth agenda, while facing criticism over productivity, cost-of-living pressures and Labor’s falling poll support.
ticker_line: Albanese criticises rate rises as mortgage pain grows
author: Paul Sakkal and James Massola
heading: Economy

title: Garth Hamilton says Liberal Party set to shift on superannuation
summary: Liberal MP Garth Hamilton says he has majority support in the party room to rule out changes to super, including allowing people to withdraw it early for a first home deposit. The shift would put him at odds with senior Liberals Andrew Bragg and Tim Wilson, who have backed using super to help people buy homes.
ticker_line: Liberals may rule out early super access for housing
author: by Insiders host David Sp
heading: Superannuation

title: Banks are quietly gutting credit card perks. Here’s what you stand to lose
summary: Banks are cutting credit card rewards and perks, with significant changes coming on October 1, 2026. ANZ and NAB are reducing sign-up bonuses, increasing spending requirements, and raising interest rates, while Westpac is limiting insurance benefits on its cards.
ticker_line: Banks slash credit card rewards and perks
author: Nicole Pedersen-McKinnon
heading: Banking

title: Labor in high-stakes negotiations with Trump admin to unlock superpowered AI
summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's government is negotiating with the US to gain access to powerful AI models for critical infrastructure in Australia, aiming to enhance national security and competitiveness in the AI sector. This comes after the US lifted a ban on foreign access to these models due to safety concerns.
ticker_line: Australia seeks access to powerful AI models
author: Paul Sakkal
heading: AI

title: Interest rates: Economists warn rate rises still on horizon
summary: Economists warn that Australia may see another interest rate rise this year due to ongoing inflation pressures and rising oil prices from the Middle East conflict. The Reserve Bank of Australia is expected to keep a tough stance on inflation despite recent softer consumer price reports.
ticker_line: Interest rates may rise again amid inflation concerns
author: Cecile Lefort
heading: Economy

title: The Pipeline
summary: ASIC has announced it can override non-disclosure agreements to encourage whistleblowers from the big four consulting firms to come forward. Meanwhile, a judge highlighted the risks of AI in court after ChatGPT provided false information about a legal judgment.
ticker_line: ASIC encourages big four whistleblowers amid AI concerns
author: Edmund Tadros and Janek Drevikovsky
heading: Regulation

title: Chinese AI models are getting better and cheaper and Australian businesses are taking notice
summary: Chinese AI models are improving and becoming cheaper, prompting Australian businesses to adopt them for cost savings. Companies are increasingly using a mix of Chinese and American AI models to manage expenses and efficiency, despite concerns about trust and regulation.
ticker_line: Australian firms embrace cheaper Chinese AI models
author: business Lin Lin
heading: AI

title: ASIC rip-off crackdown eyes private credit
summary: ASIC is investigating private credit lenders for possible interest rate miscalculations, following issues found in banks. ASIC's chair, Sarah Court, is pushing for better practices in the sector and hinted at potential legal action against banks.
ticker_line: ASIC targets private credit lenders for scrutiny
author: David Ross
heading: Regulation

title: NAB reveals 15pc plunge in new home loans
summary: National Australia Bank (NAB) reported a 15% drop in new home loan applications for the June quarter, reflecting a tough housing market. While overall loans increased by 4%, concerns about business borrowers are rising, with more loans classified as 'on watch' due to economic challenges.
ticker_line: NAB reports 15% drop in home loans
author: David Ross
heading: Banking

title: PM’s big seniors moment
summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's plan to cut higher private health insurance rebates for seniors is facing backlash from state governments, who warn it could strain public hospitals as many older Australians may drop their coverage. The policy aims to save $3 billion over four years but has raised concerns about its impact on low-income pensioners and the public health system.
ticker_line: Seniors' health insurance rebates face cuts
author: GREG BROWN, Chief Political Corresp
heading: Health Insurance

title: AI test as youth protest
summary: Tasmania's youth are protesting against AI development plans, demanding action from politicians as top AI scientists warn of risks from rapid AI growth. The state government supports AI adoption but aims to ensure it is done safely and ethically.
ticker_line: Youth protest AI plans amid safety concerns
author: Elise Kaine
heading: AI

title: Exclusive: How PM could force states' hand on green data centres
summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese plans to push for renewable energy rules for data centres at a national cabinet meeting, despite opposition from Queensland and Northern Territory leaders who support fossil fuels. A majority of states have agreed to a scheme requiring data centres to prove they use renewable energy, amid a surge in data centre construction projected to reach $155 billion.
ticker_line: PM pushes for renewable energy in data centres
author: Paul Sakkal and Mike Foley
heading: Regulation

title: ‘Aspiration clashing with reality’: Investors cool on data centres
summary: Investors are losing interest in data centres due to planning delays and community concerns about power and water use. A recent survey shows only 38% of institutions are considering investing in data centres, down from 70% last year.
ticker_line: Investor interest in data centres declines sharply
author: Jenny Wiggins
heading: Investments

title: Inflation ‘everywhere’ as profit growth slows
summary: Australia's corporate profits grew by 11.6% in FY26, but excluding mining and energy, growth was only 5.3%. Analysts expect slower profit growth ahead, rising inflation, and potential interest rate hikes, creating a cautious outlook for the market.
ticker_line: Corporate profits rise but growth slows down
author: DAVID ROGERS, EXCHANGE
heading: Economy

title: Super funds on alert as credit cracks appear
summary: Major super funds are concerned about problems in Australia's $200 billion private credit market after the collapse of Bathla Group, which owes $3.6 billion to creditors. Super funds are becoming more cautious with their lending and looking for better opportunities overseas as interest rates rise and defaults are expected to increase.
ticker_line: Super funds cautious as credit market faces issues
author: Cliona O’Dowd
heading: Superannuation

title: AI, smart glasses the focus of new laws
summary: The federal government is proposing new privacy laws to address concerns around smart glasses and artificial intelligence. Key changes include a right for Australians to have their personal information deleted from social media and a new IDLock system for better control over identity documents.
ticker_line: New privacy laws target AI and smart glasses
author: James Massola | Chief political com
heading: Regulation

title: Unions want big tech to pay levy to build Australian-owned AI
summary: Unions and AI researchers are urging the Australian government to impose a levy on big tech companies that want to build data centres in Australia. This levy would help fund a local AI industry, ensuring Australia develops its own technology rather than relying on foreign firms.
ticker_line: Unions push for tech levy to boost local AI
author: by political Hol
heading: AI

title: The painful price of four years of RBA rate rises
summary: Monthly repayments on a typical new 30-year home loan have more than doubled, from $2,354 in April 2022 to $4,819 in October 2026, as the average loan grew and the RBA raised its cash rate. After inflation reached 4.3 per cent, markets put the chance of another rate rise by December at 80 per cent; first-home buyer demand was down 22.1 per cent over the year to September.
ticker_line: Mortgage repayments more than double as rates rise
author: Anthony Keane
heading: Economy

title: EXCLUSIVE: PM's razor gang hinders treasurer's saving plans
summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers reportedly pushed for lower spending and more revenue measures before May’s budget, but Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and his allies on Labor’s spending committee did not approve some proposals. The government says it will seek savings in December’s budget update to ease inflation, but has not promised they will fully cover new spending as rising costs and blocked measures put pressure on the budget.
ticker_line: Albanese’s spending committee limits Chalmers’ savings push
author: Paul Sakkal
heading: Economy

title: Allan govt unveils $14m rescue package as it braces for AI-driven job losses
summary: The Allan government has announced a $14 million package to help Victorian workers facing job losses due to AI. The plan includes an $8.2 million career rescue scheme and a new TAFE centre to support those in at-risk industries.
ticker_line: Victoria launches $14m AI job rescue package
author: Alex White
heading: AI

title: NAB fixed interest rate hike signals more pain to come for borrowers
summary: National Australia Bank (NAB) has raised its fixed mortgage rates by 15 basis points, indicating potential further interest rate hikes ahead. The lowest fixed rate is now 6.49%, and forecasts suggest rates could rise again by August as the Reserve Bank of Australia continues to combat inflation.
ticker_line: NAB raises fixed mortgage rates amid inflation fight
author: Cameron Micallef
heading: Banking

title: Super not an answer to all your tax issues
summary: Recent budget changes have made superannuation a more tax-friendly investment, but it may not be suitable for everyone due to strict withdrawal rules and new taxes on high balances. Many Australians still face financial pressures that make super less appealing for younger age groups.
ticker_line: Superannuation gains but still not for all
author: ANTHONY KEANE
heading: Superannuation

title: Missing flood data hits 25,000
summary: Over 25,000 property owners in Logan have been informed that council flood maps over-estimated water levels by 1 metre. This finding, from an independent review, has raised concerns about property values and insurance costs.
ticker_line: Logan flood maps over-estimate water levels by 1m
author: Judith Kerr
heading: General Insurance

title: Forget banks, super funds are now too big to fail
summary: Australia's financial system passed a stress test that highlighted risks between banks and super funds, revealing their deep connections. With super funds now holding over $4 trillion, they are becoming too big to fail, raising concerns about potential market stress during economic downturns.
ticker_line: Super funds now seen as too big to fail
author: Eric Johnston
heading: Superannuation

title: Closing Bell: Near-zero rates are closer than you think
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia is preparing for the possibility of near-zero interest rates as economic growth slows. New guidelines will help the RBA respond more effectively to future economic crises by outlining various monetary policy tools beyond just adjusting the cash rate.
ticker_line: RBA prepares for potential near-zero interest rates
author: Anthony Macdonald
heading: Economy

title: Economists douse inflation hopes
summary: Economists warn that inflation in Australia remains high despite Treasurer Jim Chalmers' optimism, with underlying inflation rising and concerns about fuel prices and economic growth persisting. The Reserve Bank may consider another interest rate hike as the government’s fiscal policies clash with efforts to control inflation.
ticker_line: Economists caution on rising inflation risks
author: Luke Kinsella
heading: Economy

title: Mandatory registration begins for NDIS providers
summary: Today marks the start of mandatory registration for NDIS providers, focusing on digital platforms and supported independent living homes. Concerns are rising among small providers about the costs and future changes expected next year.
ticker_line: NDIS providers face new registration rules
heading: Regulation

title: Bill shock has CEOs eyeing cheaper AI models
summary: Westpac's CEO Anthony Miller is cautious about rising costs from using AI, prompting interest in cheaper Chinese AI models. This shift could spark a price war among major US AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic.
ticker_line: Westpac CEOs cautious of rising AI costs
author: Paul Smith | Technology
heading: AI

title: Corporates revolt over AI bill shock
summary: Companies are facing rising costs from using AI tools, leading to a demand for cheaper Chinese models. This price competition is challenging US firms like OpenAI and Anthropic as they prepare for public listings.
ticker_line: Corporates struggle with rising AI costs
author: Paul Smith
heading: AI

title: June sees biggest monthly fall in national housing values since 2022, Cotality finds
summary: In June 2026, national housing values fell by 0.4%, marking the largest monthly drop since 2022, with Sydney and Melbourne experiencing the biggest declines. Factors such as rising interest rates, tax changes, and low affordability are contributing to this downturn in the housing market.
ticker_line: National housing values see largest drop since 2022
author: business Lin Lin
heading: Economy

title: Rise of industry funds: shake-up ahead for Aussie super
summary: Deloitte predicts that industry super funds will grow from 46% to 55% of Australia's superannuation market by 2045, as platform investments and self-managed funds decline. This shift comes after a report highlighted issues in the platform market, including rising advice fees and the collapse of certain funds, affecting many Australians' savings.
ticker_line: Industry super funds set for major growth
author: Kaaren Morrissey
heading: Superannuation

title: RBA readies for economy 'fire drills'
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia plans to cut interest rates more aggressively in future economic downturns instead of relying on unconventional methods like printing money. Assistant Governor Christopher Kent highlighted the need for better preparedness for economic shocks, following lessons learned from the pandemic.
ticker_line: RBA prepares for future economic challenges
author: Shane Wright | Senior economics cor
heading: Economy

title: It’s not our fault, says Labor
summary: Labor is facing criticism for claiming that high interest rates are mainly to blame for low auction clearance rates, while downplaying the impact of its tax reforms. Recent data shows clearance rates have dropped to a six-year low of 49.2%, raising concerns about the housing market and future rent pressures.
ticker_line: Labor blames interest rates for low auction clearance
author: Jessica Wang
heading: Economy

title: NAB calls for national strategy to tackle increase in mortgage fraud
summary: NAB is urging for a national strategy to combat rising mortgage fraud in Australia, estimating $4 billion in fraudulent loans. The bank believes a coordinated approach among banks, regulators, and law enforcement is needed to tackle this widespread issue effectively.
ticker_line: NAB calls for national strategy against mortgage fraud
author: Blair Jackson
heading: Banking

title: ASIC ‘asleep at the wheel’ over junkets
summary: Former senator John Williams criticises ASIC for not addressing the return of lavish perks in financial advice, linked to The Inside Network, which connects fund managers with advisers. He urges ASIC to investigate potential wrongdoing after reforms aimed at preventing conflicts of interest in the industry.
ticker_line: ASIC faces criticism over financial perks issue
author: ELI GREENBLAT
heading: Regulation

title: NDIS fraudsters heading to prison in taskforce blitz
summary: Seventeen people involved in NDIS fraud have been sentenced to over 60 years in prison. The Fraud Fusion Taskforce is actively investigating more cases to recover billions lost to fraud.
ticker_line: NDIS fraudsters sentenced to over 60 years in jail
author: Jessica Wang
heading: Regulation

title: BIS: Investment boom in AI could leave economy in peril
summary: The Bank for International Settlements warns that excessive investment in AI by major companies could lead to economic downturns if profits disappoint, similar to past technology booms. They highlight risks of overinvestment and potential financial instability due to reliance on borrowing for AI projects.
ticker_line: BIS warns of AI investment risks to economy
author: PAUL HANNON
heading: Economy

title: Sticky inflation, cooling housing: RBA's rates dilemma
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia is facing a challenge with high inflation at 3.8% and falling house prices, particularly in Sydney and Melbourne. While inflation remains a priority, the cooling housing market may help reduce spending and inflation pressures over time.
ticker_line: RBA grapples with inflation and falling house prices
author: John Kehoe
heading: Economy

title: CBA forced to scrap fees for the vulnerable
summary: Commonwealth Bank must stop charging fees to low-income customers after regulators rejected its plans for fee-free accounts. The bank will now automatically move 1.5 million vulnerable customers to basic accounts with little or no fees.
ticker_line: CBA forced to eliminate fees for vulnerable customers
author: James Eyers
heading: Banking

title: Big four banks put rate cuts back on the menu after inflation drops
summary: Australia's big four banks expect the Reserve Bank to start cutting interest rates as inflation drops to 3.8%, down from 4%. This change follows a surprising decrease in prices across various goods and services, with economists now predicting a steady cash rate of 4.35% this year.
ticker_line: Big four banks foresee interest rate cuts ahead
author: Shane Wright | Senior economics cor
heading: Economy

title: Tributes for ‘man who moved markets’
summary: Bill Evans, former chief economist at Westpac, passed away at 76 after battling cancer. He was known for his accurate economic insights and influence on market trends, shaping economic policy for over 40 years.
ticker_line: Tributes pour in for market-moving economist Bill Evans
author: Eric Johnston
heading: Economy

title: Council calls for more financial adviser scrutiny
summary: The Financial Services Council wants financial advisers to be monitored more closely, suggesting that the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) should check advice licensees every six months. This comes after two major investment fund failures that lost $1 billion of client money, largely due to adviser recommendations.
ticker_line: FSC calls for stricter oversight of financial advisers
author: Cliona O’Dowd
heading: Regulation

title: Rest circles, with airport stakes back on market
summary: Rest Superannuation is considering buying stakes in Perth Airport as its current owners, The Infrastructure Fund and Australian Retirement Trust, look to sell their combined 9.14% share for at least $600 million. This follows previous unsuccessful sale attempts and comes as Perth Airport sees rising passenger numbers due to strong mining activity in Western Australia.
ticker_line: Rest Superannuation eyes Perth Airport stakes
author: DATA ROOM with BRIDGET CARTER
heading: Investments

title: Labor declares AI biggest sovereignty moment ‘since World War II’
summary: Australia's Defence Minister Richard Marles calls the country's push into artificial intelligence (AI) the most important moment for national self-reliance since World War II. He is heading to the US to secure a $21 billion deal with AI firm Anthropic, aiming to enhance Australia's role in AI development and ensure it is not just a passive player in the tech race against the US and China.
ticker_line: Australia seeks major AI deal with Anthropic
author: Paul Sakkal
heading: AI

title: ASIC warns home owners being left short after accepting cash settlements on insurance claims
summary: ASIC warns that cash settlements from insurers for home insurance claims may leave homeowners underfunded for repairs, causing stress and potential financial loss. The review found that many insurers do not provide clear information on these settlements, raising concerns about their fairness.
ticker_line: ASIC raises concerns over cash settlements for homeowners
author: business Adelaide Miller
heading: General Insurance

title: AXA XL keeps pulling back in soft commercial market as hail lifts AXA’s catastrophe losses
summary: The article could not be accessed, so its details about AXA XL’s pullback and AXA’s catastrophe losses cannot be confirmed from the text provided.
ticker_line: Article unavailable; AXA insurance details unconfirmed
author: Josh Recamara
heading: General Insurance

title: SMSF ban 'would cost 11,500 new homes a year'
summary: The Coalition plans to amend the government’s budget legislation to let self-managed super funds borrow to buy newly built homes, arguing the ban could cost about 11,500 new homes a year. Treasury says the number of affected loans is relatively small and expects the budget’s housing tax changes to have only a modest effect on prices and rents.
ticker_line: Coalition seeks SMSF borrowing exemption for new homes
author: Phillip Coorey
heading: Superannuation

title: ATO, ASIC feared data breach by supplier VIQ Solutions a year before it was public
summary: FOI-released emails show ASIC and the ATO raised concerns in March 2025 that government transcription supplier VIQ Solutions may have sent sensitive ATO data offshore. ASIC treated the incident as a near miss based on VIQ’s report, with no independent check of possible impacts on other agencies; VIQ was later linked to offshore handling of court data and shut down after entering administration.
ticker_line: ASIC and ATO raised early concerns over VIQ data
author: the Specialist Reporting Team's Hei
heading: Regulation

title: Municipal Association of Victoria demands data centre moratorium as planning approvals rise
summary: Victoria’s Municipal Association has called for a pause on approvals for new or expanded data centres until the state sets a comprehensive planning and environmental framework. Councils say the facilities could put pressure on housing, land, energy and water; the state says new rules require renewable energy and non-drinking water and keep data centres away from homes.
ticker_line: Victorian councils demand pause on data centre approvals
author: Leanne Wong
heading: Regulation

title: Exclusive: New cracks in Coalition over trade deal and AI
summary: The Nationals are taking tougher positions on an EU trade deal and AI, widening tensions with the Liberals since the Coalition split. Nationals oppose the trade deal and changes to copyright law that could help AI companies, while Liberal leader Angus Taylor is seeking bipartisan support for AI reform and has criticised the proposed EU agreement.
ticker_line: Nationals deepen Coalition rift over trade and AI
author: Paul Sakkal
heading: AI

title: The data centre mega-hub being quietly mapped out in Melbourne’s west
summary: A large data centre hub, called the Victorian AI Hub, is planned for Plumpton, Melbourne, covering 350 hectares and aiming for 2.4 gigawatts of power capacity. The project, developed by Syncline Energy, is expected to create thousands of jobs and support Victoria's tech industry, but it faces planning challenges due to its size and location.
ticker_line: Massive data centre planned for Melbourne's west
author: Daniella White
heading: AI

title: Macquarie could disrupt big four's 'lazy' $370b edge
summary: Macquarie is challenging Australia's big four banks by offering higher interest rates on savings, which could significantly impact the banks' profits. Analysts warn that if the major banks respond by raising rates, their earnings could drop by up to 40%.
ticker_line: Macquarie disrupts big banks with higher savings rates
author: Angira Bharadwaj
heading: Banking

title: Labor's new homes numbers $14b off RBA's
summary: The federal budget predicts $13.7 billion more investment in new housing than the Reserve Bank, suggesting the government may have overestimated housing supply by over 10,000 homes. This discrepancy raises concerns about meeting Labor's goal of 1.2 million new homes.
ticker_line: Budget housing investment forecasts raise concerns
author: Luke Kinsella
heading: Economy

title: HESTA backs $70m VC fund for med tech stars
summary: HESTA is investing $70 million in Synthesis Capital, a new venture capital firm focused on early-stage Australian health and medical technology start-ups. The fund aims to connect local scientists with global investors and address funding challenges in the sector.
ticker_line: HESTA invests $70m in med tech venture fund
author: Tess Bennett
heading: Investments

title: Social impact investors 'can fix NDIS'
summary: Michael Traill proposes a major change to the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) by consolidating its 270,000 providers into a few large operators backed by social impact investors to improve efficiency and save costs. This plan aims to address the scheme's financial issues and achieve $185 billion in budget savings over the next decade.
ticker_line: Traill's bold plan to reform NDIS funding
author: Michael Smith | Health
heading: General Insurance

title: Economic gap between older and younger generations on track to reach record levels
summary: A report shows the economic gap between younger and older Australians is growing, with younger people struggling more with home ownership and stagnant wages. This inequality could reach record levels in the coming years.
ticker_line: Economic gap between generations set to widen
author: business Adelaide Miller
heading: Economy

title: Bendigo deal on union’s hit list
summary: Bendigo Bank plans to transfer hundreds of tech workers to Infosys, but unions warn the new contracts could strip away basic rights and worsen pay conditions. The Finance Sector Union is advising workers not to sign these agreements.
ticker_line: Bendigo Bank's tech workers face contract concerns
author: Rishab Jain
heading: Banking

title: Cancer serious but falls short of policy definition
summary: A man has lost his claim for trauma benefits from Zurich after the Australian Financial Complaints Authority ruled his cancer did not meet the policy's strict definition, despite being a serious condition. The policy specifically excluded his type of cancer, which was classified as non-invasive.
ticker_line: Man's cancer claim denied by Zurich insurer
heading: Life Insurance

title: Queensland ‘loses out’ under disaster funding shake-up
summary: Queensland may lose $500 million a year due to proposed federal changes to disaster funding, which will shift from a 75% federal contribution to a 50:50 split. This could lead to delays in repairs for local councils, especially in regional areas, as they struggle with high disaster costs.
ticker_line: Queensland faces $500 million loss in disaster funding
heading: General Insurance

title: Bigger buffer on household line shows ‘underlying uncertainty’
summary: Insurers are increasing their financial buffers for household insurance due to rising uncertainties like natural disasters and inflation. The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority's latest data shows risk margins for household insurance have grown since 2013, reflecting a more cautious approach to unexpected claims.
ticker_line: Insurers raise buffers amid rising uncertainties
heading: General Insurance

title: ICA levy call as NSW annual insurance haul tops $3b
summary: New South Wales will collect over $3 billion annually from insurance levies and duties, with emergency services levy expected to rise significantly. The Insurance Council of Australia urges for reform to reduce the financial burden on homeowners and businesses.
ticker_line: NSW insurance levies exceed $3 billion annually
heading: General Insurance

title: High-stakes code review still has some way to run
summary: The Insurance Council of Australia is updating its code of practice, which will now be part of customer contracts and needs approval from the Australian Securities and Investments Commission. Key changes include automatic acceptance of home and motor claims after 12 months and new definitions for vulnerability and urgent financial needs, with submissions on the draft due by July 21.
ticker_line: Insurance Council updates code for better consumer protection
heading: Regulation

title: ASIC slams super safety failures
summary: ASIC has found that superannuation trustees are failing to protect member savings, highlighting serious issues with monitoring fees and risky strategies. The regulator warns that immediate improvements are needed to avoid enforcement action.
ticker_line: ASIC warns super trustees on safety failures
author: JOSEPH CARBONE
heading: Superannuation

title: Private health group Ramsay given special access to public hospital emergency patients
summary: Ramsay Health Care has been allowed to transfer privately insured patients from a Queensland public hospital's emergency department to its private facilities, raising concerns about patient pressure and fairness in healthcare access. The trial, which has already moved over 2,000 patients, is set to expand nationally.
ticker_line: Ramsay gains access to public hospital emergency patients
author: business Alison Branley
heading: Health Insurance

title: Post-COVID debt growth challenges all but one state
summary: Most Australian states and territories face rising debt and interest costs, forcing them to consider cuts to services. Only Western Australia is not under similar pressure, while overall state debt is expected to reach nearly $1 trillion by 2030.
ticker_line: States struggle with soaring debt and interest costs
author: Shane Wright | Senior economics cor
heading: Economy

title: AI bonanza doesn’t add up for Qld
summary: Queensland is opposing the Albanese government's $150 billion data centre plan, raising concerns about costs and energy reliability. The state wants more details before agreeing to national energy proposals that could affect electricity prices for residents.
ticker_line: Queensland challenges federal data centre energy plan
author: PERRY WILLIAMS, CHIEF BU
heading: Energy

title: Inside the data governance crisis in the public service
summary: A recent study found that 67% of public service employees struggle to understand their organisations' data, highlighting serious gaps in data management and governance. Many agencies are failing to complete important metadata fields, risking the security and proper use of sensitive information.
ticker_line: Public service data governance crisis revealed
author: Ray Athwal
heading: Regulation

title: DATA CRISIS EXPOSED
summary: A survey reveals that one in three public-sector data professionals distrust their own data, with many lacking tools to manage it properly. This comes amid serious data management issues, highlighting gaps in data governance and the need for better documentation and oversight.
ticker_line: Public sector data trust issues revealed in survey
author: Ray Athwal
heading: Regulation

title: Investment bankers jump ship as data centre talent war heats up
summary: Investment banks are losing talent to data centre companies like Iren, which are offering high salaries and shares to attract skilled workers. Notable hires include JPMorgan's Bob Chen, who will focus on investor relations at Iren, as the demand for AI infrastructure grows.
ticker_line: Data centre firms lure top talent from banks
author: Joanne Tran and Jenny Wiggins
heading: Investments

title: Monash Uni to offer AI cybersecurity degree
summary: Monash University is launching a new Bachelor of CyberAI degree in partnership with CyberCX to address the shortage of cybersecurity experts in Australia. The program, starting next year, will focus on the intersection of artificial intelligence and cybersecurity to better prepare students for the workforce.
ticker_line: Monash Uni introduces CyberAI degree to tackle skills gap
author: Maani Truu | Education corresponden
heading: AI

title: Headline inflation softer than expected in June, but rate hikes not off the table
summary: Headline inflation in Australia fell to 3.8% in June, down from 4% in May, mainly due to lower fuel prices. Economists believe the Reserve Bank may not raise interest rates next month, but underlying inflation remains a concern.
ticker_line: Inflation drops, interest rate hike uncertain
author: business Gareth Hutchens
heading: Economy

title: Exclusive: AI job losses poised to upend Labor's electoral heartland
summary: A new report warns that AI could lead to job losses in white-collar sectors, affecting Labor's stronghold areas and creating political instability similar to past economic shifts. The Albanese government is facing pressure to balance job protection with the need for investment in AI technology.
ticker_line: AI job losses threaten Labor's electoral base
author: Paul Sakkal | Chief political corre
heading: Economy

title: Origin hack hits 900,000 customers
summary: Origin Energy has confirmed a major data breach affecting about 900,000 current and former customers, with personal information accessed. The company is offering identity protection and has warned customers to be cautious of suspicious communications.
ticker_line: Origin Energy data breach affects 900,000 customers
author: Nick Toscano and David Swan
heading: General Insurance

title: Superannuation: APRA test trips $7.5b construction fund
summary: BUSSQ, a Queensland superannuation fund with nearly $7.5 billion, has failed the APRA performance test for the first time since 2023, requiring it to inform over 59,000 members of its poor investment returns. If it fails again next year, it risks being banned from accepting new members into its main product, potentially leading to a merger.
ticker_line: BUSSQ fails APRA test, risks member ban
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Superannuation

title: Older Australians consider dropping private health insurance over proposed rebate changes
summary: Older Australians are considering dropping private health insurance due to proposed government changes that would reduce rebates based on income rather than age, potentially increasing costs by 4 to 12 percent. This could lead to a significant number of seniors leaving private cover, putting more pressure on the public health system.
ticker_line: Older Australians rethink private health insurance plans
author: Sarah Buchecker and Grace Marshall
heading: Health Insurance

title: Warning on scams, market’s dark threat
summary: A recent investigation by AUSTRAC revealed that mortgage fraud is rising due to scams using AI, with banks uncovering hundreds of millions in suspected fraudulent loans linked to Sydney. The report highlights the need for better protection against these modern financial crimes, which are becoming more sophisticated and widespread.
ticker_line: Mortgage fraud rises as AI scams increase
author: JONATHAN CHANCELLOR
heading: Regulation

title: Card surcharge ban signals cash is back
summary: The Reserve Bank's ban on card surcharges starting October 1 is expected to lead to a rise in cash usage, with businesses likely to offer cash discounts or go cash-only. This shift may encourage younger consumers, who are used to digital payments, to start carrying cash more often.
ticker_line: Cash usage expected to rise after surcharge ban
author: Anthony Keane
heading: Economy

title: OpenAI Medicare breach fuels push for tougher rules on rogue AI incidents
summary: The Australian government plans to require tech companies to quickly report AI-related breaches to both affected organisations and cyber authorities after OpenAI's delay in notifying about a Medicare data breach. This incident has prompted calls for stronger cybersecurity measures and new legislation aimed at improving national AI standards.
ticker_line: New rules for reporting AI breaches proposed
author: chief digital political corresponde
heading: Regulation

title: Controversial Sydney data centre project pulled amid community anger
summary: Goodman Group has cancelled its $1.2 billion Project Mars data centre in Sydney's north shore due to community opposition and changes in regulations. The decision follows local concerns about environmental impacts and comes amid a broader debate on data centre developments in Australia.
ticker_line: Goodman Group pulls Sydney data centre project
author: National AI Cam Wilson and
heading: Regulation

title: Currencies: Short bets on Aussie dollar surge to record
summary: Institutional fund managers have built a record $12.9 billion bet on the Australian dollar falling, partly to protect against a possible global tech and sharemarket slump, while hedge funds are betting it will rise. The Aussie was trading at US70.20¢, supported by expectations the RBA may raise rates; hotter-than-expected inflation data could trigger a sharp rise as investors unwind their bets against the currency.
ticker_line: Record bets against Aussie dollar clash with hedge fund optimism
author: Cecile Lefort
heading: Investments

title: CBA faces $3b pre-listing dilemma
summary: Commonwealth Bank is unlikely to sell its nearly $3 billion stake in AI company Anthropic when it lists, analysts say, though it may be able to sell a small portion. The stake was valued at more than $1.5 billion at June 30, and could deliver an estimated $2.8 billion paper gain if Anthropic reaches a valuation of up to $US2 trillion; CBA has not commented on its plans.
ticker_line: CBA may hold its Anthropic stake through IPO
author: Joyce Moullakis
heading: Banking

title: ‘Economic sadism’ if RBA hikes: union boss
summary: Union leader Dustin Halse urged the Reserve Bank not to raise interest rates again, saying higher rates punish people facing rising prices rather than those driving inflation. Economists say strong government spending is adding to demand and inflation, while forecasts point to inflation remaining above the RBA’s 2–3 per cent target and a possible fifth rate rise this year; the Greens’ David Shoebridge is also proposing $22 billion in tax cuts and higher support payments.
ticker_line: Union warns against rate rise as inflation stays high
author: GREG BROWN, MATTHEW CRANSTON, EXCLU
heading: Economy

title: Rate hold expectations on slowdown
summary: Inflation in Australia slowed to 4.2% in April, partly due to the government's fuel excise cut, leading economists to expect the Reserve Bank to keep interest rates steady in June. However, rising costs in housing and transport, along with ongoing global issues, may continue to challenge inflation.
ticker_line: Inflation slows, interest rates likely to hold
author: Lea Jurkovic | Economics correspond
heading: Economy

title: Big fine for big four bank
summary: Westpac has been fined $26 million by the Federal Court for not properly handling over 200 customer requests for financial help between 2017 and 2023. The court found the bank was grossly negligent in its response to customers facing hardships like job loss and illness.
ticker_line: Westpac fined $26 million for customer neglect
author: David Hannant
heading: Banking

title: RBA’s dilemma: Fight inflation or save growth?
summary: Australia's economy is slowing down while inflation stays high, creating a tough situation for the Reserve Bank. With rising unemployment and concerns over new tax changes, the bank may need to decide soon whether to raise interest rates or keep them steady.
ticker_line: RBA faces tough choices amid slowing economy
author: David Rogers, markets
heading: Economy

title: Inflation dip may hold off rate rise
summary: Inflation in Australia has dropped to 4.2% in April, down from 4.6% in March, which may lead the Reserve Bank to pause interest rate hikes next month. However, ongoing global conflicts could still impact future inflation and rate decisions.
ticker_line: Inflation drop may pause interest rate hikes
author: Duncan Evans
heading: Economy

title: Audit reveals cyberattack fears over this year's census
summary: An audit has revealed that the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) needs to fix important cybersecurity issues before the upcoming census on August 11, 2026. The report highlights that while some improvements have been made, there are still critical gaps that could leave the system vulnerable to cyberattacks.
ticker_line: Census cybersecurity concerns raised ahead of August survey
author: Rob Harris | National correspondent
heading: AI

title: NSW teens’ tech literacy falling sharply
summary: IT literacy among 15 to 16-year-olds in NSW has dropped to record lows, with only 37% achieving a proficient standard in 2025, down from 44% in 2022. This decline reflects a national trend, despite many students reporting regular use of technology and AI.
ticker_line: NSW teens' IT skills hit record low
author: Will Paige and Mary Papadakis
heading: AI

title: 36yo left shocked at peak tax age realisation
summary: A new report shows that Australians aged 30 pay significantly more tax than those aged 70, despite earning the same income, highlighting a major wealth gap in the tax system. The findings reveal that middle-aged workers are the biggest taxpayers, while retirees benefit from government support.
ticker_line: Tax burden shifts from young to old Australians
author: Ben Graham
heading: Economy

title: ‘Deeply concerning’: ASIC warns on gaps in oversight of $300b in super
summary: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) has raised concerns about the lack of oversight in the superannuation sector, specifically regarding excessive fees charged by financial advisers on platforms managing $300 billion in member funds. ASIC's review found that trustees are not adequately protecting members' retirement savings, especially those with low balances, and highlighted the need for better monitoring of fees and adviser practices.
ticker_line: ASIC warns on superannuation fee oversight gaps
author: Clancy Yeates
heading: Superannuation

title: ASIC says too many Australians' retirement savings being wiped out
summary: ASIC warns that many Australians' retirement savings are at risk due to poor oversight by superannuation trustees, following the loss of $1 billion from the collapse of Shield and First Guardian. The watchdog urges trustees to improve safeguards and for Australians to engage more with their superannuation.
ticker_line: ASIC raises alarm over retirement savings safety
author: business correspondent David Taylor
heading: Superannuation

title: Insurance gap leaves home builders ruined
summary: Michael Nelson faces a $300,000 loss after his builder went bankrupt, leaving his home renovation unfinished. He is unable to access the increased insurance coverage due to starting his project before the new rules took effect.
ticker_line: Builder insolvency leaves homeowners in crisis
author: Georgina Sebar
heading: General Insurance

title: Reserve Bank governor warns world facing increased supply shocks
summary: Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock warns that Australia faces challenges from rising oil prices and slow productivity growth, which could lead to higher inflation and limit economic growth. She highlights the need for careful monetary policy to manage these issues while noting that the economy is more resilient than in the past.
ticker_line: RBA warns of rising inflation risks ahead
author: business Gareth Hutchens
heading: Economy

title: Price of oil could derail economy, says Treasury
summary: Treasury warns that rising oil prices due to global conflicts could lead to higher inflation and slower economic growth in Australia. Prime Minister Albanese is announcing funding for a new oil refinery to help mitigate these effects.
ticker_line: Rising oil prices threaten Australian economy
author: Shane Wright and Mike Foley
heading: Economy

title: For the young, super won’t be a golden ticket
summary: A new study shows younger generations in Australia are likely to earn lower returns on their superannuation investments compared to Baby Boomers, making it harder for them to save for retirement while also facing high housing costs.
ticker_line: Younger Australians face lower super returns
author: Adam Creighton
heading: Superannuation

title: IAG, Suncorp in frame for $20bn Tokio Marine play
summary: Japanese insurer Tokio Marine is considering a buyout of either Insurance Australia Group (IAG) or Suncorp, with the deal potentially exceeding $20 billion. Both companies have strong market values and have recently faced challenges, but are seen as attractive targets for Tokio Marine's expansion into Australia.
ticker_line: Tokio Marine eyes $20bn buyout of insurers
author: DATA ROOM with BRIDGET CARTER
heading: General Insurance

title: We pay our way already: Data centres reject new tax
summary: Australia's data centre industry opposes new taxes, claiming it already contributes adequately to the economy. The sector is experiencing a surge in electricity demand due to the rise of artificial intelligence, prompting discussions on how to fund the necessary infrastructure without burdening households.
ticker_line: Data centres reject new tax amid AI boom
author: Colin Packham
heading: Economy

title: Govern AI before it governs you
summary: As AI technology grows in businesses, boards must improve their understanding of AI governance to manage risks and ensure accountability. A recent Deloitte survey shows that effective communication and strategic planning are key to enhancing organisational resilience in the face of AI integration.
ticker_line: Boards urged to enhance AI governance practices
author: John Marcante
heading: AI

title: Bleak outlook for shares as RBA ponders move
summary: The outlook for Australian shares is grim as the Reserve Bank considers raising interest rates again due to rising inflation. This could further impact the S&P/ASX 200, which has already lagged behind the US market's performance.
ticker_line: RBA may raise rates, hurting ASX shares
author: David Rogers, Markets
heading: Economy

title: Wesfarmers recruits bot for productivity mission
summary: Wesfarmers is using artificial intelligence in its stores to improve productivity and sales, with Bunnings' chatbot answering over 350,000 questions. The company reported a slight increase in annual sales but a dip in net profit, while also addressing challenges in the housing market and consumer spending.
ticker_line: Wesfarmers boosts productivity with AI tools
author: Eli Greenblat
heading: AI

title: Bank chief risk officers are losing sleep over rogue AI agent threats
summary: Banks are increasingly worried about the risks posed by rogue AI agents that could disrupt their systems or cause financial chaos. While they are taking steps to improve cybersecurity, the potential for cyber incidents remains high, prompting calls for better governance and oversight of AI technologies.
ticker_line: Banks on high alert over rogue AI threats
author: Joyce Moullakis
heading: Banking

title: NAB hiring in Asia, cutting in Australia
summary: NAB has 172 vacancies across India, Vietnam and Singapore, including roles in lending and wealth, while it plans to cut 2500 jobs, mostly in Australia. The hiring has raised concerns that the bank is shifting work offshore to reduce costs and could weaken skills development in Australia; NAB chief executive Andrew Irvine is due to face questions at a parliamentary hearing on November 13.
ticker_line: NAB hires across Asia as Australian job cuts loom
author: James Eyers and Jack Derwin
heading: Banking

title: Retirement income: AMP backs contested pension boost offering
summary: AMP has defended its Lifetime Boost retirement product, which can increase retirees’ income and help them qualify for more age pension by reducing the super balance counted under pension rules. The defence comes as Treasury prepares to consult on the products, which critics say can cost taxpayers and discourage customers from switching super funds; AMP says about 60 per cent of its customers have less than $500,000 in super.
ticker_line: AMP defends retirement products ahead of Treasury review
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Superannuation

title: Extension for workers' comp review
summary: The Minns government has extended its review of NSW’s workers compensation scheme to November 8 after receiving nearly 550 submissions, many from employers seeking more predictable premiums and rewards for good safety records. Construction groups say high industry-wide premiums hurt small builders and hiring, as the sector recorded nearly 900 insolvencies in NSW in the September quarter, a record high.
ticker_line: NSW extends workers’ compensation review after employer submissions
author: Madeleine Bower
heading: General Insurance

title: Super savings in AI criminals' sights
summary: Australia’s cyber agency says reports of potentially malicious activity rose 80 per cent in 2025-26, as advanced AI helps attackers find weaknesses and launch attacks faster. APRA deputy chairman David Bradbury warned an AI-assisted attack could drain super accounts, which hold more than $4.5 trillion, while the agency urged organisations to update old systems and strengthen basic protections.
ticker_line: AI-driven cyberattacks put super savings at risk
author: Shane Wright
heading: Superannuation

title: Bosses failing to offer AI training for workers
summary: A survey shows that nearly 80% of workers using AI have not received any formal training from their employers, raising concerns about companies' readiness to adapt to new technologies. While many employees recognise the need for AI skills, employers are struggling to provide the necessary training and support.
ticker_line: Workers lack AI training as companies lag behind
author: EWIN HANNAN
heading: AI

title: House prices on road to nowhere, or ‘modest’ squeeze
summary: Macquarie analysts predict a possible decline in Australian house prices by 5% due to recent tax changes by the Albanese government, which may lead to a long period of stagnant prices. They warn that investor activity in the housing market could drop significantly, affecting new home lending and overall market turnover.
ticker_line: House prices face potential 5% decline
author: David Ross
heading: Economy

title: Australia:A sustainable CSLR needs structural reform, says Insurance Council
summary: The Insurance Council of Australia is urging for major changes to the Compensation Scheme of Last Resort (CSLR) to ensure its long-term sustainability, rather than just finding new funding methods. They believe reforms should focus on the root causes of costs and ensure that only those responsible for misconduct fund the compensation.
ticker_line: Insurance Council pushes for CSLR reform
author: Jimmy John
heading: General Insurance

title: Return to rural banking is a growth story for Westpac
summary: Westpac is reopening branches in rural Australia, including Moree, to better serve local communities and farmers. This move comes after years of branch closures, highlighting the importance of personal banking relationships in agriculture.
ticker_line: Westpac expands rural banking network for growth
author: Tim Johnston
heading: Banking

title: ASX hits the skids as costs up 21pc
summary: ASX shares fell 13% after the company announced a cost increase of up to 21% next year due to higher technology expenses and regulatory issues. This follows criticism from the Australian Securities and Investments Commission for prioritising profits over market stability.
ticker_line: ASX shares plunge as costs soar 21%
author: Cliona O’Dowd
heading: Banking

title: ‘No guarantees’ on Labor’s NDIS bill
summary: Opposition NDIS spokeswoman Melissa McIntosh warns there are 'no guarantees' the Coalition will support Labor's plan to cut $185 billion from the NDIS over the next decade, raising concerns about potential unfair cuts to participants. Any delays in passing the legislation could jeopardise the government's budget goals.
ticker_line: Coalition's support for NDIS cuts uncertain
author: Sarah Ison, Senior political report
heading: General Insurance

title: Data centres can wind up energy
summary: Energy Minister Chris Bowen believes Australia's data centre industry can help boost renewable energy projects, especially wind farms, as the country struggles to meet its 2030 renewable energy targets. With data centres expected to double their energy needs by 2030, new rules may be needed to ensure they contribute positively to the energy grid.
ticker_line: Data centres to aid Australia's renewable energy goals
author: Perry Williams, Elizabeth Pike
heading: AI

title: Tailored training and a trade focus means no one need be left behind
summary: AI has the potential to improve productivity for Australia's skilled tradespeople by reducing administrative tasks and enhancing safety, but it requires proper training and worker involvement for successful adoption.
ticker_line: AI could boost productivity for tradespeople
author: Steven Miller
heading: AI

title: AI’s economic gains proving elusive: Altman
summary: OpenAI's CEO Sam Altman says the expected economic benefits of artificial intelligence are harder to achieve than anticipated, impacting jobs in unexpected ways. He highlighted recent job cuts at companies like CBA and Block due to AI, while also noting Australia's potential as a global data centre hub.
ticker_line: AI's economic impact harder to achieve, says Altman
author: David Ross
heading: AI

title: Goodman upbeat on race for AI riches
summary: Billionaire Greg Goodman believes Australia can benefit from the global AI investment boom, which could be worth up to $1.4 trillion. He highlights the need for better infrastructure and affordable power to attract AI companies and meet growing demand for data centres.
ticker_line: Goodman optimistic about Australia's AI future
author: Ben Wilmot
heading: AI

title: Business council out of step with youth on AI
summary: Australia's business leaders warn that failing to prioritise AI and data centres could cost the economy $1.4 trillion, but many young people want more regulation due to job fears. The debate intensifies as major tech companies announce job cuts while investing heavily in AI infrastructure.
ticker_line: AI investment debate divides business and youth
author: Tansy Harcourt
heading: AI

title: Why big super is investing your money in AI despite ‘biggest risk’
summary: Aware Super, a large Australian superannuation fund, is investing in AI despite concerns about high valuations and market risks. The fund recently participated in SpaceX's IPO but is cautious about future investments in other AI companies like Anthropic and OpenAI due to potential market volatility.
ticker_line: Aware Super invests in AI amid market risks
author: Cliona O’Dowd
heading: Superannuation

title: Super funds freeze dead partners’ cash
summary: Grieving families face long delays of over six months to access death benefit payouts from superannuation funds, causing financial stress. A review by ASIC reveals slow progress in improving these processes, with calls for better communication and mandatory service standards.
ticker_line: Super funds delay death benefit payouts for families
author: David Bonaddio
heading: Superannuation

title: Home truths for SMSF property investors in race to beat the ban
summary: New laws will ban self-managed super funds from borrowing to buy residential properties, effective mid-August 2026. Investors must act quickly to secure properties before the deadline, while commercial property purchases remain unaffected.
ticker_line: SMSF property investment ban set for August
author: JAMES GERRARD, ANALYSIS
heading: Superannuation

title: ANZ wants to change the way companies shift money overseas
summary: ANZ plans to launch a new type of deposit later this year that will allow large companies to transfer money across borders instantly, using blockchain technology. This move aims to improve the speed of cross-border payments and keep funds within the banking system, addressing common issues faced by corporate treasurers.
ticker_line: ANZ to launch instant cross-border deposit system
author: James Eyers
heading: Banking

title: Canberra consults over add-on cover rule exemptions
summary: The Federal Treasury is asking for feedback on draft rules to exempt certain valuable add-on insurance products from a four-day pause rule, which is set to expire on October 5. Financial Services Minister Daniel Mulino supports these exemptions, stating they are important for consumers and will continue until 2031.
ticker_line: Treasury seeks feedback on insurance rule exemptions
heading: Regulation

title: Repairers’ group slams IAG ‘fig leaf’ on RAC Insurance buyout
summary: The Motor Trades Association of Australia criticises IAG's proposed remedies for its buyout of RAC Insurance, claiming they do not address competition concerns and could harm small repair businesses in WA. They urge regulators to reject the acquisition or impose stricter oversight.
ticker_line: Repairers group opposes IAG's RAC Insurance buyout
heading: General Insurance

title: ‘We need to be honest about affordability challenge’
summary: Richard Feledy from the Insurance Council of Australia highlighted the growing issue of insurance affordability in a speech, noting that rising costs and taxes, like the emergency services levy in NSW, are making it harder for Australians to afford insurance. He called for government and industry collaboration to address these challenges and improve community resilience.
ticker_line: Insurance Council calls for action on affordability
heading: General Insurance

title: New ACCC merger rules unfairly cover family businesses, car dealers say
summary: Car dealers are concerned that new merger rules unfairly affect small family-owned businesses, requiring them to notify the ACCC about acquisitions that meet certain financial thresholds. The Australian Automotive Dealers Association argues that these rules, aimed at larger companies, do not reflect the competitive nature of the car dealership market.
ticker_line: New merger rules hit family car dealers hard
author: Sam Irvine
heading: Regulation

title: Big super 'must unite' on cybersecurity
summary: The Albanese government is urging the superannuation industry to work together to improve cybersecurity after concerns about slow responses to threats. Assistant Treasurer Daniel Mulino has called for key lobby groups to unite to enhance the sector's cyber resilience.
ticker_line: Super funds urged to unite on cybersecurity
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Superannuation

title: SMSF debt ban underestimated non-bank loans
summary: Non-bank lenders provided over 16,000 loans to self-managed super funds (SMSFs) last year, far more than the 4,000 cited by the government, raising concerns that a new ban on SMSF borrowing could severely impact housing supply and development projects in Australia.
ticker_line: SMSF loan ban could disrupt housing market
author: Michael Bleby | Deputy property edi
heading: Superannuation

title: Banks look to shore up AI defences
summary: Australian banks are prioritising cybersecurity as they face increased threats from AI-powered hackers. They are changing their response strategies to act faster against potential breaches, with new AI tools like Anthropic's Mythos highlighting vulnerabilities in their systems.
ticker_line: Banks ramp up AI cybersecurity measures
author: James Eyers
heading: Banking

title: SUPER SAFETY: SHARK ALARM
summary: The article warns Australians about the risks of switching to self-managed super funds (SMSFs), especially for those with low balances, as they may face higher costs and lower returns compared to regulated funds. It calls for stronger protections and limits on fees to prevent exploitation by unscrupulous advisers.
ticker_line: Risks of self-managed super funds highlighted
author: Kristian Fok
heading: Superannuation

title: Super giant Cbus calls for SMSF restrictions
summary: Cbus, a large super fund, is urging for new rules on self-managed super funds (SMSFs) to protect Australians from risks like losing their retirement savings. They suggest setting minimum balance requirements and limiting advice fees to prevent people with small super balances from being misled.
ticker_line: Cbus calls for SMSF restrictions to protect retirees
author: Cliona O’Dowd
heading: Superannuation

title: Private credit faces 'real test' as cracks show
summary: Australia's $200 billion private credit sector is facing stress as major firms limit withdrawals, following the collapse of property developer Bathla. The corporate regulator warns of significant issues in the industry, prompting calls for improved standards and oversight.
ticker_line: Private credit sector shows signs of distress
author: Jonathan Shapiro, James Eyers and J
heading: Investments

title: Investors pouring money into malls
summary: Investors are heavily investing in retail properties, with MA Financial and HMC Capital leading the way. Major deals include MA Financial's $120 million purchase of Taigum Square in Brisbane and Australian Retirement Trust's $882.5 million acquisition of a stake in Westfield Mount Gravatt.
ticker_line: Investors flock to retail property sector
author: Ben Wilmot
heading: Investments

title: ‘Agnostic’ mayor supports mixed energy supplies
summary: Western Downs Mayor Andrew Smith supports a mix of energy sources for a proposed data centre, highlighting the region's energy infrastructure. Meanwhile, Queensland Premier David Crisafulli opposes the federal government's push for data centres to use only renewable energy.
ticker_line: Mayor backs mixed energy for data centre growth
author: MARCUS DE BLONK SMITH, MACKENZIE SC
heading: Investments

title: WiseTech bets on AI, cuts 1700 jobs
summary: WiseTech has cut about 1,700 jobs as it shifts focus to artificial intelligence, despite reporting a record profit of $1.4 billion. The company's outlook has worried investors, leading to a drop in its stock price amid ongoing investigations by the ACCC and issues involving its founder.
ticker_line: WiseTech cuts jobs while boosting AI focus
author: Jared Lynch
heading: AI

title: 'Factories of the digital economy': ACT promises new data centre rules
summary: The ACT government plans new rules for data centres to ensure they protect residential areas and water while promoting economic growth and job creation. The framework will include clear guidelines for building locations, standards, and assessments, alongside a focus on renewable energy and artificial intelligence.
ticker_line: ACT introduces new rules for data centres
author: Jasper Lindell
heading: Economy

title: Commonwealth debt: Interest bill to eclipse Medicare spend by 2029
summary: By 2028-29, Australia's interest payments on government debt are expected to exceed spending on Medicare, as $165 billion in low-cost COVID-era debt is refinanced at much higher rates. This shift will increase annual interest costs to $41.9 billion, raising concerns about the long-term budget deficit.
ticker_line: Interest payments to surpass Medicare spending by 2029
author: Michael Read | Deputy economics edi
heading: Economy

title: Risk: CFS shuns Australian private credit market
summary: Colonial First State, a major superannuation fund, is avoiding Australian private credit investments due to high risks linked to property development, especially after the $3.4 billion collapse of Bathla. The fund's CIO, Jonathan Armitage, prefers overseas private credit managers who lend to more stable businesses.
ticker_line: CFS avoids risky Australian private credit market
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Superannuation

title: CLOSING BELL: Bathla hasn't scared ART off private credit
summary: Australian Retirement Trust chief investment officer Ian Patrick says the fund’s private credit investments remain in good shape despite rising defaults and the collapse of builder Bathla, where ART has $22 million invested through a PAG fund. ART is reviewing its holdings but is staying neutral on private credit: it will not cut its allocation, but is not planning to increase it.
ticker_line: ART holds steady on private credit after Bathla collapse
author: James Thomson
heading: Superannuation

title: Retirement scheme crackdown looms
summary: Treasury is considering a review of retirement products from major super funds such as AMP, MLC and Colonial First State that can increase members’ age pension entitlements by reducing the super counted under pension rules. The products manage more than $21.5 billion, but critics say they may cost taxpayers and lock members into a fund; the super industry says it has followed existing rules, while Treasury has yet to begin a promised wider consultation.
ticker_line: Treasury weighs crackdown on pension-boost super products
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Superannuation

title: Disruptions 'inevitable' as AI-powered cyber threats grow, Australian Signals Directorate says
summary: Australian Signals Directorate chief Abigail Bradshaw says AI-powered cyber attacks are likely to cause more disruption to websites, data and everyday services. The agency reported a 20 per cent rise in cyber incidents it handled last financial year, and says it has disrupted criminal operations that had access to 180,000 computers and destroyed millions of stolen files.
ticker_line: ASD warns AI cyber attacks will disrupt services
author: by political Tom
heading: AI

title: NAB cultivates cheap talent offshore as Australian jobs are axed
summary: NAB plans to add at least 180 jobs in India and Vietnam while cutting 2,500 roles, including 1,500 by mid-December, from its Australian workforce. More than a third of its Vietnamese staff are interns or recent graduates, and a junior software engineer there can cost about $20,000 a year compared with at least $80,000 in Australia; the Financial Sector Union has challenged the cuts.
ticker_line: NAB cuts Australian jobs while expanding offshore hiring
author: Cliona O’Dowd
heading: Banking

title: AMP eyes bank shake-up as takeover talk builds
summary: AMP is reportedly considering a funding model that would let a private equity firm fund its bank’s loans, freeing up capital and reducing AMP’s exposure to lending risks. The move could make AMP easier to buy or split up, with Insignia Financial mentioned as a possible buyer; AMP’s bank has $17.8bn in deposits and made $20m in profit in the six months to June, down 33.3 per cent.
ticker_line: AMP weighs bank funding shift as takeover talk grows
author: DATA ROOM with BRIDGET CARTER
heading: Banking

title: Taylor’s $31bn in budget savings
summary: Opposition Leader Angus Taylor says the Coalition has identified $31 billion in savings to fund its planned income tax cuts, leaving the budget $22 billion better off over four years from 2028. The savings include ending net-zero programs and housing measures, but the tax plan would cost more than $200 billion over a decade; Labor says the Coalition’s broader policies would increase deficits by nearly $140 billion over four years.
ticker_line: Taylor claims $31bn in savings will fund tax cuts
author: Greg Brown, Chief Political Corresp
heading: Economy

title: Regulation: Regulator to cease action against Super Retail board
summary: ASIC says it will take no further action against Super Retail Group or anyone else connected with the company, apart from former chief executive Anthony Heraghty. Heraghty faces court over allegations he failed to disclose and manage a conflict of interest; Super Retail must fund his legal defence for now, but may recover the costs if he is found not entitled to indemnity.
ticker_line: ASIC targets former Super Retail chief, not board
author: Colin Kruger
heading: Regulation

title: Tokio Marine cools on Suncorp
summary: Tokio Marine has reportedly put its interest in buying Suncorp on hold for now, as Suncorp’s rising share price makes a deal harder to afford. The Japanese insurer could move quickly if the price falls, while Suncorp says it has received no offer and is not in takeover discussions.
ticker_line: Tokio Marine cools on Suncorp as shares rise
author: DATA ROOM with BRIDGET CARTER
heading: General Insurance

title: REA confident in the power of AI for growth
summary: REA Group chief executive Cameron McIntyre says AI is becoming more useful for property searches, agents and mortgage brokers, and the company sees it as a way to improve products and grow. The property market remains challenging, with listings expected to fall by a low single-digit percentage this financial year, while REA expands overseas through stakes in Irish and Canadian businesses.
ticker_line: REA sees AI driving growth as property listings soften
author: Ben Wilmot
heading: AI

title: EXCLUSIVE: Voters want local AI laws as data centre concern rises
summary: A Resolve poll of 2,200 people found 81% support regulating AI, with more people favouring Australian laws than an international approach, as concern grows about AI’s risks. Australians were divided over new data centres, with many worried about their power and water use; modelling by the Smart Energy Council warns that meeting their demand without new clean energy could raise household and business power bills.
ticker_line: Voters favour local AI laws as data centre concerns rise
author: Shane Wright
heading: AI

title: Commonwealth Bank boss Matt Comyn says government should reconsider CGT on non-passive assets
summary: Commonwealth Bank CEO Matt Comyn has urged the government to limit capital gains tax changes to passive assets like housing, arguing that broader applications could discourage investment and innovation. He plans to discuss these concerns with Treasurer Jim Chalmers soon.
ticker_line: CBA CEO calls for targeted capital gains tax reform
heading: Banking

title: Investors on shaky ground as data points to a market slowdown
summary: Investors are facing challenges as new federal budget changes, including the removal of negative gearing for existing properties, are expected to reduce demand and lending in the housing market. Data shows a decline in housing loan commitments and a drop in consumer confidence, particularly among owner-occupiers.
ticker_line: Market slowdown as investor demand weakens
author: Nina Hendy
heading: Economy

title: Call to ban lead generators for super
summary: The Super Members Council is calling for a ban on lead generators in superannuation to protect Australians from fraud and unsafe financial practices. They urge the government to strengthen regulations and complete reforms to financial advice to ensure better safety for retirement savings.
ticker_line: Call to ban lead generators in superannuation
author: David Ross
heading: Superannuation

title: The AI experiment is over: Australian leaders now have to move
summary: Australian leaders must quickly decide which AI programs to scale up, as the trial phase is over and the country is lagging behind global trends in AI investment and adoption. Effective organisational change and clear standards are essential for successful AI integration.
ticker_line: Australian leaders urged to scale AI quickly
author: Bec McConnochie
heading: AI

title: Australia, UK tackle AI safety
summary: Australia and the UK have signed an agreement to share information on artificial intelligence risks, even before Australia establishes its own AI safety watchdog. This partnership aims to enhance research and responses to AI threats.
ticker_line: Australia and UK unite on AI safety measures
author: Jared Lynch
heading: AI

title: Insurance Council of Australia launches consultation on revised General Insurance Code
summary: The Insurance Council of Australia is seeking public feedback on a revised General Insurance Code aimed at improving consumer protections and customer service. Key changes include making the Code legally enforceable, automatic acceptance of certain claims after 12 months, and better support for vulnerable customers.
ticker_line: ICA seeks feedback on new insurance code
author: Jake Nathanoel Dellosa
heading: General Insurance

title: Jobs and spending data put rate rise back in play
summary: Australia's jobless rate fell to 4.4% and household spending rose 1.3% in May, suggesting the economy is still strong and may lead to more interest rate hikes by the Reserve Bank. The data shows resilience in spending despite concerns about inflation and cost-of-living challenges.
ticker_line: Strong jobs and spending data may prompt rate hikes
author: Luke Kinsella
heading: Economy

title: UniSuper, Hostplus lead super thrivers
summary: UniSuper and Hostplus are leading Australia's super funds with high-growth returns of 12.8% and 12.3% respectively, as the financial year ends. Other funds like AustralianSuper and HESTA also performed well, but some lagged behind with lower returns amid global market volatility.
ticker_line: UniSuper and Hostplus top super fund returns
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Superannuation

title: Unemployment drops but labour market cracks emerge
summary: Australia's unemployment rate fell to 4.4% with over 40,000 jobs added in May, but revisions show previous job losses and a drop in job vacancies indicate a weakening labour market. Economists expect the unemployment rate to rise to 5% by early 2027 due to slower hiring.
ticker_line: Unemployment drops but labour market shows cracks
author: Thomas Henry, Matthew Cranston
heading: Economy

title: Risky business: Life insurers aren’t just investors in private credit. They’re lenders, too
summary: A report shows that many life insurers are not only investing in private-credit funds but also lending money to them, increasing both potential returns and risks. This double exposure could lead to significant losses if loans default, raising concerns about the stability of the insurance sector.
ticker_line: Life insurers double down on risky private credit
author: MATT WIRZ, SHANE SHIFFLETT
heading: Life Insurance

title: NSW Coalition promises to protect jobs amid AI push
summary: The NSW Coalition promises to protect frontline public sector jobs from AI job losses while planning to increase AI use for efficiency in government. They will require agencies to find AI improvements and establish a fund for public-interest AI development if they win the next election.
ticker_line: NSW Coalition vows to protect jobs from AI
author: Lachlan Leeming
heading: AI

title: Surcharge ban could end popular free travel insurance perk
summary: A new ban on surcharges starting October 1 may limit the free travel insurance benefits offered by premium credit cards in Australia. Travel agents warn this could lead to fewer rewards and higher costs for customers, as they may have to pay by direct deposit instead of credit cards.
ticker_line: Surcharge ban threatens free travel insurance perks
author: Elias Visontay
heading: Regulation

title: Managers risk losing job to AI
summary: A study shows that nearly half of Australian middle managers are at risk of losing their jobs to AI, with one in five facing significant danger. Experts advise that managers need to adapt by learning AI skills and demonstrating their value in the workplace.
ticker_line: Many managers face job loss due to AI
author: Ruby Stewart
heading: AI

title: E-bike 'hoon boys' not saddled with insurance
summary: The NSW government will not require e-bike riders to have insurance, despite a rise in cycling accidents linked to e-bikes. A report found that enforcing insurance would be costly and ineffective, recommending better law enforcement instead.
ticker_line: NSW rejects e-bike insurance despite rising crashes
author: Paul Karp
heading: Regulation

title: Inflation slows again in July but heightens risk of interest rate hike by RBA
summary: Inflation in Australia slowed to 3.5% in July, down from 3.8% in June, but rising costs in housing and fuel raise concerns about a possible interest rate hike by the Reserve Bank of Australia. Economists are divided on whether the RBA will increase rates at its next meeting on September 29.
ticker_line: Inflation slows but rate hike risk rises
author: business Kate Ainsworth
heading: Economy

title: Macquarie Group dumps KPMG from audit contract
summary: Macquarie Group has decided to end its audit contract with KPMG due to concerns over the firm's handling of confidential information and ongoing scandals. The company will recommend PwC as its new auditor at the upcoming annual general meeting.
ticker_line: Macquarie Group drops KPMG as auditor
heading: Regulation

title: Flyers ‘should do sums’ on double points plan
summary: Qantas is offering double status credits or points for flights booked from now until September 2 to encourage bookings, while ANZ and Commonwealth Bank are cutting benefits on points-linked credit cards. Frequent flyers should compare prices carefully before booking to maximise their benefits.
ticker_line: Qantas launches double points promotion for flyers
author: Robyn Ironside
heading: General Insurance

title: Private credit defined at last
summary: Australia's Financial Services Council has proposed a formal definition for private credit, aiming to improve transparency and standards in the sector. This move comes as the corporate regulator, ASIC, increases its focus on private credit practices and potential conflicts of interest among lenders.
ticker_line: New rules proposed for private credit sector
author: David Ross
heading: Regulation

title: ‘Super tax’ puts SMSFs on red alert
summary: The self-managed super fund industry warns that new tax rules could raise effective tax rates for many retirees, especially those using managed investment trusts.
