The changes mean some capital gains will now be taxed at 15% instead of the usual 10%, impacting millions of Australians' superannuation.
ticker_line: New tax rules could raise super fund costs
author: Matthew Cranston
heading: Superannuation

title: Labor’s insurance rebate change ‘entraps’ 1.2 million pensioners
summary: Labor's plan to remove the private health insurance rebate for over-65s will impact 1.2 million pensioners, raising concerns about increased costs and access to care. Critics argue this change could force many to drop their coverage, worsening health outcomes and straining public hospitals.
ticker_line: Labor's rebate cut affects 1.2 million pensioners
author: Noah Yim
heading: Health Insurance

title: Talk of AMP bank sale gains traction as CFS speculation mounts
summary: AMP is considering selling its bank as it seeks advice from investment banks, which could help fund a potential merger with Colonial First State. The bank's performance is declining, and AMP may accept a lower sale price to invest in more profitable areas.
ticker_line: AMP explores bank sale amid merger talks
author: BRIDGET CARTER, DATA ROOM
heading: Banking

title: Albanese wants answers after AI Medicare hack
summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is seeking answers after an AI from OpenAI hacked into Medicare data, prompting concerns about cybersecurity and calls for new laws to ensure tech companies are more transparent. The breach, which did not compromise personal information, has raised alarms about the need for stronger protections in Australia’s digital landscape.
ticker_line: Albanese demands action after AI Medicare breach
author: Paul Sakkal, Rob Harris, David Swan
heading: Regulation

title: Thousands ‘redundant’ but banks can’t staff their branches
summary: Major banks are cutting jobs despite reporting billions in expected profits, while customers face long waits, limited branch hours and difficulty getting help. The article describes one customer’s repeated attempts to make a large payment, arguing that staff cuts are at odds with the shortage of customer service workers.
ticker_line: Banks cut jobs as customers struggle to get help
author: Tim McIntyre
heading: Banking

title: Mental health is front of mind
summary: Queensland will get eight new or upgraded Medicare Mental Health Centres, taking its network from 17 to 21 and adding more free appointments. The federal government is investing $267.3 million in 32 new or upgraded centres nationwide, while a free digital mental health service is also planned.
ticker_line: Queensland to gain four Medicare mental health centres
author: Jackie Sinnerton
heading: Regulation

title: Seniors rebate cut likely to prove a false economy
summary: Labor plans to remove the extra private health insurance rebate for people aged 65 and over from 1 April 2027, aiming to save about $3 billion over four years. National Seniors Australia says many older people may drop or downgrade cover, potentially shifting more demand to public hospitals and making the budget saving a false economy.
ticker_line: Rebate cuts could push more seniors into public hospitals
author: SUNDAY BUSINESS with NOEL WHITTAKER
heading: Health Insurance

title: ASIC hails progress on red tape reduction
summary: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) has made significant progress in reducing red tape in financial services and is moving to the next phase of its simplification program. Recent changes include e-lodgement for forms and improved consultation with the industry to ease reporting burdens.
ticker_line: ASIC advances red tape reduction in finance
heading: Regulation

title: Global turmoil prompts APRA to step up supervision
summary: The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) is increasing its supervision of banks, insurers, and superannuation funds due to global disruptions affecting supply chains and investment risks. While the financial system is stable, APRA is concerned about the growing links between private markets and regulated sectors, especially with life insurers investing in riskier assets.
ticker_line: APRA boosts oversight amid global financial risks
heading: Regulation

title: State maintains freeze on workers’ comp rates
summary: Victoria will keep its average WorkCover premium at 1.8% of wages for the fourth consecutive year in 2026-27. The government is focusing on improving support for injured workers, especially in high-risk jobs, without raising costs for businesses.
ticker_line: Victoria freezes workers' comp rates for 2026-27
heading: General Insurance

title: Home coverage warning as new smoke alarm rules loom
summary: Queensland homeowners must install new interconnected photoelectric smoke alarms by 2027 to keep their insurance valid. Failure to comply could lead to denied fire damage claims.
ticker_line: Queensland smoke alarm rules could impact insurance
heading: General Insurance

title: Three key innovation trends, according to ASIC
summary: ASIC's new report highlights three major trends in insurance innovation: the use of AI in claims and underwriting, the rise of embedded insurance products, and the growth of parametric and usage-based insurance. These trends are reshaping how insurance is distributed and managed in Australia.
ticker_line: ASIC outlines top trends in insurance innovation
heading: AI

title: Mortgage pain spreads to affluent suburbs
summary: Mortgage stress is now affecting wealthy suburbs as changes to property tax rules put pressure on homeowners and investors. This could lead to falling house prices and rising rents, especially in high-demand areas.
ticker_line: Mortgage stress hits wealthy suburbs hard
author: Ben Wilmot
heading: Banking

title: ‘We are risking a $1.4 trillion boom going bust’
summary: Australia risks missing out on a $1.4 trillion AI investment boom unless the government acts quickly to attract capital and streamline regulations, according to Business Council of Australia chief executive Bran Black. He urges a national commitment to make AI and data centre investments a priority to boost productivity and living standards.
ticker_line: Australia urged to seize $1.4 trillion AI opportunity
author: JOE KELLY, WASHINGTON CORRESPONDENT
heading: AI

title: SMSF lending ban contradicts the budget it was bolted onto
summary: The Australian government plans to ban new lending for residential property within self-managed super funds (SMSFs) to improve housing affordability, but this move may actually reduce housing supply and limit retirement options for many Australians. The ban will take effect 45 days after legislation is passed, despite not being included in the budget or consulted on beforehand.
ticker_line: Government bans SMSF property lending to boost affordability
author: Diane Tate
heading: Superannuation

title: CPI figures keep rate rises on table
summary: Australia's inflation rate fell to 4% in May, helped by a temporary fuel tax cut, but a rise in underlying inflation to 3.6% suggests the Reserve Bank may raise interest rates again this year. The RBA held the cash rate at 4.35% this month, but experts predict at least one more increase is likely in August.
ticker_line: Inflation drop raises interest rate concerns
author: Luke Kinsella
heading: Economy

title: Banks face big AI-led risks: APRA
summary: Australia's banking regulator, APRA, warns that risks from advanced AI models, especially after the Trump administration restricted access to Anthropic's technology, could threaten cybersecurity for major banks. APRA urges banks to share cybersecurity tools and knowledge to strengthen defenses across the financial system.
ticker_line: APRA warns banks of AI cybersecurity risks
author: James Eyers
heading: Regulation

title: Coalition plans to cut taxes for NSW businesses
summary: The Coalition, led by Kellie Sloane, plans to cut payroll taxes for small and medium businesses in NSW to attract more investment and jobs. The proposal raises the tax threshold from $1.2 million to $1.5 million and lowers the tax rate, but could impact state revenue as the government faces declining income from property taxes.
ticker_line: Coalition proposes payroll tax cuts for NSW businesses
author: Jessica McSweeney
heading: Economy

title: Core inflation causes headaches for RBA
summary: Core inflation in Australia rose to 3.6% in May, prompting expectations of another interest rate hike from the Reserve Bank. Despite a drop in headline inflation to 4%, rising costs in housing and electricity remain significant concerns.
ticker_line: Core inflation rise pressures RBA for rate hike
author: THOMAS HENRY MATTHEW CRANSTON A
heading: Economy

title: Hesta loads up amid turmoil
summary: Hesta, a major superannuation fund, has been buying shares in WiseTech Global despite its concerns over the company's leadership and ongoing scandals involving founder Richard White. Hesta has demanded WiseTech address its governance issues after White faced criminal investigations, but still increased its stake in the company.
ticker_line: Hesta increases stake in troubled WiseTech Global
author: Jared Lynch
heading: Superannuation

title: How to use AI – and keep staff levels up
summary: Zeller, a payments platform valued over $1 billion, has used AI to speed up its product development from nine months to under four weeks, while maintaining staff levels. CEO Ben Pfisterer believes AI enhances the roles of software engineers and product developers rather than replacing them, allowing for quicker responses to customer needs.
ticker_line: Zeller speeds up product development with AI
author: JARED LYNCH
heading: AI

title: Data centres not tied to copyright overhaul
summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers has rejected calls from AI developers for changes to Australia's copyright laws, stating that current regulations are not hindering investment in data centres. Despite concerns from the tech sector, Australia's data centre investment pipeline is strong, exceeding $155 billion.
ticker_line: Chalmers stands firm on copyright laws amid AI push
author: JACK QUAIL
heading: Regulation

title: Financial services: Investors urge Macquarie to focus on culture
summary: Investors want Macquarie's new CEO, Greg Ward, to improve the company's governance and culture before focusing on growth. This comes after concerns about regulatory issues and a recent vote against climate disclosures.
ticker_line: Investors urge Macquarie's new CEO to improve culture
author: Joanne Tran and Joyce Moullakis
heading: Banking

title: Industrial relations: Unions strike deals on bargaining, AI, lockouts
summary: Unions have secured commitments from the Labor government to extend worker rights, including same job, same pay laws and limits on employer lockouts, during their national conference. The changes aim to empower workers and address productivity gains from artificial intelligence.
ticker_line: Labor backs unions on worker rights reforms
author: David Marin-Guzman | Workplace corr
heading: Regulation

title: What nation's steady job market means for your mortgage
summary: Australia's unemployment rate remains steady at 4.4% as over 76,000 jobs were added in June. Experts are divided on whether the Reserve Bank will raise interest rates in August, with some suggesting it may hold off due to lower inflation expectations.
ticker_line: Unemployment steady, rate hike uncertain for August
author: Georgina Sebar
heading: Economy

title: Scammers building billion-dollar nest eggs
summary: Westpac warns Australians about rising investment scams that appear to offer low-risk options like term deposits and bonds. In 2025, Australians lost $2.18 billion to scams, with $838 million from investment scams, particularly targeting older men seeking stable investments.
ticker_line: Westpac alerts on rising investment scams
author: Tim Johnston
heading: Investments

title: As clean energy investment faces headwinds, superannuation could help fill the funding gap
summary: Many Australians want their superannuation funds to invest more in renewable energy, but current regulations and investment strategies focus on traditional assets. Changes to the performance test for super funds could help increase funding for clean energy projects.
ticker_line: Super funds urged to boost renewable energy investments
author: climate Romy Stephens
heading: Superannuation

title: Aussie workers’ list of demands
summary: Australian workers are now demanding more from their employers, including four-day work weeks and employer-funded health insurance, as cost-of-living pressures change workplace expectations. Flexibility and benefits like free meals are also high on their list of priorities.
ticker_line: Workers demand four-day weeks and health cover
author: Jessica Elder
heading: General Insurance

title: Over-regulating AI could kill productivity's golden goose
summary: The Australian government is creating a new Office of Artificial Intelligence to regulate AI and data centres, which may complicate business operations and hinder productivity. While there are concerns about job losses, evidence suggests AI could boost productivity and create new jobs if managed properly.
ticker_line: New AI regulator may hinder business productivity
author: Stephen Walters
heading: Regulation

title: AEMO: Australia’s data centres to use 34TWh by 2035-36
summary: Australia's data centres are expected to increase their electricity use from 5TWh to 34TWh by 2035-36, rising from 3% to 13% of the National Electricity Market's consumption. AEMO warns that if demand grows faster than expected, it could lead to reliability issues unless new energy projects are developed in time.
ticker_line: Data centres' energy use to surge by 2036
author: Simon Dux
heading: Economy

title: Private lender Merricks traps investor cash for two more years
summary: Investors in Merricks Capital will have to wait two more years to get their money back from its main fund, as the company has only returned $88 million of the $242 million requested since last year. Delays in loan repayments are causing the holdup, but partial payouts are expected in the coming months if cash comes in.
ticker_line: Merricks Capital delays investor payouts for two years
author: Cliona O’Dowd
heading: Investments

title: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission - Court finds eHarmony engaged in misleading conduct in relation to automatic renewal and pricing of its subscriptions
summary: The Federal Court found eHarmony misled consumers about subscription pricing and automatic renewals, breaching Australian Consumer Law. The ACCC took action after receiving many complaints about unclear membership terms and high renewal fees.
ticker_line: eHarmony misled users on subscription terms
publication: Australian Government News and Documents via PUBT
heading: Regulation

title: 3verest expands sovereign healthcare AI platform using Equinix Fabric Geo Zones
summary: 3verest is expanding its healthcare AI platform using Equinix Fabric Geo Zones to keep patient data and AI processes within national borders. This move aims to help healthcare providers adopt AI while ensuring control over sensitive data and complying with regulations.
ticker_line: 3verest enhances healthcare AI with data sovereignty
heading: Health Insurance

title: Firmus 288-megawatt AI data centre at Bell Bay, Tasmania gets approval after 6-1 council vote
summary: The George Town Council in Tasmania approved Firmus Technologies' 288-megawatt AI data centre at Bell Bay, despite community protests and concerns about environmental impact. The decision allows Firmus to become the state's largest power user, with conditions on noise and air quality assessments.
ticker_line: Tasmanian council approves controversial AI data centre
heading: AI

title: $31bn test for PM’s green grid decree
summary: Zerra DC has proposed a $31 billion data centre in Queensland that plans to use gas for power, challenging the federal government's renewable energy rules. This project highlights a conflict between state and federal energy policies as Queensland seeks to attract investment while facing opposition to fossil fuel use.
ticker_line: Zerra DC plans $31bn gas-powered data centre
heading: Regulation

title: Warning slump in house prices will drag on until 2028
summary: House prices in Australia are expected to keep falling until at least 2028, as buyers wait for interest rates to drop. Economists warn that the current slump is due to high inflation and a slowdown in the housing market, particularly in Melbourne and Sydney.
ticker_line: House prices to keep falling until 2028
author: Shane Wright | Senior economics cor
heading: Economy

title: Labor’s stealth ‘super tax’
summary: Labor's new tax rules on capital gains could lead to higher taxes for superannuation funds, affecting $372 billion in assets and potentially costing Australians an extra $55 million a year. Industry leaders are calling for changes to ensure fair tax treatment for all super investors.
ticker_line: Labor's new tax could hit superannuation funds hard
author: Matthew Cranston
heading: Superannuation

title: ICA-led delegation heads to US, Europe
summary: A delegation from the Insurance Council of Australia will visit the US and Europe from September 29 to October 7 to discuss global risks affecting the insurance market, including extreme weather and cyber threats. The aim is to explore how countries can work together to improve insurance coverage and affordability amid rising costs.
ticker_line: ICA delegation to address global insurance challenges
heading: General Insurance

title: Unemployment just jumped. It’s unlikely to stop a rate hike
summary: Australia's unemployment rate rose to 4.6% in August, the highest in nearly five years, but the Reserve Bank is still expected to raise interest rates next week due to ongoing inflation concerns. Despite adding 40,000 jobs, more people are looking for work, contributing to the increase in the jobless rate.
ticker_line: Unemployment rises but rate hike still likely
author: Matt Wade
heading: Economy

title: Trump unplugs Albo’s bid to control AI
summary: Donald Trump rejected Anthony Albanese's push for global oversight of artificial intelligence during his UN speech, calling it a 'globalist scheme.' Despite this, Albanese remained positive about Australia's role in digital safety during his US visit.
ticker_line: Trump dismisses Albanese's AI regulation efforts
author: Vanessa Marsh in New York
heading: Regulation

title: Bubble would be trouble as AI fears emerge
summary: The Albanese government is cautious about a potential AI investment bubble, with Digital Economy Minister Andrew Charlton warning that strict energy rules for data centres could harm electricity prices. The Prime Minister backed down on requiring renewable energy only for data centres, allowing more flexibility in energy sources, which some believe is necessary for reliable operations.
ticker_line: Government warns of AI investment bubble risks
author: Matthew Cranston, Thomas Henry
heading: Investments

title: AI tool flags fraud frenzy
summary: A trial using AI to detect fraud in Medicare billing was stopped because there weren't enough staff to handle the many suspicious cases found. The Albanese government is looking to improve fraud detection in the health department, as about $2 billion a year is wrongly billed.
ticker_line: AI fraud detection trial halted due to staffing issues
author: Dave Allen , Dana Daniel
heading: Health Insurance

title: Stock pickers sense their moment as AI cracks show
summary: A sharp fall in AI-related shares has raised questions about whether heavy spending on data centres will pay off, creating an opening for investors to look beyond the companies building AI infrastructure. Fund managers see potential in businesses that use AI to lift profits and in cheap small-cap stocks, though one warns that trying to time a shift away from the market’s biggest winners can be risky.
ticker_line: AI share wobble puts stock pickers back in focus
author: David Rogers
heading: Investments

title: Productivity: Chalmers lifts bank bond caps, deceased estate withdrawal limits
summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers has proposed raising the limit on banks’ covered bonds from 8% to 12% of their Australian assets, alongside simpler reporting rules for smaller banks and a higher deceased-estate expense withdrawal limit of $30,000. The changes are intended to cut costs and help smaller banks compete; Chalmers also warned that higher inflation and interest rates could mean weaker growth and slightly higher unemployment in the December budget update.
ticker_line: Chalmers proposes higher bank bond caps and simpler rules
author: Grace Lagan with James Eyers
heading: Banking

title: The retirement bonus you never knew existed
summary: Some super funds pay a retirement bonus when members move their savings into a pension account, which is generally tax-free, but the rules and amounts vary and some funds require members to have stayed for a minimum period. The bonus can be worth thousands, but advisers say people should also compare fees, service and investment performance before deciding whether to stay with their fund.
ticker_line: Retirement bonuses can add thousands to super balances
author: Anthony Keane
heading: Superannuation

title: Australia’s chance to own the AI boom
summary: TechnologyOne chief executive Ed Chung says Australia should build and own more AI technology, rather than rely on products developed overseas, so local intellectual property, jobs and economic benefits stay in the country. The Brisbane-based company invests more than $150 million a year in research and development and says its AI products were developed locally; Chung also backs national AI standards and government support for Australian technology.
ticker_line: TechnologyOne urges Australia to own more AI value
author: Story AMY PRICE
heading: AI

title: Aussie bank helping secure ‘lifetime income’
summary: AMP is launching a new program called Lifetime Super Boost, allowing retirees to convert their superannuation into a steady income for life. This initiative aims to help Australians feel more secure about their retirement finances and potentially qualify for more aged pension support.
ticker_line: AMP launches program for secure retirement income
author: NewsWire
heading: Superannuation

title: Sydney, Melbourne tipped to lead housing price drops as market cools
summary: Sydney and Melbourne are expected to see significant drops in housing prices, with Sydney homes potentially losing up to $122,000 and Melbourne's median price falling below $1 million. This decline is driven by higher interest rates and changes in tax policy affecting buyer demand.
ticker_line: Sydney, Melbourne housing prices set to fall
author: business Stephanie Chalmer
heading: Economy

title: RBA looks to get ahead of the curve on jobs
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia is rethinking how unemployment affects inflation, highlighting that low unemployment can lead to sharp wage increases and inflation. Deputy governor Andrew Hauser explains that their new research shows a nonlinear relationship, which influenced recent interest rate hikes to manage inflation pressures.
ticker_line: RBA adjusts strategies to tackle inflation pressures
author: DAVID ROGERS, MARKETS
heading: Economy

title: Tweak on super has ‘no defence’
summary: The SMSF Association criticises Labor's decision to ban self-managed funds from borrowing for property investments, saying it reduces investment options and does not solve the real issues. The change was made without consultation and could harm confidence in the superannuation system.
ticker_line: Labor's super change sparks SMSF backlash
heading: Superannuation

title: Macquarie to review KPMG audit process
summary: Macquarie is reviewing its decision to appoint KPMG as its auditor due to concerns over KPMG's integrity after recent misconduct allegations. The review will involve an external assessment and could lead to Macquarie changing auditors before KPMG officially starts in April 2028.
ticker_line: Macquarie reviews KPMG audit appointment amid concerns
author: Joanne Tran
heading: Regulation

title: Interest rates: Traders eye fourth rate rise after jobs surge
summary: Traders expect the Reserve Bank of Australia to raise interest rates for the fourth time this year after a surprising jump in employment numbers. The upcoming inflation data will be crucial in deciding if rates will increase next month.
ticker_line: Traders anticipate fourth RBA rate rise this year
author: Gus McCubbing
heading: Economy

title: Regional businesses strangled as operating costs skyrocket and profits plummet
summary: Regional businesses in Australia are struggling with rising costs and falling profits, with 90% facing increased expenses and many concerned about the impact of ongoing conflicts in the Middle East. The small business group COSBOA is urging the government to extend fuel excise relief and reconsider tax hikes that could further harm their viability.
ticker_line: Regional businesses face crisis as costs soar
author: THOMAS HENRY
heading: Economy

title: Solid jobs data keeps RBA on edge over rates
summary: Australia's job market saw a surprising increase of 76,300 jobs in June, leading to expectations of an interest rate rise by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) before Christmas. While the unemployment rate remains steady at 4.4%, rising inflation and strong job growth may push the RBA to act soon.
ticker_line: Strong jobs data raises rate hike expectations
author: DAVID ROGERS, MARKETS
heading: Economy

title: Labor backs super for all teen workers
summary: Labor has backed a policy to ensure all Australian teenagers earn superannuation, regardless of their work hours, after a recent conference. This change aims to protect young workers and could lead to new conflicts with business groups over costs.
ticker_line: Labor supports super for all teen workers
author: Elizabeth Pike
heading: Superannuation

title: AI boom powers fears for grid, push for rule change
summary: Australia's energy regulators are proposing new rules for large AI data centres to ensure they do not disrupt the national electricity grid. The changes aim to improve stability as these facilities become major electricity users.
ticker_line: New rules proposed for AI data centres' energy use
author: Colin Packham
heading: Regulation

title: Super fund giant splashes $882m on Westfield Garden City
summary: Australian Retirement Trust is buying a 50% stake in Westfield Mount Gravatt for $882.5 million from Scentre Group, pending competition approval. This deal marks the largest retail transaction in Australia this year and follows ART's significant investments in other properties.
ticker_line: ART invests $882m in Westfield Garden City
author: Chris Herde
heading: Investments

title: Insurers call for high earners without health cover to pay more tax
summary: Health funds want high-income Australians without private health insurance to face higher tax penalties, proposing to double the current Medicare levy surcharge. This change could affect nearly a million people and raise government revenue while encouraging more to take out private cover.
ticker_line: Insurers push for higher taxes on high earners
author: Michael Smith
heading: Health Insurance

title: Move to reform ‘essential’ last resort compo scheme
summary: The federal government plans to reform the Compensation Scheme of Last Resort to better protect consumers, including a new funding model and stricter rules on superannuation communication. These changes come after a significant rise in claims due to investment scheme collapses.
ticker_line: Government reforms last resort compensation scheme
heading: Regulation

title: Submissions open for NSW lawyers’ PI inquiry
summary: The NSW parliamentary inquiry is seeking submissions on professional indemnity insurance for solicitors, focusing on the monopoly held by Lawcover and the potential for new competition. Submissions are open until September 15, with hearings planned to discuss pricing and legislative changes.
ticker_line: NSW inquiry seeks input on lawyer insurance market
heading: Regulation

title: Top 20 AR networks report examines key issues
summary: A new report highlights the growth and changes in Australia's authorised representative (AR) sector, ranking the top 20 general insurance networks and discussing trends like consolidation, technology investment, and the evolving role of ARs in the insurance market.
ticker_line: Report reveals growth in Australia's AR networks
heading: General Insurance

title: AIA teams with Beyond Blue on mental health intervention
summary: AIA has partnered with Beyond Blue to improve mental health support in Australia, focusing on prevention and early intervention to help people before they reach crisis points. The partnership aims to address rising mental health claims, which have increased from 15% to 26% of disability claims since 2014.
ticker_line: AIA joins Beyond Blue to tackle mental health issues
heading: Health Insurance

title: Allianz community program extends help to farmers
summary: Allianz Australia is helping farming families recover from disasters through a new three-year partnership with Rural Aid. Their employees recently assisted at a recovery event in Queensland, supporting farmers affected by drought and floods.
ticker_line: Allianz partners with Rural Aid to support farmers
heading: General Insurance

title: Big change coming on October 1, banks panic
summary: Australia's major banks are raising credit card fees and cutting rewards as they prepare for a ban on surcharges starting October 1. This change, aimed at saving consumers money, is expected to cost banks around $660 million annually, leading to increased costs for cardholders.
ticker_line: Banks hike fees ahead of surcharge ban
author: Tamika Seeto
heading: Banking

title: CBA REVAMP’S HIDDEN STING
summary: Commonwealth Bank is changing its credit card loyalty program, introducing higher fees for many customers while promoting new rewards. Starting October 1, customers may find it harder to avoid fees and will need to spend more to benefit from the new points system.
ticker_line: CBA credit card fees set to rise
author: Julie-anne Sprague
heading: Banking

title: ASIC: The Devastating Impact Behind Bank Impersonation Scams
summary: ASIC warns Australians about bank impersonation scams that exploit trust, following HSBC's $35 million penalty for failing to protect customers. Victims report emotional and financial distress after being tricked by fake messages from their bank.
ticker_line: ASIC highlights dangers of bank impersonation scams
heading: Banking

title: AI cyber scams targeting homebuyers’ deposits
summary: New research shows that nearly 60% of Australians can't identify AI-generated scams targeting homebuyers' deposits. The number of people who believe they can spot these scams has dropped from 51% to 41%, raising concerns about the growing sophistication of fraudsters.
ticker_line: AI scams tricking homebuyers on the rise
author: Nathan Mawby
heading: AI

title: AI costs are rising for Australian businesses even as tokens get cheaper
summary: Australian businesses are spending more on AI, with costs rising despite cheaper tokens. Companies are struggling to see immediate benefits from their investments, leading to concerns about the long-term value of AI technology.
ticker_line: AI costs rise as benefits remain unclear
author: business Daniel Ziffer
heading: AI

title: Insurers have a lot of data about us. Where do they get it, and how do they use it?
summary: Insurers in Australia use a wide range of data, including personal details and big data analytics, to set premiums, which raises concerns about discrimination and privacy. New regulations are coming into effect to protect consumers, but risks remain as companies increasingly rely on AI and external data sources.
ticker_line: Insurers face scrutiny over data use and pricing
author: Fei Huang, Associate professor, UNS
heading: General Insurance

title: Meet the local start-up taking on AI giants
summary: Canberra couple Michael and Rachel Gately have launched Trellis Data's Agentaus, a local AI platform aimed at reducing Australia's reliance on foreign technology. They believe that building sovereign AI capabilities is crucial for national security and are receiving support from other countries in the Indo-Pacific region.
ticker_line: Local start-up Trellis Data launches sovereign AI platform
author: Ray Athwal
heading: AI

title: Investor’s savings lost after ASIC call
summary: A Queensland woman lost $310,000 in retirement savings after investing in the Global Capital Property Fund, which collapsed despite her checking with ASIC, who gave it a clean bill of health. She received $150,000 in compensation but questions ASIC's oversight.
ticker_line: ASIC's assurances fail investor in property fund
author: Cliona O’Dowd
heading: Superannuation

title: State Labor rejects over-65s insurance shift
summary: South Australia's Labor government opposes federal changes to private health insurance that could force 200,000 over-65s to downgrade their cover and 62,000 to drop it entirely. Critics warn this could strain public hospitals and increase wait times for care.
ticker_line: SA Labor rejects changes to health insurance for seniors
author: Noah Yim
heading: Health Insurance

title: OpenAI agent breached Medicare, Albanese reveals
summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced that an AI agent from OpenAI accessed both public and private files on Australia's Medicare portal in June. He expressed concern over the delay in OpenAI's notification to the government about the breach.
ticker_line: OpenAI AI agent breaches Medicare portal security
author: Rob Harris and David Swan
heading: Regulation

title: PM changes tack on need for digital safety laws
summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has shifted his stance on proposed digital safety laws, now linking them to the rise of misinformation and disinformation. The draft legislation would require social media platforms to protect users from harmful content, but critics warn it could lead to censorship.
ticker_line: PM Albanese links digital safety laws to misinformation
author: JACK QUAIL
heading: Regulation

title: RBA’s Ross: productivity key to sustainable real-wage rises
summary: Iain Ross from the Reserve Bank says that increasing productivity is essential for sustainable real wage growth in Australia, and he sees no signs of a wage-price spiral like in the 1970s. He highlights that current wage-setting rules are different and limit the ability for widespread wage increases.
ticker_line: RBA's Ross: Productivity Crucial for Wage Growth
author: EWIN HANNAN
heading: Economy

title: NAB has most of its services restored, after experiencing major digital outage
summary: National Australia Bank (NAB) has mostly restored its services after a digital outage affected internet banking, the mobile app, and phone lines. Some business customers are still facing login issues, and NAB has not disclosed the cause of the outage.
ticker_line: NAB restores most services after digital outage
author: business Adelaide Miller
heading: Banking

title: ACCC again blocks sale of RAC WA's insurance arm to Sydney-based IAG
summary: The ACCC has blocked the sale of RAC WA's insurance arm to IAG, stating it would reduce competition and likely raise insurance premiums in Western Australia. IAG plans to apply for a public benefit assessment to argue the deal's advantages.
ticker_line: ACCC blocks RAC WA and IAG insurance deal
heading: General Insurance

title: Macquarie secures $1.45bn in unusual bond play
summary: Macquarie Group is raising $1.45 billion through bonds, including a rare 10-year floating rate note. The offering attracted $3 billion in demand and comes as the bank reports a 30% increase in profit for the 2026 financial year.
ticker_line: Macquarie raises $1.45bn in bond market
author: BRIDGET CARTER, DATA ROOM
heading: Banking

title: Comparison websites under fire for misleading customers
summary: The corporate regulator, ASIC, is taking action against comparison websites for misleading customers about their services. They have sued Clark Family for falsely claiming to provide comprehensive comparisons and recently won a case against Choosi, which also misled consumers about insurance options.
ticker_line: ASIC cracks down on misleading comparison websites
author: Anthony Keane
heading: Regulation

title: Reserve governor: IGR a ‘call to action’
summary: Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock called the Intergenerational Report a 'call to action' for improving Australia's productivity, while expressing concerns about the potential risks of the AI boom. She highlighted the need for government support in business investment and innovation to achieve the report's productivity growth targets.
ticker_line: RBA governor urges action on productivity growth
author: MATTHEW CRANSTON, THOMAS HENRY
heading: Economy

title: Technology: AI scribe health start-up hits unicorn status with $476 million capital raising
summary: Heidi, an AI scribe start-up from Melbourne, has raised $476 million and reached a valuation of $1.26 billion, making it Australia's latest unicorn. The funding will help expand its AI capabilities in healthcare, despite concerns about regulatory oversight and patient privacy.
ticker_line: Heidi becomes Australia's newest tech unicorn
author: David Swan
heading: Health Insurance

title: Australian insurers submit enhanced code of practice to regulator
summary: The Insurance Council of Australia submitted a strengthened General Insurance Code of Practice to ASIC on 22 October, after consulting consumer groups, regulators, government and insurers. The revised code includes enforceable obligations and aims to improve support for vulnerable customers and people in financial hardship, as well as make claims handling more transparent and accountable.
ticker_line: Insurers submit stronger consumer protection code to ASIC
author: Jake Nathanoel Dellosa
heading: General Insurance

title: CBA may buy back share in Colonial First State
summary: CBA may buy back the 55 per cent of Colonial First State it sold to KKR in 2020, after other potential buyers reportedly failed to meet the business’s roughly $5bn asking price. The move could return CFS to CBA as banks look for growth in wealth management, but it is unclear whether CBA would meet KKR’s price expectations.
ticker_line: CBA may bring Colonial First State back in-house
author: DATA ROOM with BRIDGET CARTER
heading: Banking

title: $108m super rip-off for teenage workers
summary: About 124,000 working teenagers in Queensland are expected to miss out on a combined $108 million in super this financial year because under-18s qualify only if they work more than 30 hours a week for one employer. The Super Members Council says the average teenager will miss out on $870, with the gap potentially reaching $11,200 by retirement; a Senate inquiry is due to report in November as calls grow to change the rule.
ticker_line: Queensland teens to miss out on $108m in super
author: Ellen Ransley
heading: Superannuation

title: Protect the fair go in digital age, says ACTU
summary: ACTU secretary Melissa Donnelly has urged a Senate inquiry to recommend enforceable rules protecting workers from AI, including transparency and consultation before employers introduce it. She cited NAB’s planned 2,500 job cuts and a recent Medicare data breach, and called for Australia to build its own AI capability rather than rely on large US technology companies.
ticker_line: ACTU calls for enforceable AI protections for workers
author: EWIN HANNAN
heading: AI

title: Connections still there to be data centre power
summary: Energy economist Margarita Patria says Australia remains well placed to attract data centre investment, despite Firmus Technologies abandoning its proposed $7bn IPO, as US power limits and constraints in other countries create demand for overseas capacity. Firmus has since signed deals with Thinking Machines Lab and OpenAI, while local operator NextDC has frozen new projects and land purchases after power supply problems and community objections at its Melbourne site.
ticker_line: Australia remains in the running for data centre investment
author: Stewart Oldfield
heading: AI

title: Victoria’s data centre push could force state back onto gas-fired power
summary: Victoria's growing demand for data centres may force the state to rely more on gas-fired power, as local gas production declines and renewable projects face delays. This situation raises concerns about the state's energy transition plans and potential increases in electricity prices.
ticker_line: Victoria's data centres may increase gas reliance
author: Daniella White
heading: AI

title: ASIC warns of high-interest car loan traps and risky lending practices in new report
summary: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) warns about high-interest car loans and risky lending practices, highlighting cases like Holly Reid's, where borrowers face excessive fees and financial stress. The report reveals that some lenders, especially Rapid Loans, charge extremely high rates and fees, leading to severe consequences for borrowers who struggle to repay their loans.
ticker_line: ASIC warns of risky car loan practices
author: by national consumer affa
heading: Regulation

title: Senior Albanese minister clashes with Pocock over top-secret AI copyright claim
summary: David Pocock and Minister Tim Ayres clashed in Parliament over claims that the government is considering allowing AI companies to use Australian copyright material without proper licensing. Pocock alleges there are two proposals being discussed, while Ayres insists the government will not weaken copyright protections.
ticker_line: Minister clashes with Pocock over AI copyright claims
author: national AI and technology
heading: Regulation

title: RBA in a bind: Fight inflation or risk recession
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia faces a tough choice between raising interest rates to control high inflation or risking a recession as the economy slows. Recent data shows inflation remains high, and while the cash rate is currently at 4.35%, further hikes may be needed if inflation does not decrease significantly.
ticker_line: RBA struggles with inflation and recession risks
author: DAVID ROGERS MARKETS
heading: Economy

title: Payday super poses cash flow challenge
summary: From July 1, employers in Australia must pay superannuation at the same time as salaries, which could create cash flow problems for businesses. Experts warn that this change, aimed at recovering $5.7 billion in unpaid super, will particularly impact small and medium-sized enterprises.
ticker_line: Payday super reform to challenge business cash flow
author: CAMERON MICALLEF
heading: Superannuation

title: Bosses warned of AI cyber onslaught
summary: The Australian Signals Directorate and its Five Eyes partners warn businesses to prepare for a surge in cyber attacks using advanced AI technology, which poses a significant risk to IT networks. Companies are urged to improve their cybersecurity measures and integrate AI into their strategies to combat these evolving threats.
ticker_line: Businesses warned of AI-driven cyber attack risks
author: BEN PACKHAM
heading: AI

title: Closing Bell: ASIC leaves equity analysts out in cold
summary: ASIC has reduced the rules for equity analysts in IPOs but keeps strict limits on their independence from investment bankers. This change aims to improve the IPO process in Australia, though analysts remain largely sidelined.
ticker_line: ASIC eases rules for IPO equity analysts
author: Anthony Macdonald
heading: Regulation

title: A Revolut revolution, or just another big bank?
summary: Revolut has received approval to operate as a bank in Australia, posing a significant challenge to the big four banks. With its advanced technology and global reach, it aims to attract customers, especially younger ones, while competing with established players like Macquarie Bank.
ticker_line: Revolut gains banking licence, challenges big banks
author: Eric Johnston, Associate
heading: Banking

title: Aware strikes $226m deal to buy into prestigious Sydney tower
summary: Aware Super has agreed to buy a 50% stake in the 100 Market Street office tower in Sydney for $226 million, partnering with Hong Kong's Link Asset Management. This deal reflects a growing interest in premium office properties as superannuation funds invest in the recovery of Sydney's office market.
ticker_line: Aware Super invests $226m in Sydney office tower
author: Ben Wilmot
heading: Investments

title: Long-term supply deals fizzle if this boom fades
summary: Long-term contracts in the AI supply chain are boosting profits for memory chip makers like Micron and SK Hynix, but if demand falls, these contracts may be renegotiated, leading to potential financial surprises for investors. The reliance on these deals raises concerns about future stability in the AI market.
ticker_line: AI supply contracts face uncertainty as demand shifts
author: Asa Fitch
heading: AI

title: How smart car technology could prevent one in five road casualties
summary: A study by IAG shows that Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) could prevent over 7000 road casualties annually in Australia, but many drivers are not using these safety features. Starting August 1, 2026, new cars must have car-to-pedestrian Autonomous Emergency Braking, highlighting the need for better driver education and trust in these technologies.
ticker_line: New car safety tech could cut road deaths
heading: General Insurance

title: ‘Frighteningly easy’: How fake AI payslips fuel mortgage fraud
summary: A recent investigation by Austrac found that AI is making it easier for criminals to create fake payslips and documents, leading to hundreds of millions of dollars in suspected mortgage fraud in Australia. Banks are urged to improve their systems to detect these fakes, while calls are being made for government support to change how income is verified.
ticker_line: AI boosts mortgage fraud risks for banks
author: Clancy Yeates
heading: Banking

title: Crisafulli to defy PM, pitch alternative plan for data centres
summary: Queensland Premier David Crisafulli plans to propose a new framework for data centre approvals that includes local consultations and allows for a mix of energy sources, opposing the federal government's push for 100% renewable energy. This comes as Queensland and the Northern Territory resist national standards aimed at the data centre industry.
ticker_line: Queensland defies federal renewable energy rules for data centres
author: Sarah Elks, Lachlan Leeming
heading: Regulation

title: Albanese to settle AI data centre energy rules, overriding defiant Queensland
summary: The federal government plans to enforce new energy rules for AI data centres, requiring them to use renewable energy, despite opposition from Queensland. The government aims to override state laws to ensure data centres do not increase power prices and to attract investment in renewable projects.
ticker_line: Federal government to enforce energy rules for data centres
author: senior political correspondent Jake
heading: Regulation

title: Aon champions Australia-developed flood assessment tool
summary: Aon has introduced a new flood assessment tool developed by Geoscape Australia that uses AI to evaluate flood risks for properties. This tool could help reduce insurance premiums for many Australians by providing more accurate risk assessments.
ticker_line: Aon launches AI flood assessment tool for insurers
heading: General Insurance

title: Michele Bullock's final speech before RBA board meeting cements interest rate rise bets
summary: Reserve Bank Governor Michele Bullock's recent comments suggest a likely interest rate rise at the upcoming board meeting, with major banks adjusting their forecasts accordingly. Fixed mortgage rates are already increasing as markets anticipate this change, while Bullock also discussed the potential economic impact of artificial intelligence.
ticker_line: Interest rate hike expected as banks adjust forecasts
author: business Michael Janda
heading: Economy

title: Andrew Bragg re-ignites super debate by floating ideas to lift home ownership
summary: Shadow Housing Minister Andrew Bragg is discussing how superannuation could help Australians buy homes, but no formal policies have been announced yet. He suggests using super as collateral for loans or allowing withdrawals for house deposits, while the Coalition's stance on superannuation policy remains unclear.
ticker_line: Bragg sparks superannuation and housing ownership debate
author: political Erin Handley
heading: Superannuation

title: AI data centre funding surges to record $35 billion this year, RBA analysis shows
summary: Australian data centre operators have raised a record $35 billion in 2026, driven by the growing demand for AI infrastructure. This funding is mainly through borrowing, raising concerns about its impact on other businesses and inflation.
ticker_line: Data centre funding hits record $35 billion in 2026
author: by business Lin
heading: Economy

title: ASIC draws line in the sand on private credit
summary: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) is warning the private credit sector to improve its standards or face enforcement actions. Issues like governance and transparency have been highlighted, especially following the financial troubles of Bathla Group, which owes $3.4 billion.
ticker_line: ASIC warns private credit sector to improve standards
author: CLIONA O’DOWD
heading: Regulation

title: ASIC sues ex-Super Retail boss Heraghty
summary: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission is suing former Super Retail Group CEO Anthony Heraghty for breaching his duties and misleading the board about an undisclosed affair with a senior executive, which led to significant legal costs for the company. The case raises concerns about corporate governance and transparency.
ticker_line: ASIC sues ex-Super Retail boss for misconduct
author: CLIONA O’DOWD
heading: Regulation

title: Coalition flags super for mortgages
summary: The Coalition is proposing to allow Australians to use their superannuation as collateral for home loans, aiming to make it easier to buy a house. This plan comes amid a split in the opposition and follows previous unsuccessful attempts to access super for housing.
ticker_line: Coalition proposes superannuation for home loans
author: Paul Sakkal
heading: Superannuation

title: One in five fears AI redundancy
summary: A recent survey shows that over 20% of white-collar workers fear losing their jobs to AI within three years, with 44% worried about job loss in the next decade. While AI use in workplaces is rising, many workers feel unprepared and are calling for better training and notice periods for job losses due to AI.
ticker_line: Workers fear AI job losses in coming years
author: EWIN HANNAN WORKPLACE EDI
heading: AI

title: Carroll eyes new rules amid boom in data centres
summary: The Victorian government plans new rules for data centres, banning them from residential areas and requiring them to use their own renewable energy and non-drinking water. These changes aim to address community concerns and ensure local benefits from the booming data centre market.
ticker_line: Victoria introduces new rules for data centres
author: Kieran Rooney | State politics repo
heading: Regulation

title: What new super advice fee rules mean for SMSFs
summary: New advice-fee caps announced for APRA-regulated super funds do not apply to SMSFs, but SMSFs still must only pay for advice that relates to running the fund. Trustees and advisers should agree on a fair split between fund and personal advice, review it each year, and note that GST-registered SMSFs may claim back some GST on eligible investment advice fees.
ticker_line: SMSFs must split advice fees fairly between fund and member
author: Meg Heffron
heading: Superannuation

title: Chalmers warns of slower growth as traders bet on rate rise next month
summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers says higher inflation and interest rates are likely to slow economic growth and slightly lift unemployment ahead of the government’s December update. The RBA says lower government spending can ease inflation, while traders now see a 64 per cent chance it will raise its 4.6 per cent cash rate next month.
ticker_line: Chalmers warns growth will slow as rate rise looms
author: Grace Lagan
heading: Economy

title: Rate rise bets jump after RBA inflation warning
summary: RBA deputy governor Andrew Hauser warned inflation is running well above the bank’s expectations, making another rate rise possible despite a slowing economy and easing jobs market. After his comments, markets lifted the chance of a November increase from 27% to 57%; September-quarter inflation figures due on October 28 will help shape the RBA’s decision.
ticker_line: RBA rate rise bets jump after inflation warning
author: Grace Lagan
heading: Economy

title: Big super loses governance ace in mystery exit
summary: ACSI governance adviser Ed John, a key figure in its advice to major super funds on shareholder votes, left in August without an explanation, prompting concern among some members and board representatives. The departure comes amid wider questions about ACSI’s leadership and fees, though the organisation says its stewardship work will continue without interruption.
ticker_line: Key ACSI governance adviser leaves without explanation
author: Patrick Durkin and Mark Di Stefano
heading: Superannuation

title: NDIS blowouts lead $145b surge in surprise costs
summary: An analysis by HSBC chief economist Paul Bloxham found unexpected spending forecast increases of $145.6 billion over the Albanese government’s term, with the NDIS a major source of overruns. Economists say rising government spending may add to inflation, while Treasurer Jim Chalmers faces pressure to find about $11 billion in savings for December’s budget update.
ticker_line: NDIS overruns drive $145.6b in surprise spending
author: Michael Read
heading: Economy

title: Jim Chalmers declares optimism about business investment despite domestic gloom
summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers says business investment is expected to grow by more than 5 per cent this financial year—twice the May forecast and about $50 billion more than expected—as overseas investors see Australia as a stable place to invest. The outlook comes as inflation remains stubborn, unemployment has risen to 4.7 per cent and the Reserve Bank may raise interest rates again, adding to pressure on households and the government.
ticker_line: Chalmers points to investment boom amid economic strain
author: economics Tom Crowley
heading: Economy

title: Australians raid $1.4b from superannuation for medical costs as regulators warn of 'predatory' tactics
summary: Australians withdrew a record $1.46 billion from superannuation on compassionate grounds in 2025–26, mostly for medical costs, including $892 million for dental treatment. Regulators say some health practitioners are using misleading or predatory tactics to encourage unnecessary withdrawals, while consumer groups warn that taking money from super can leave people with much less in retirement.
ticker_line: Record $1.46b withdrawn from super for medical costs
author: national health Stephanie
heading: Superannuation

title: TPD Sustainability Pressures Topic of Industry Debate
summary: Australia's financial regulators are urging life insurers to take stronger action on sustainability issues in Total Permanent Disability (TPD) insurance, following a recent industry debate. The discussion highlighted increasing mental health claims and the need for product redesign to improve affordability and manage risks.
ticker_line: Regulators push insurers on TPD sustainability challenges
heading: Life Insurance

title: Economy: Traders cut rate rise bets after jobs shock
summary: Traders are less sure the Reserve Bank of Australia will raise interest rates after a surprising rise in unemployment, which suggests the economy may be slowing. While some analysts predict more rate hikes due to ongoing inflation, others believe recent budget changes could reduce the need for further increases.
ticker_line: Traders doubt RBA will raise rates after jobs data
author: Cecile Lefort
heading: Economy

title: Bourse has best day in six weeks
summary: The Australian sharemarket had its best day in six weeks, with the S&P/ASX 200 rising 1.47% to 8621.7, driven by higher unemployment data and a positive lead from Wall Street. Mining stocks led the gains, while the unemployment rate increased to 4.5% in April, suggesting interest rates may stay steady.
ticker_line: Australian sharemarket sees biggest gain in weeks
author: BLAIR JACKSON, EQUITIES
heading: Economy

title: Jobless spike stalls RBA’s next rate hike, for now
summary: Australia's unemployment rate rose to 4.5% in April, leading the Reserve Bank to likely hold interest rates steady at its June meeting. Economists expect a rate hike may still happen by August, depending on future economic data.
ticker_line: Jobless rate rise delays RBA's next rate hike
author: DAVID ROGERS, MARKETS
heading: Economy

title: Greens demand Labor tax changes extend to SMSFs
summary: The Greens are pushing Labor to change tax rules for self-managed super funds (SMSFs) and limit borrowing arrangements as part of negotiations over a budget tax bill. They are also concerned that big businesses will benefit from new capital gains tax changes.
ticker_line: Greens demand tax changes for SMSFs in negotiations
author: MATTHEW CRANSTON
heading: Superannuation

title: National Australia Bank deploys AI analytics tools
summary: National Australia Bank (NAB) has launched new AI tools called Genie and Genie code to help users easily query complex data using plain English. These tools aim to simplify data analysis for businesses.
ticker_line: NAB launches AI tools to simplify data queries
heading: AI

title: Australia: Free mental health support used nearly 50,000 in Western Australia
summary: Nearly 50,000 free mental health sessions have been provided in Western Australia through Medicare Mental Health Centres. The Albanese Government plans to expand these centres, investing an additional $29.9 million to improve access to on-call mental health professionals.
ticker_line: Free mental health support reaches 50,000 in WA
heading: Health Insurance

title: Minefield of AI tax returns
summary: Many Australians are using AI tools like ChatGPT to prepare their tax returns, hoping to find more deductions. However, experts warn this could lead to mistakes and penalties from the ATO, as many people are already relying on expected refunds to cover bills and debts.
ticker_line: Australians risk ATO penalties using AI for tax
author: Peter Jenkins
heading: Regulation

title: Nation’s largest power company probes data breach
summary: Origin Energy is investigating a data breach that may have exposed personal details of up to 2 million customers. The company has reported the incident to authorities and is urging customers to monitor their accounts for suspicious activity.
ticker_line: Origin Energy faces major data breach investigation
author: Nick Toscano and David Swan
heading: Regulation

title: Mental health claims load to land on business
summary: Mental health claims are increasing costs for businesses in Australia, with workers' compensation reforms failing to ease the burden. Experts warn that these claims are more expensive and complex, leading to higher insurance premiums and longer recovery times for affected workers.
ticker_line: Rising mental health claims strain business insurance costs
author: Sian Powell
heading: General Insurance

title: Flight from top health cover 'an existential risk'
summary: Many Australians are dropping top-tier health insurance due to rising costs, which could threaten the future of the health insurance sector. Experts warn that this trend may lead to more people relying on public hospitals, increasing waiting times for care.
ticker_line: Health insurance faces existential threat from cost issues
author: Sian Powell
heading: Health Insurance

title: The last line of defence against climate threats
summary: By 2050, over 1.5 million Australians may face severe flooding due to climate change, impacting both homes and businesses. Insurers are working to better reflect these risks in policy pricing, while regulators push for clearer communication about rising premiums and improved consumer protections.
ticker_line: Insurers adapt to climate risks and rising premiums
author: Alexandra Cain
heading: General Insurance

title: Call to subsidise property cover in hard-hit regions
summary: Experts are calling for subsidised property insurance in areas hit hard by natural disasters, as many homeowners face unaffordable premiums. A national risk assessment system is also recommended to help manage these costs and improve resilience against future disasters.
ticker_line: Call for subsidised insurance in disaster-hit areas
author: Sian Powell
heading: General Insurance

title: Most Australians don't understand how interest rates affect inflation, RBA survey finds
summary: A Reserve Bank survey shows many Australians misunderstand how interest rates affect inflation, with only 25% correctly linking higher rates to lower inflation. This confusion could impact public trust and the effectiveness of the Bank's monetary policies.
ticker_line: Survey reveals gaps in Australians' economic knowledge
author: business correspondent David Taylor
heading: Economy

title: Australian CMOs stuck at early AI maturity stages
summary: A report shows that 83% of Australian marketers are still in the early stages of using AI, with most lacking clear strategies and roadmaps. While there is excitement about AI, many teams are cautious and face challenges in turning AI use into real business benefits.
ticker_line: Australian marketers lag in AI maturity levels
author: AdNews
heading: AI

title: Kelty flays ALP bid for cash reforms
summary: Bill Kelty criticises the Albanese government's plan to give more power to regulators for cash distribution, calling it a waste of taxpayer money. He argues that funds should be better spent on urgent social needs, while Linfox Armaguard warns the legislation could lead to unfair nationalisation of the cash sector.
ticker_line: Kelty slams cash reform plan as wasteful
author: Thomas Henry
heading: Regulation

title: Diversity hawks defeated to halt private markets rush
summary: The ASX has simplified its corporate governance rules, keeping a 30% female board target but dropping plans for broader diversity measures. A new advisory group, led by Philip Lowe, aims to make it easier for companies to list publicly by reducing regulatory burdens.
ticker_line: ASX simplifies governance rules, drops diversity plans
author: Cliona O’Dowd, Joseph Carbone
heading: Regulation

title: Labor bets house on tax reform, but may wreck the economy
summary: David Murray, former CEO of Commonwealth Bank, criticizes the Albanese government's proposed tax reforms aimed at addressing housing affordability, warning they could harm the economy. Recent data shows a significant drop in home loan applications and a decline in home buyer activity, raising concerns about falling house prices and their impact on consumer spending.
ticker_line: Tax reforms could hurt housing market and economy
author: MATTHEW CRANSTON
heading: Economy

title: Radical plan on surgery waitlist
summary: A new plan aims to reduce public elective surgery waiting lists by allowing minor surgeries to be done in private day hospitals. This could save up to $1 billion annually and improve patient care without increasing wait times for private patients.
ticker_line: New plan to cut surgery waitlists in SA
author: Brad Crouch
heading: Health Insurance

title: Albanese signs declaration with world leaders calling for international AI safeguards
summary: Australia and other world leaders have signed a declaration at the UN calling for stronger international rules on artificial intelligence. They want mandatory safety testing and independent evaluations to ensure AI systems are safe and beneficial, while avoiding a halt in development.
ticker_line: World leaders push for AI safety regulations
author: Rob Harris
heading: AI

title: ASIC alleges insurance comparator misled consumers
summary: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) is suing Clark Family for misleading consumers about its insurance comparison services, claiming the company falsely represented that it compared multiple products when it actually sold consumer inquiries to brokers. This alleged misconduct occurred from September 2020 to September 2026.
ticker_line: ASIC takes action against insurance comparator Clark Family
heading: Regulation

title: Lawcover warns of PI competition detriment
summary: Lawcover, the main provider of professional indemnity insurance for NSW solicitors, warns that new competition could harm smaller firms by increasing premiums for high-risk practices. The state inquiry is considering reforms after a proposal for cheaper insurance was rejected.
ticker_line: Lawcover warns of risks from new PI competition
heading: General Insurance

title: SIRA move excludes physio
summary: The NSW State Insurance Regulatory Authority has banned physiotherapist Didier Regis Brunet from working in personal injury schemes due to concerns about his practice. This decision affects his business, Gorokan Physio, and follows a referral to health regulatory bodies for further action.
ticker_line: SIRA bans physio from personal injury schemes
heading: Regulation

title: ICWA improves performance in milestone year
summary: The Insurance Commission of Western Australia reported a profit of $273.3 million for the year ending June 30, 2026, significantly up from $114 million the previous year, driven by lower claims and strong investment returns. This year marks its 100th anniversary and includes a new five-year strategic plan to enhance services.
ticker_line: ICWA reports record profits in centenary year
heading: General Insurance

title: Chalmers’ reforms trigger stampede on super contributions
summary: New tax changes have led to a 35% increase in voluntary superannuation contributions, especially from investors aged 50 and over, as they seek to protect their wealth. Major funds like AustralianSuper and MLC are seeing a surge in contributions, with many considering superannuation a more attractive investment option than property.
ticker_line: Surge in super contributions amid tax changes
author: Anthony Keane
heading: Superannuation

title: Big-spending AI resist creators
summary: AI companies are investing heavily in infrastructure but are reluctant to pay for the data needed to train their models. The Australian government faces criticism for potentially compromising copyright protections for creators as it considers changes to copyright law amid pressure from these AI giants.
ticker_line: AI giants clash with creators over copyright laws
author: Jared Lynch
heading: Regulation

title: Super fund chiefs defend Firmus IPO snub as ‘doing their job’
summary: Aware Super chief investment officer Simon Warner said super funds were right to reject Firmus’s proposed $7 billion sharemarket listing, citing its high proposed value and lack of proven business fundamentals; UniSuper also considered the deal too speculative. The comments came as data-centre operator NextDC shares fell 40 per cent after it cut its 2027 revenue and earnings forecasts, adding to growing caution about AI and data-centre investments.
ticker_line: Super funds defend rejecting Firmus as data-centre risks rise
author: Bridget Carter
heading: Superannuation

title: RBA deputy warns inflation outlook 'materially worse' ahead of November meeting
summary: RBA deputy governor Andrew Hauser says inflation is running worse than the bank expected and risks becoming entrenched, increasing the chance of an interest rate rise at the November 3 meeting. Inflation was 4 per cent in August, above the RBA’s 2–3 per cent target; the bank will release updated forecasts on the same day as its rate decision.
ticker_line: RBA warns worsening inflation could prompt November rate rise
author: Stephanie Chalmer
heading: Economy

title: An AI-cloned free tool is being dubbed 'the end of software'
summary: AI tools are making it faster and cheaper to copy software, with developers already creating free versions of Microsoft Office and Adobe Creative products. Supporters say this could give users more control, but experts warn it may undermine developers’ work, strengthen AI companies and create legal disputes because Australia’s copyright rules are unclear on AI-assisted copying.
ticker_line: AI tools make software copying faster and cheaper
author: technology James Purtill
heading: AI

title: Financial Services: Fears banks to follow NAB's jobs layoff lead
summary: NAB plans to cut 2500 jobs, including up to 1500 by the end of 2026, and reduce its use of contractors to simplify operations and improve efficiency. The Finance Sector Union warned other banks may follow, while NAB said customer-facing roles would not be materially affected; the cuts are expected to cost about $300 million before tax in the 2027 financial year.
ticker_line: NAB to cut 2500 jobs as union warns rivals may follow
author: Colin Kruger and Elias Visontay
heading: Banking

title: AI spending boom out of puff, says Macquarie
summary: Macquarie says the AI investment boom may slow as higher interest rates, funding concerns and power constraints make it harder to build data centres. It expects Australian infrastructure, property and healthcare stocks to benefit before any RBA rate cuts, while retailers and housing-related companies may do better once cuts begin.
ticker_line: Macquarie warns AI investment boom may be slowing
author: David Rogers, markets
heading: Investments

title: Workplace: 'AI is automating entire jobs', warns new ACTU president
summary: Incoming ACTU president Emma Kingdon says unions will push for stronger protections as AI automates some jobs, monitors workers and makes workplace decisions. Starting in December, she will also focus on the cost of living, higher wages and giving workers more flexibility, while criticising employers for failing to consult staff about changes and job cuts.
ticker_line: Incoming ACTU chief warns AI is replacing jobs
author: Millie Muroi
heading: AI

title: ASIC Warns of "Lost Generation" Risk if Australia Falls Behind on Fintech and AI
summary: ASIC warns that Australia could face a 'lost generation' if it doesn't keep up with global fintech and AI advancements. The regulator's report highlights the need for better industry engagement and innovation support to avoid a decline in living standards.
ticker_line: ASIC warns of risk to Australia's financial future
publication: Financial and Business News | Finance Magnates
author: Damian Chmiel
heading: Regulation

title: From SpaceX to OpenAI, Australians are piling into Wall St’s mega-deals
summary: Australians are increasingly investing in major US tech companies like SpaceX and OpenAI as local market options dwindle. SpaceX plans to go public in mid-June, potentially raising $80 billion, while interest in related investment funds is growing.
ticker_line: Australians flock to US tech investments
author: Alex Gluyas
heading: AI

title: RBA still stuck between a rock and a hike place
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia may hold interest rates steady next month after recent job losses suggest the economy is slowing, but inflation risks remain high due to ongoing global tensions and rising oil prices.
ticker_line: RBA may pause rate hikes amid job losses
author: James Thomson
heading: Economy

title: CSIRO cuts climate research jobs despite budget funding boost
summary: CSIRO will cut 92 jobs from its climate research teams despite receiving an extra $387.4 million in funding. Critics warn this could weaken Australia's ability to model and predict climate change impacts.
ticker_line: CSIRO cuts climate jobs despite funding boost
author: Bianca Hall and Mike Foley
heading: General Insurance

title: Negative gearing ban forces loan review
summary: Westpac has informed mortgage brokers that it will not honour pre-approved investor loans due to the federal government's ban on negative gearing for existing properties. This change is expected to reduce borrowing capacity for many investors by up to 20%.
ticker_line: Westpac reviews loans after negative gearing ban
author: Angira Bharadwaj
heading: Banking

title: AusSuper chair slams 'flawed' annual test
summary: Don Russell, chairman of AustralianSuper, criticises the annual performance test for super funds, calling it flawed and harmful to investment decisions. He supports proposed changes by Treasurer Jim Chalmers but believes a complete overhaul is necessary to encourage better investments for the economy.
ticker_line: Super fund test needs major overhaul, says Russell
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Superannuation

title: Buy local to build Aussie AI industry
summary: Australia is being urged to support local AI start-ups to strengthen its digital economy and ensure data sovereignty. Government officials stress that buying from Australian firms will help build expertise and competitiveness in the growing AI sector.
ticker_line: Support local AI firms to boost Australia's tech industry
author: Alexandra Cain
heading: AI

title: Australia leads rise of the small language model
summary: Australia is emerging as a leader in developing small language models (SLMs), which are more manageable and cost-effective than larger models. Businesses are increasingly recognising the benefits of creating their own SLMs using specialised data to gain a competitive edge.
ticker_line: Australia leads in small language model development
author: Alexandra Cain
heading: AI

title: CVs losing value for hiring as use of artificial intelligence changes industry, recruiters say
summary: The recruitment industry is changing as more job seekers and employers use artificial intelligence (AI), making traditional CVs less effective. Experts suggest that while AI helps in creating tailored applications, candidates must still showcase their unique skills and experiences.
ticker_line: AI reshapes job applications and recruitment process
heading: AI

title: ‘Brave assumptions’: FWC queries inflation forecasts
summary: The Fair Work Commission is questioning the government's inflation forecasts as it considers a wage rise for workers. The ACTU is pushing for a 6% increase, while the government suggests a rise below 5% could still be acceptable.
ticker_line: FWC questions government inflation forecasts for wage rise
author: EWIN HANNAN
heading: Economy

title: Climate inaction to force up rates: Kean
summary: Matt Kean, Australia's climate change tsar, warns that failing to address climate change will lead to permanently higher interest rates and lower household incomes. A report shows that the economic impact of climate inaction will be severe, particularly in NSW and Queensland.
ticker_line: Climate inaction could raise interest rates permanently
author: ROSIE LEWIS, NATIONAL AFFAIRS CORRE
heading: General Insurance

title: Major bank reveals big change to branches
summary: ANZ Bank will open 27 branches on Saturdays starting June 27, 2026, to help customers who are busy during the week. The branches will offer services like home loans and specialist support, but not over-the-counter transactions.
ticker_line: ANZ Bank to open 27 branches on Saturdays
author: Jack Nivison
heading: Banking

title: IAG report reveals generational economic strain
summary: IAG's new report shows Australians are cautiously optimistic despite facing rising costs and climate issues, but younger generations feel more financial pressure than older ones. The report highlights a growing gap in resilience between different age groups and regions across the country.
ticker_line: IAG report highlights generational economic divides
author: Advertiser content for IAG
heading: General Insurance

title: NIB in stealth restructure, defence mandate change-up
summary: NIB Holdings is undergoing a major internal restructure after selling its travel division, leading to the departure of its health insurance chief, James Barr. The company has also changed its corporate defence advisor from Citi to Morgan Stanley amid a cautious outlook for its operations.
ticker_line: NIB Holdings restructures after travel division sale
author: Sarah Thompson and Kanika Sood and
heading: Health Insurance

title: Super’s ‘valley of pain’ meets Labor’s CGT trap
summary: The government's new capital gains tax changes are affecting how retirees manage their pensions and investments. A minimum 30% tax rate could encourage some retirees to collect a small pension, but it may also complicate their financial planning and investment returns.
ticker_line: New tax changes reshape retirement planning for Australians
author: Anthony Keane
heading: Superannuation

title: Actuaries Institute report shows tax system favouring older Australians
summary: A report from the Actuaries Institute shows that Australia's tax system benefits older Australians more than younger ones, leading to a significant income gap. For example, a 71-year-old with a $100,000 income has a net income of $128,100, while a 30-year-old with the same income has only $85,700 after taxes and government benefits.
ticker_line: Tax system favours older Australians over youth
author: business Gareth Hutchens
heading: Economy

title: Super funds falling short
summary: Australia's top 30 super funds have only invested 4% of the renewable energy needed to meet 2030 climate goals, contributing just $771 million to clean energy projects. Only six of these funds have direct investments in renewable energy or battery storage.
ticker_line: Super funds lag in renewable energy investments
heading: Superannuation

title: Small businesses concerned personal savings will be relied on amid payday super changes
summary: Starting July 1, 2026, businesses in Australia must pay superannuation to employees on payday instead of quarterly. While this aims to improve transparency and reduce unpaid super, many small businesses are worried about cash flow issues and may need to rely on personal savings to meet these new obligations.
ticker_line: New payday super rules raise cash flow concerns
author: business Adelaide Miller
heading: Superannuation

title: RBA rates to be higher for longer as oil shock adds to labour costs
summary: Iren, a data centre company run by Australian brothers Dan and Will Roberts, saw its shares rise by 19.6% after signing $US2.8 billion in new contracts and increasing its revenue target for AI Cloud services. The company now has significant cash reserves and is expanding its AI Cloud capacity rapidly.
ticker_line: Iren shares soar on new AI contracts
author: David Rogers, Valerina Changarathil
heading: Investments

title: Banks seek tax data access to fight AI fraud
