summary: Major banks are urging the Australian government to allow them access to tax data to help prevent a rise in fraudulent loan applications, which have reached at least $4 billion. They argue that using AI to create fake documents is making it easier for fraudsters to exploit the system.
ticker_line: Banks push for tax data access to combat fraud
author: James Eyers
heading: Banking

title: Family of seven's home uninhabitable after Suncorp insurance delay exacerbates damage
summary: The Balzan family of seven is living in a caravan after Suncorp delayed repairs on their home, worsening damage from a toilet leak. They have been without proper accommodation since October last year and are struggling with uncertainty and stress over their insurance claim.
ticker_line: Suncorp delays worsen family's home damage
author: business Adelaide Miller
heading: General Insurance

title: GO2 Health medical clinic in Brisbane waited almost three months to alert patients it was hacked
summary: GO2 Health clinic in Brisbane took nearly three months to inform patients about a data breach caused by hackers accessing their email. Some patients' sensitive information may have been compromised, raising concerns about the clinic's handling of personal data.
ticker_line: Brisbane clinic delays patient breach notification
heading: Health Insurance

title: Westpac grills its customers
summary: Westpac is asking customers for detailed personal and financial information by August 31, or they may face banking restrictions. This is part of the bank's compliance with anti-money laundering laws, but some customers thought the requests were scams.
ticker_line: Westpac demands customer info or faces restrictions
author: Judith Kerr
heading: Banking

title: Adoption rates high but AI is yet to deliver
summary: AI adoption in Australia is high, but it is not improving productivity as expected. Experts warn that companies need to change their work habits instead of just using AI to do the same tasks faster.
ticker_line: AI fails to boost productivity in Australian firms
author: Jared Lynch
heading: AI

title: DAY OF RECKONING FOR UNIS
summary: The job market for young Australians entering the workforce in 2027 is expected to be challenging due to a business downturn in NSW and Victoria, worsened by rising costs and the impact of artificial intelligence. Universities need to adapt their teaching to prepare students for this new reality, or face significant job losses among graduates.
ticker_line: Job market struggles loom for young Australians
author: Robert Gottliebsen
heading: Economy

title: Australia must move up the AI ‘value chain’ to capture maximum benefit from the technology: Andrew Charlton
summary: Australia's Assistant Minister Andrew Charlton urges the country to enhance its role in the AI industry by moving beyond just hosting data centres. He warns that without action, Australia risks becoming a major importer of AI technology, losing out on economic benefits that could be retained domestically.
ticker_line: Australia urged to boost AI industry value
heading: AI

title: Rate rise still in play despite jobless spike
summary: Australia's unemployment rate rose to 4.5% in July, the highest in nearly five years, as 15,800 jobs were lost. Despite this increase, experts believe there may still be a chance for another interest rate rise this year as the economy shows signs of slowing down.
ticker_line: Unemployment rises, interest rate hike still possible
author: Grace Lagan
heading: Economy

title: Oz national debt passes $1 trillion
summary: Australia's national debt has surpassed $1 trillion, with projections indicating it could reach $2 trillion by 2030. This situation raises concerns about potential interest rate hikes and economic risks, especially as unemployment has also increased to 4.5%.
ticker_line: Australia's national debt exceeds $1 trillion
author: Ellen Ransley
heading: Economy

title: Medibank calls for health reform as it reports $638m full-year profits
summary: Medibank reported a 27.5% rise in profits to $638.7 million for the 2026 financial year, while calling for health reform to help reduce costs as more Australians choose lower-tier health insurance policies. The company also increased its premiums by an average of 5.1% in April to manage rising healthcare expenses.
ticker_line: Medibank profits rise, calls for health reform
author: Joseph Carbone
heading: Health Insurance

title: Medibank boss cracks open a can of worms
summary: Medibank CEO David Koczkar criticises online insurance comparison sites for increasing costs and driving up premiums, while still using some of them for sales. He argues that these aggregators should be held to the same scrutiny as other health insurance costs.
ticker_line: Medibank CEO slams insurance comparison sites
author: Anthony Macdonald
heading: Health Insurance

title: Levy changes would mean 'obscene' tax rise
summary: Kennards Self Storage could face a $2.2 million tax increase under proposed changes to NSW's emergency services funding, shifting from an insurance levy to a land tax. This change may benefit most households but significantly impact industrial and commercial landowners, with some estimates showing tax rises of up to 990%.
ticker_line: Kennards Self Storage faces massive tax hike in NSW
author: Paul Karp
heading: Regulation

title: NDIS funding cuts hit four in 10 plan reviews
summary: The federal government is cutting funding for 40% of NDIS participants after plan reviews, affecting around 18,000 people. This move is part of efforts to reduce the scheme's costs, but it has sparked criticism from disability advocates who say it harms those with significant needs.
ticker_line: NDIS funding cuts impact 40% of participants
author: Michael Read | Deputy economics edi
heading: Regulation

title: AI job disruption priced into man's compensation payout in first known case
summary: A NSW man received a $950,000 payout after a car accident, with the impact of artificial intelligence on future job prospects considered in the decision. This is the first known case where AI's role in the workforce was explicitly included in calculating compensation for reduced working capacity.
ticker_line: AI impact factored into injury compensation payout
author: national AI Cam Wilson
heading: AI

title: Professional services: KPMG begins talks with senior partners on staff cuts
summary: KPMG is in talks to cut up to 500 jobs, including senior partners, due to a whistleblower scandal. The firm faces scrutiny after allegations of mishandling confidential information, leading to lost contracts with major clients like Lendlease.
ticker_line: KPMG plans major job cuts amid scandal
author: Colin Kruger
heading: Regulation

title: ‘Doing it tough’: Diesel shock puts brakes on Super Retail sales
summary: Super Retail Group's sales fell as rising diesel prices and cost-of-living pressures kept customers at home. The company reported a 7.2% drop in annual net profit to $205.9 million, despite a boost from FIFA World Cup merchandise sales.
ticker_line: Super Retail profits drop amid rising fuel costs
author: Eli Greenblat
heading: Economy

title: Dole and pensions set to rise
summary: From September 20, over five million Australians will see an increase in social security payments, including a rise in Jobseeker and pension rates. The federal government is also updating deeming rates for financial assets used in means testing.
ticker_line: Social security payments to increase for millions
author: Ria Pandey
heading: Economy

title: ABS shows record business vehicle leasing as claims costs climb
summary: Australian businesses committed a record $978.5 million to road-vehicle leases in the September quarter, up 17.8% from the previous quarter, while vehicle values and repair bills are pushing insurance claims higher. The leasing figures measure dollars, not vehicle numbers, and insurers are increasingly looking at fleet risk records as they set prices; businesses also need to check new vehicles are properly covered under their policies.
ticker_line: Record vehicle leasing adds pressure to insurance costs
author: Matthew Sellers
heading: General Insurance

title: Media release: Cotton On pays penalties for alleged product safety reporting breaches
summary: Cotton On Australia has paid $19,800 in penalties after the ACCC issued two notices over alleged failures to report serious injuries linked to products sold by its Supre and Typo subsidiaries. The reports were required within two days of the company becoming aware of the injuries.
ticker_line: Cotton On pays $19,800 over safety reporting breaches
author: ACCC Media <do-not-reply@accc.gov.au>
heading: ACCC

title: APRA’s latest System Risk Outlook warns of rising threats to financial stability
summary: APRA says Australia’s financial system remains strong, but growing global market uncertainty, AI-related cyber and operational risks, and high household debt could make future shocks harder to manage. It will focus on ensuring banks, insurers and superannuation funds can withstand financial and operational disruptions, including crises where several pressures hit at once.
ticker_line: APRA warns rising risks could test financial stability
author: APRA web updates <subscriptions@apra.gov.au>
heading: APRA

title: ASIC sues Commonwealth Bank alleging tens of thousands of business customers overcharged fees
summary: ASIC has started civil penalty proceedings against Commonwealth Bank, alleging tens of thousands of CommBiz business customers, many of them small businesses, were charged millions of dollars in fees they had not been told about. The allegations have not been proven in court.
ticker_line: ASIC alleges CBA overcharged thousands of business customers
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Separate assets for cost-base adjustment
summary: SMSFs holding investments through a wrap account may need to separate the investments in their records to use the Division 296 cost-base adjustment. Heffron’s Lyn Formica recommends doing this in the 2026 financial statements, so the fund can record each asset’s cost base and value at 30 June 2026; some funds may need to start from 1 July 2025 to track assets and discount eligibility accurately.
ticker_line: SMSFs urged to separate wrap account assets early
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: Many still unsure about retirement target
summary: A Selfwealth by Syfe survey found 61% of Australians have not worked out how much they will need for retirement, including 47% of people aged 55 and over. People who used a calculator or adviser to set a savings target were more confident they could reach it, while many said not having enough money was stopping them from investing more.
ticker_line: Many Australians still lack a retirement savings target
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: Vero's Anthony Pagano: cash-strapped SMEs need a broker who does more than place cover
summary: Vero’s 2026 SME Insurance Index found 43% of small businesses had lower revenue over the past year, while 74% had never formally assessed their risks. Vero distribution head Anthony Pagano says brokers can help by advising on risks, staff and business continuity as well as arranging insurance; most businesses surveyed had used a broker, and 95% of heavy broker users were satisfied with how their claim was handled.
ticker_line: Vero says brokers can help SMEs manage risk
author: Daniel Wood
heading: General Insurance

title: Lithium battery fires push insurers into underwriting questions and pricing: report
summary: Australian insurers say home fire claims linked to lithium-ion batteries have almost doubled in three years, with fires often causing severe damage and losses above $500,000. The Insurance Council warns the risk may affect premiums and urges people to tell insurers about e-bikes and e-scooters, while commercial insurers are asking more about battery charging, storage and safety procedures.
ticker_line: Battery fires prompt tougher insurance questions
author: Josh Recamara
heading: General Insurance

title: Gilchrist Connell adds liability principal in Sydney as complex claims build
summary: Gilchrist Connell has appointed insurance litigator Judy Truong as a principal in its Sydney office. The firm says her experience will help it handle complex claims involving serious injuries, contracts, labour hire, insurance cover and recovery, as it continues to add senior staff.
ticker_line: Gilchrist Connell appoints Sydney liability claims principal
author: Josh Recamara
heading: General Insurance

title: ASIC forms markets expert advisory group
summary: ASIC has formed a temporary 12-member expert group to advise on practical ways to make Australia’s capital markets more resilient, accessible and competitive. The group will consider issues including investor access, funding options for small and medium businesses, market growth and the need to maintain trust amid rising cyber, AI and global risks.
ticker_line: ASIC creates expert group to strengthen capital markets
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Regulation

title: Macquarie lands new investment chief for wealth division
summary: Macquarie has appointed David Carruthers as chief investment officer of its wealth business, promoting him from head of fixed income. He will lead more than 30 investment professionals, replacing Paul Huxford, who left for New Zealand’s Fisher Funds Management this month.
ticker_line: Macquarie promotes David Carruthers to wealth investment chief
author: Matthew Wai
heading: Investments

title: ASIC Daily News round-up - 11 November 2026
summary: ASIC’s 11 November round-up covers court penalties and bans for three former Youpla Group directors, feedback on a proposed general insurance code, and a review of small business restructuring. ASIC also urged people to check their savings interest, while Macquarie admitted failures in promoting its Welcome Rate offer.
ticker_line: ASIC targets director duties and savings rate failures
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Former Youpla Group executives Jonathan Law, Michael Wilson and Geoffrey Clayton found to have breached their directors' duties
summary: The Federal Court found former Youpla Group board members Jonathan Law, Michael Wilson and Geoffrey Clayton breached their duties as directors of Youpla companies. They have been banned from managing corporations and ordered to pay penalties.
ticker_line: Former Youpla directors banned and ordered to pay penalties
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: ASIC opens consultation on code of practice
summary: ASIC is seeking public feedback by December 23 on the Insurance Council of Australia’s proposed rewrite of the General Insurance Code of Practice, lodged on October 22. The draft would make the code contractually enforceable for the first time and includes changes to claims handling, support for vulnerable customers, family violence protections and expert reports; the ICA may revise it before submitting a final version.
ticker_line: ASIC seeks feedback on proposed insurance code rewrite
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: AI agents clear the submission but the broker still holds the licence
summary: Insurance services firm Xceedance says its AI agents can make policy and submission work more efficient, and it plans to charge clients for completed tasks rather than hours worked. The firm says brokers’ licence obligations and accountability do not change: people must review and approve the work, while ASIC and APRA rules leave regulated firms responsible for outsourced services.
ticker_line: AI agents speed insurance work, but humans remain accountable
author: Daniel Wood
heading: General Insurance

title: Top insurance brokerage West Rock keeps growing as a joint venture
summary: West Rock Insurance Brokers has again been named one of Insurance Business Australia’s Top Brokerages and Fast Brokerages, a year after joining McLardy McShane Insurance Advisors as a joint venture partner. Founded by Wes Strong in 2019, the brokerage has grown to an $14 million portfolio and 11 staff, with the network providing more training and support while West Rock retains its local, client-first approach.
ticker_line: West Rock grows with McLardy McShane partnership
author: Chris Sweeney
heading: General Insurance

title: Not a profession: court strips insurer’s power to hide fraud tipster
summary: The NSW Supreme Court has ordered MLC Limited, now Acenda, to hand over unredacted communications from a confidential source who accused a claimant of working while disabled. The court found claims handling is not a profession covered by the relevant evidence privilege; the dispute over the claimant’s $400,000 total and permanent disablement benefit is still unresolved.
ticker_line: Court orders insurer to reveal confidential fraud tip-offs
author: Elaine Abasta
heading: Life Insurance

title: ASIC review highlights how small business restructuring can help businesses experiencing financial difficulty
summary: ASIC has published a review of the small business restructuring process, covering 6,606 appointments that began between 1 January 2021 and 30 June 2026. The report examines how the process has worked and the outcomes for businesses facing financial difficulty.
ticker_line: ASIC reviews five years of small business restructuring
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: ASIC warns Australians may be missing out on savings interest
summary: ASIC says Australians may be earning less interest on their savings than they expect. It is urging people to check that their bank is paying the rate they were promised.
ticker_line: ASIC urges savers to check their bank interest
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Macquarie admits failures over savings account Welcome Rate offer
summary: Macquarie Bank has admitted it failed to properly promote its Welcome Rate offer to new savings account customers. The notice does not provide details of the failures or any consequences.
ticker_line: Macquarie admits failures over savings rate offer
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Longevity risk now intensifying
summary: Challenger research says Australians may spend longer in retirement as the gap grows between leaving work and the end of life. At 65, the chance of reaching 95 is 21% for men and 28% for women; for a couple, there is a 43% chance at least one partner will reach 95, raising questions about how long retirement savings must last. Stanford researchers also argue longer lives call for more flexible paths through education, work and retirement, and say age-diverse workplaces can bring benefits.
ticker_line: Longer lives raise pressure on retirement savings
author: Darin Tyson-Chan
heading: Superannuation

title: No asset transfer shortcut
summary: Heffron’s Natasha Panagis says SMSF members cannot transfer money between accounts using only a journal entry, even if they are related. A withdrawal of cash or assets must actually occur, followed by a contribution; the same applies when paying death benefits to another member.
ticker_line: SMSF transfers need real withdrawals and contributions
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: SMSF tied to Part IVA breach
summary: The High Court ruled that Part IVA tax rules applied to the Merchant Family Trust’s sale of Billabong shares to Gordon Merchant’s SMSF, finding the main purpose was to create a capital loss and gain a tax benefit. The ruling came despite an earlier decision overturning Merchant’s disqualification as an SMSF trustee over other alleged breaches.
ticker_line: High Court finds SMSF share sale aimed at tax benefit
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: ASIC warning receives wide support
summary: The SMSF Association, ASFA and the Super Members Council have backed stronger action against harmful lead generation in financial advice, with ASFA and the council calling for an outright ban. Their comments follow an ASIC review of 15 licensed organisations, which found risks to consumers and advisers; the groups say safeguards should protect people before they lose money.
ticker_line: Super groups back ban on harmful advice leads
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: PI insurers weigh lead generation risk after ASIC letter
summary: Professional indemnity insurers have told ASIC they will consider the risks of advice businesses using lead generators to attract clients for superannuation switching. ASIC found weak supervision at some firms and warned that poor controls could put licences at risk; the review follows the collapse of Shield and First Guardian, which left about 12,000 investors with combined losses of $1 billion.
ticker_line: PI insurers weigh risks of lead-generated super advice
author: Josh Recamara
heading: Regulation

title: Life insurers seek fix to capital loss rules in tax reform bill
summary: The Council of Australian Life Insurers has asked a Senate committee to clarify that proposed tax relief on capital losses also covers life companies’ superannuation businesses, including virtual pooled superannuation trusts. Without the change, members could receive lower after-tax returns than people in standard super funds holding the same investments; the committee is due to report by November 13.
ticker_line: Life insurers seek equal tax relief for super members
author: Josh Recamara
heading: Life Insurance

title: CALI names eight women for first life insurance leadership cohort
summary: CALI has selected eight women for the first year-long ReCALIbrate leadership programme, with most working in life insurers across claims, underwriting, product, legal and customer roles; one is a financial adviser. The programme offers mentoring and leadership training, marking a shift from ReCALIbrate’s earlier focus on grants for women in advice as adviser numbers fall and the government moves ahead with plans for limited advice from life insurers and super funds.
ticker_line: CALI backs eight women in life insurance leadership
author: Josh Recamara
heading: Life Insurance

title: Future Fund names new chief
summary: The Future Fund has appointed its current chief investment officer, Richard Brandweiner, as chief executive from 1 January 2027. He will replace Raphael Arndt, who is leaving for the private sector after almost 20 years at the fund; the search for a new chief investment officer will begin in due course.
ticker_line: Future Fund names Richard Brandweiner as new chief
author: Eliza Bavin
heading: Investments

title: ASIC Daily News round-up - 10 November 2026
summary: ASIC’s second review of private credit found that many investors still lack clear information about the risks, fees and conflicts involved. The regulator said complex structures and poor disclosure continue to make these investments hard to assess.
ticker_line: ASIC says private credit investors remain in the dark
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: BizCover moves into commercial landlord cover - and brokers should take note
summary: BizCover has launched online commercial landlord insurance for owners of shops, offices and warehouses, with cover underwritten by Vero, AIG and QBE. The product allows owners to insure up to 10 properties, but brokers may retain more complex portfolios; the article warns that landlords choosing building values and other cover details themselves risk being underinsured.
ticker_line: BizCover brings commercial landlord cover online
author: Josh Recamara
heading: General Insurance

title: ASIC forms Markets Expert Advisory Group to strengthen Australia’s market resilience and competitiveness
summary: ASIC has formed a Markets Expert Advisory Group of market leaders and experts. The group will help identify and prioritise practical ways to make Australia’s capital markets more resilient, efficient, accessible and competitive.
ticker_line: ASIC forms group to strengthen Australia’s capital markets
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: No injuries, old grief: a rear-ender tests the 10% psych threshold
summary: A NSW review panel cut an Uber driver's impairment rating from 12% to 8% after a low-speed bus crash, finding he had depression but did not meet the diagnostic test for PTSD. Because his rating is now below the 10% threshold, he can still receive treatment and income support but cannot pursue lump-sum damages for pain and suffering.
ticker_line: NSW panel cuts crash impairment rating below 10%
author: Elaine Abasta
heading: General Insurance

title: APRA finalises simpler, faster, and more transparent bank licensing framework
summary: APRA has introduced a simpler bank licensing process, with clearer requirements and timeframes while keeping its prudential standards. Applicants will have up to 12 months to meet the criteria, and APRA will decide within 90 days once an application is substantially complete; the change also ends the Restricted ADI pathway.
ticker_line: APRA simplifies bank licensing and sets clearer timeframes
author: APRA web updates <subscriptions@apra.gov.au>
heading: APRA

title: Media release: ACCC warns against misleading ‘storewide’ or ‘limited time’ Black Friday sales claims
summary: The ACCC has warned retailers to ensure Black Friday claims such as “storewide” and “limited time” are accurate and not misleading. The warning was issued on 10 November 2026.
ticker_line: ACCC warns retailers over Black Friday sale claims
author: ACCC Media <do-not-reply@accc.gov.au>
heading: ACCC

title: Trust structure critical in new tax regime
summary: A proposed tax regime from 1 July 2028 could impose a minimum 30% tax on income earned by discretionary trusts, and SMSFs may lose some of the tax offsets if they invest through a unit trust that is not fixed. DBA Lawyers’ Fraser Stead says SMSFs should check whether their unit trust meets the new fixed-trust rules or have its terms changed, as pension and accumulation arrangements can affect how much tax is wasted.
ticker_line: SMSFs urged to check unit trusts under proposed tax rules
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: ASIC halts two private credit funds over PDS, Bathla disclosure concerns
summary: ASIC has temporarily stopped Angas Securities from offering or selling interests in its Angas Prime Income Fund and Angas Direct Mortgage Fund, citing concerns that investors were not properly told about the firm’s financial position and the risks involved. ASIC is also concerned about the Prime Income Fund’s exposure to collapsed property developer Bathla Group, and will consider final stop orders after hearing from Angas.
ticker_line: ASIC halts two Angas funds over disclosure concerns
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Regulation

title: ASIC issues serious and final warning on lead generation
summary: ASIC warned financial advice firms they could lose their licences if they fail to properly oversee lead generators, some of which went beyond marketing and carried out tasks requiring authorisation. The review found lead generators brought in 7,639 clients and were linked to more than $678 million in investments or super switches; ASIC cited weak oversight and potentially misleading sales tactics, while the Super Members Council called for an outright ban.
ticker_line: ASIC warns advice firms over lead generator oversight
author: Vinny Vucago
heading: Regulation

title: AI moves beyond pilot phase for Aussie businesses: Deloitte
summary: Deloitte says Australian businesses are moving beyond AI trials, with 39% redesigning several key processes around AI and 73% expecting it to handle most routine knowledge work within three years. AI is speeding up decisions, but deep business transformation remains uncommon, and some organisations still lack clear accountability when AI causes harm.
ticker_line: Australian businesses redesign work around AI
author: Karren Vergara
heading: AI

title: APRA deputy chair defends super board tenure limits
summary: APRA deputy chair David Bradbury defended a proposed 12-year default tenure limit for non-executive directors on super fund boards, saying regular renewal brings fresh perspectives and helps boards manage growing risks. APRA is consulting on changes to its governance standard, with the final version expected by the end of 2026.
ticker_line: APRA defends proposed 12-year super board limit
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Superannuation

title: Healthcare liability bucks soft market with rises of up to 40%
summary: Australian healthcare professional liability premiums are rising despite falling insurance rates elsewhere, with loss-free buyers facing increases of up to 40% on excess cover and buyers with claims facing larger rises. Lockton says higher claims costs, longer-running cases and tighter insurer capacity are driving the increases, while stronger risk controls and clear claims data may help at renewal.
ticker_line: Healthcare liability premiums rise by up to 40%
author: Rod Bolivar
heading: General Insurance

title: Update from the Treasury
summary: The Treasury issued an update announcing a speech to the United States Studies Centre on 9 November 2026. The alert does not include the speech or details of what was discussed.
ticker_line: Treasury announces speech to US Studies Centre
author: The Treasury <noreply@treasury.gov.au>
heading: Treasury

title: ASIC Daily News round-up - 9 November 2026
summary: ASIC’s 9 November round-up says Dat Dean Nguyen is the first person charged with failing to obey an ASIC order to return company property to a liquidator. ASIC also issued interim stop orders on two Angas Securities funds over concerns about disclosures on the company’s financial position and one fund’s exposure to the Bathla Group, and warned financial advice licensees that using unlicensed or unqualified lead generators could put their licences at risk.
ticker_line: ASIC targets fund disclosures and advice lead generators
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Queenslander Dat Dean Nguyen first person charged with failing to comply with an ASIC order for the return of company property
summary: Dat Dean Nguyen, of Logan, Queensland, appeared in Beenleigh Magistrates’ Court on 6 November 2026, charged with failing to follow an ASIC order to return a vehicle to a company’s liquidator. ASIC says he is the first person charged with failing to comply with this type of order.
ticker_line: Queenslander charged over ASIC vehicle return order
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Australians in dark on true scale of flood risk
summary: A Youi survey of more than 1,200 recent home insurance buyers found many Australians underestimate flood risk: only 8% knew more than 2 million homes face some risk, while 53% thought fewer than 1 million were exposed. Most people who believe their homes are not at risk are unwilling or unsure about paying higher premiums to help make cover more affordable, but respondents backed limiting development in flood-prone areas and building defences.
ticker_line: Survey finds Australians underestimate flood risk
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: Cyclone pool helping but is no cure-all, MPs hear
summary: Australia’s cyclone reinsurance pool has helped lower average home insurance premiums in medium- and high-risk areas by 17% to 37% since October 2022, while the chance of getting a quote has also improved. But many people still lack cover, especially for contents, and the Insurance Council says the pool must be backed by measures such as stronger building standards, retrofitting and flood defences.
ticker_line: Cyclone pool cuts premiums, but cover gaps remain
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: ICA and state recovery agency strengthen ties
summary: The Insurance Council of Australia and the NSW Reconstruction Authority have signed an agreement to improve how they share information and plan for disasters. It will also help insurers work with recovery centres and communities, as insurers have received more than $4.79 billion in NSW extreme-weather claims since 2022.
ticker_line: Insurers and NSW agency strengthen disaster recovery ties
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: Court rejects exclusion to uphold disability claim
summary: The Queensland Court of Appeal has rejected AIA’s appeal over its refusal to pay chef Luke Kelly-Stevens’ total and permanent disability claim. The court found his failure to meet the policy’s requirement to work at least 15 hours a week for three months did not cause his disabling injuries, so the Insurance Contracts Act could prevent AIA relying on that exclusion to deny the claim.
ticker_line: Court rejects AIA’s hours-worked exclusion
author: Insurance News
heading: Life Insurance

title: ICA conference weighs the ‘existential challenge’
summary: The Insurance Council of Australia is calling for much greater investment in flood protection, saying the $1 billion Disaster Ready Fund is far short of what is needed as insurance becomes less affordable and harder to obtain. Insurers also pointed to rising repair and rebuilding costs, regulatory costs and the risks and opportunities of AI, while the government continues talks on how to address disaster insurance affordability without removing price signals.
ticker_line: Insurers call for major boost to flood protection
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: ASIC issues interim stop orders against two Angas Securities funds over PDS and Bathla disclosure concerns
summary: ASIC has temporarily stopped Angas Securities from offering interests in two managed investment schemes. It is concerned their product disclosure statements do not adequately explain Angas Securities’ financial position, and that one fund’s exposure to the Bathla Group is not properly disclosed.
ticker_line: ASIC halts two Angas funds over disclosure concerns
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: ASIC’s final warning to licensees – using lead generators may put your licence at risk
summary: ASIC says its review found unlicensed or unqualified lead generators involved in financial advice, raising concerns about how licensees supervise them. The regulator has warned licensees that using lead generators could put their licences at risk.
ticker_line: ASIC warns lead generators could put licences at risk
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Brokers see bigger BI gap than power clients over equipment waits
summary: An FM survey found 73% of brokers believe business interruption cover falls short of the time needed to recover from equipment failures, compared with 59% of power companies. Replacement equipment can take years to arrive, while common Australian policies cover only 12 to 24 months, prompting calls to review cover and recovery plans.
ticker_line: Equipment delays expose gaps in power insurance cover
author: https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/au/authors/rod-bolivar/
heading: General Insurance

title: Insurers price ADAS on fitment, but drivers keep switching it off
summary: A RACQ survey found 35% of Queensland drivers have switched off lane departure warnings, while national IAG research found 60% of drivers turn off at least some driver-assistance features. The systems could prevent an estimated 7,850 Australian road deaths and hospitalisations a year if used fully, but insurers also face higher repair costs as sensors and cameras make even minor crashes more expensive.
ticker_line: Drivers switch off safety features despite crash benefits
author: https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/au/authors/rod-bolivar/
heading: General Insurance

title: Direct insurer Achmea signs Ausveg deal in broker-heavy farm market
summary: Achmea Farm Insurance has partnered with Ausveg to share practical risk-management advice, events and international farming knowledge with Australian vegetable growers, building on a similar deal with Protected Cropping Australia. The direct insurer says the partnerships aim to help growers manage risks and keep their businesses resilient, as vegetable production faces pressure and many growers consider leaving the industry.
ticker_line: Achmea partners with Ausveg to support growers
author: https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/au/authors/rod-bolivar/
heading: General Insurance

title: Funeral fund founder doubled premiums to his own offshore insurer - now he's banned for 15 years
summary: The Federal Court fined the founder of three Australian funeral funds $250,000 and banned him from managing companies for 15 years after he admitted failing to manage conflicts of interest. He directed one fund to double premiums paid to his Vanuatu-based insurer, worsening its finances; all three funds later went into liquidation, putting members’ funeral cover and cancellation payments at risk.
ticker_line: Funeral fund founder banned for 15 years
author: Elaine Abasta
heading: Life Insurance

title: Wikramanayake exits Macquarie, APRA slams 'serious' governance failure
summary: APRA has imposed a new $100 million capital buffer on Macquarie Bank after finding it had held too little capital for its non-bank business since 2019, calling the issue a serious failure of governance and oversight. The action comes as chief executive Shemara Wikramanayake leaves after nearly 40 years at Macquarie, with Greg Ward taking over on November 7; APRA will assess the bank’s capital calculations and may take further action.
ticker_line: APRA adds $100 million buffer after Macquarie breach
author: Karren Vergara
heading: Regulation

title: ASIC Daily News round-up - 6 November 2026
summary: ASIC’s 6 November round-up says the Federal Court ordered lender Sunshine Loans to pay $5.5 million for charging thousands of customers a fee banned under the National Credit Code. ASIC also sought feedback on guidance and relief for a new foreign financial services provider regime starting 8 April 2027, and Commissioner Alan Kirkland spoke about trust and basic standards in insurance.
ticker_line: Sunshine Loans fined $5.5 million over illegal fees
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Minister vows to move with caution on price transparency
summary: Financial Services Minister Daniel Mulino says the Government will carefully consult on making home and contents insurance premiums clearer, aiming to help people understand price rises and encourage steps to reduce risk without limiting innovation. Treasury is also examining affordability for people in high-risk areas, using detailed industry data while seeking to retain price signals and support resilience.
ticker_line: Mulino promises careful approach to insurance price transparency
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: Sunshine Loans ordered to pay $5.5 million penalty for charging customers illegal fees
summary: The Federal Court has ordered Sunshine Loans to pay $5.5 million in penalties for charging thousands of customers a fee banned under the National Credit Code. The lender provides small loans.
ticker_line: Sunshine Loans fined $5.5 million over illegal fees
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Why chasing premium in a soft market comes back to bite
summary: Pacific commercial insurance rates fell 12% in the third quarter of 2026, marking 11 straight quarters of declines, with property rates down 14%. New Sydney agency Antipodean Underwriting founder Jaydon Burke-Douglas says growth must come from careful risk selection and strong local service, not simply chasing more business or lower prices.
ticker_line: Antipodean targets careful growth as insurance rates fall
author: Daniel Wood
heading: General Insurance

title: The insurtech founder turned broker who defied the comparison screen
summary: After more than 15 years building insurance technology, Ben Webster has become a commercial broker and says small businesses’ insurance needs cannot be handled by a simple online comparison screen: insurers classify businesses differently and ask different questions, leaving brokers to do time-consuming work. His new brokerage, Pocket, aims to help founders and small businesses earlier, as many lack risk plans and falling insurance rates mean brokers must do more work for less premium.
ticker_line: Former insurtech founder takes on small business broking
author: Daniel Wood
heading: General Insurance

title: Australian firms give AI power without full oversight
summary: Four in five Australian organisations now let AI make decisions or take actions that previously needed human approval, but only 55% can see and audit every action. Illumio’s survey found 73% had faced an AI-related security issue or warning sign in the past year, prompting warnings from the Australian Signals Directorate to restrict AI access, keep audit records and require human oversight for high-impact actions.
ticker_line: Australian firms give AI power without full oversight
author: Jonalyn Cueto
heading: Regulation

title: HIF grows faster than the market but profit falls sharply as new CEO rebuilds team
summary: Not-for-profit HIF grew its health insurance membership by 4.3% in 2025-26, ahead of the industry’s 2.1% growth, and paid more than $155 million in claims, but its profit fell to $5.9 million from $14.7 million. Under new chief executive Greg Morris, HIF has reshaped its leadership team and plans further investment, while warning that affordability pressures and a proposed change to the over-65s rebate could weigh on growth.
ticker_line: HIF membership grows as profit falls sharply
author: Jonalyn Cueto
heading: Health Insurance

title: APRA publishes Deputy Chair David Brabury's remarks to the 2026 ACTU Superannuation Forum
summary: APRA Deputy Chair David Bradbury told the 2026 ACTU Superannuation Forum that super fund trustees need stronger governance, resilience and skills to protect members as risks grow more complex. He warned that cyber incidents, long disruptions or governance failures could cost far more than the safeguards needed to prevent them.
ticker_line: APRA urges super funds to strengthen safeguards
author: APRA web updates <subscriptions@apra.gov.au>
heading: APRA

title: APRA publishes Member Suzanne Smith’s remarks to 2026 ICA conference
summary: APRA has published remarks by Member Suzanne Smith to the Insurance Council of Australia’s 2026 conference in Sydney. She said technology and AI will change how insurers assess and manage risk, but strong governance, resilience and organisational capability are needed to build trust and deliver for policyholders.
ticker_line: APRA says strong institutions will shape insurers’ future
author: APRA web updates <subscriptions@apra.gov.au>
heading: APRA

title: APRA takes action on breach of NOHC authority condition by Macquarie Group
summary: APRA found Macquarie Group had understated the capital needed for risks in its non-bank businesses since 2019, due to a failure in its governance and checks. Macquarie has corrected the shortfall and added a $100 million capital buffer; APRA will oversee a full review and may take further action, while an existing $500 million buffer for Macquarie Bank remains in place.
ticker_line: APRA orders review after Macquarie capital breach
author: APRA web updates <subscriptions@apra.gov.au>
heading: APRA

title: Bushfire risk clusters in NSW as El Niño summer approaches
summary: GIO data puts eight NSW postcodes among Australia’s 10 most bushfire-prone, as a strengthening El Niño raises the prospect of a hot, dry summer and higher fire danger. Home insurance costs in high-risk areas have risen sharply, while a federal scheme can cut premiums for some homeowners who document bushfire protection work; commercial and strata properties have no equivalent scheme.
ticker_line: NSW dominates top bushfire-risk postcode rankings
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: NSW workers comp providers face orders over billing failures
summary: NSW’s insurance regulator has ordered six workplace rehabilitation providers to supply invoicing data and I-MED New South Wales to provide invoices and reimbursement evidence for MRI services, after finding billing failures. The directions run until 2027 and aim to improve oversight of scheme costs; brokers are advised to check providers’ regulatory status and whether billing delays have affected clients’ claims.
ticker_line: SIRA orders seven providers over billing failures
author: Roxanne Libatique
heading: General Insurance

title: Rising claims costs hit corporate health renewals as HCF profit halves
summary: HCF’s 2025–26 profit more than halved to $87.8 million as claims costs rose faster than insurance revenue, highlighting pressure on health insurers and corporate health plan renewals. Employers face rising medical plan costs, while consumers are increasingly weighing affordable cover against the level of benefits.
ticker_line: HCF profit halves as health claims costs surge
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: Health Insurance

title: RAC’s profit surge hands IAG a richer prize, if the ACCC will let it through
summary: RAC Insurance lifted its 2026 pre-tax insurance profit 45% to $420.2 million, making its proposed $1.35 billion sale to IAG more valuable but also strengthening the ACCC’s view that RAC can compete on its own. IAG has offered to transfer its NRMA insurance renewals in WA to win approval; the ACCC is considering the public benefits case and is expected to decide by early February 2027.
ticker_line: RAC profit surge sharpens IAG deal’s competition test
author: Matthew Sellers
heading: General Insurance

title: SMSF registration feedback sought
summary: The SMSF Association is asking members who helped clients register a new self-managed super fund with the ATO in the past 12 months to share their experiences by 13 November. The feedback will help identify what works and where registrations run into delays or other problems, and may inform the association’s advocacy as the government considers changes including compulsory education for new trustees.
ticker_line: SMSF Association seeks feedback on ATO registrations
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: Super growth outpaces property
summary: Superannuation grew 5.2% in the June quarter of 2026, adding $231 billion to household wealth, while residential property values fell 0.3%, losing $34 billion. SuperConcepts says super is increasingly growing independently of housing, but warns a forecast 10.6% fall in capital city property prices could cut about $1.2 trillion from household wealth; from 10 August 2026, SMSFs will also be barred from taking on new borrowing to buy residential property.
ticker_line: Super growth outpaces falling property values
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: AustralianSuper scores Moody's top credit rating
summary: AustralianSuper has become the first Australian super fund to receive Moody’s highest long-term credit rating, AAA, with a stable outlook. Moody’s cited the fund’s size and Australia’s compulsory super system, while noting competitive pressures and the need to improve advice access and retirement options for members.
ticker_line: AustralianSuper earns Moody’s highest credit rating
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Superannuation

title: MUFG expands InvestStream partnership with minority stake
summary: MUFG Retirement Solutions has taken a minority stake in InvestStream, expanding a partnership launched in July to help super funds offer members personalised digital advice, guidance and education. Their services will combine InvestStream’s SuperAnne platform with MUFG’s administration expertise, with the first client rollout targeted for early 2027.
ticker_line: MUFG takes minority stake in super tech partner
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Superannuation

title: Two in three homeowners unwilling to subsidise flood-prone premiums
summary: A Youi survey of 1,222 Australian homeowners found that 66% of those who do not think their home is flood-prone are unwilling or unsure about paying higher premiums to help reduce costs for flood-affected households; most willing to contribute would pay less than $300 a year. Respondents favoured limiting development in flood-risk areas, while insurance groups say better planning and flood mitigation are needed as premiums rise and many high-risk homes lack flood cover.
ticker_line: Homeowners resist sharing flood insurance costs
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: ICA chair calls on stakeholders to ‘lock in behind’ new code
summary: Insurance Council of Australia chair Steve Johnston urged the industry and other stakeholders to support a new insurance code, now submitted to ASIC for review and consultation. He also called for clearer explanations of home insurance premiums and more investment in resilience projects such as levees and stormwater systems to help address rising risks and affordability pressures.
ticker_line: ICA chair urges support for new insurance code
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: Three weeks off, one technicality: how a chef's hand injury nearly killed his TPD claim
summary: The Queensland Court of Appeal has upheld a chef’s total and permanent disability claim after AIA Australia rejected it because a hand injury meant he did not meet the policy’s 15-hour weekly work threshold in the three months before a disabling back condition. The court found the work-hours gap was unrelated to his back injury and could not be used to deny the claim under section 54 of the Insurance Contracts Act; costs will be decided separately.
ticker_line: Court rejects AIA’s technicality in chef’s TPD claim
author: Elaine Abasta
heading: Life Insurance

title: Media release: ACCC issues Linfox Armaguard with interim direction to support ongoing access to cash
summary: The ACCC has ordered Linfox Armaguard to keep providing cash transport services and access to its facilities for existing customers and a small group of new customers across Australia. The interim direction sets service terms but does not replace current contracts, and customers can negotiate different agreements.
ticker_line: ACCC directs Armaguard to maintain cash services
author: ACCC Media <do-not-reply@accc.gov.au>
heading: ACCC

title: Is this Australia's worst insurance product?
summary: CHOICE has given Petcover’s Economy pet insurance a 2026 Shonky Award, arguing that annual policy resets can leave pets without cover for conditions they developed while insured, and that broad exclusions may also rule out unrelated illnesses with similar symptoms. Petcover disputes CHOICE’s description and says the policy is designed for older pets, but the dispute has raised concerns about how renewals, exclusions and age-based payouts work.
ticker_line: CHOICE criticises Petcover’s Economy pet insurance
author: Matthew Sellers
heading: General Insurance

title: Early storm season claims hit western Sydney as brokers brace for repeat
summary: Severe storms caused property damage across western Sydney on November 3–4, with Blacktown SES receiving more than 50 calls, as eastern Australia’s storm season begins. The article says brokers should check clients’ rebuild costs, excesses and policy cover, with recent extreme weather losses highlighting the risk of rising claims.
ticker_line: Western Sydney storms put broker readiness in focus
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: Data breaches hit record scale as cyber cover gap persists
summary: Australia’s privacy regulator received 667 data breach reports in the first half of 2026, with more incidents affecting hundreds of thousands or even millions of people. Health providers reported the most breaches, while cyber insurance remains uncommon: it accounts for less than 0.2% of industry premiums, despite rising risks from suppliers and tougher privacy penalties.
ticker_line: Large data breaches rise as cyber cover remains scarce
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: Men’s therapy dropout rate linked to mental health claims surge
summary: Bupa and Movember are training clinicians to better engage men in therapy, after research found 45% of Australian men leave treatment early. The article links poor treatment follow-through with rising insurance and workers’ compensation costs: mental health claims paid by life insurers topped $2.2 billion in 2024, while psychological injury claims often mean longer absences and higher costs.
ticker_line: Bupa and Movember target men’s therapy dropout
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: Life Insurance

title: Clearlake's founders cap a five-year rise with $82.5m Rose Bay home
summary: Clearlake Insurance Brokers founders John Angelis and Yianni Gourlas have grown the business from a network member into a stand-alone broker with more than $300 million in annual premiums, helped by acquisitions. The five-year-old firm is exploring a minority investment from private equity to fund further growth, while the founders have settled on an $82.5 million Rose Bay home.
ticker_line: Clearlake founders weigh private equity as broker grows
author: Stephen Owens
heading: General Insurance

title: Reporting Div 296 earnings favourable
summary: SMSF trustees should report Division 296 earnings in their annual returns for members known to be affected, Cooper Partners director Jemma Sanderson says, in line with the ATO’s expectation. Reporting the figures upfront could avoid extra paperwork, including getting an actuarial certificate later and amending the return; software providers are expected to help automate the process.
ticker_line: Trustees urged to report Division 296 earnings upfront
author: Darin Tyson-Chan
heading: Superannuation

title: ACR feedback a necessity
summary: The SMSF Association has asked the ANAO to recommend clearer feedback from the ATO to auditors who lodge reports about breaches in self-managed super funds, including information on what action followed. It also wants the ATO to review reporting thresholds, which have not changed since 2013 and 2011, saying many reports concern administrative errors rather than serious risks.
ticker_line: SMSF body seeks clearer ATO feedback and updated thresholds
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: Property income still a core focus
summary: DBA Lawyers principal Dan Butler says the ATO is likely to keep checking rental income and deductions reported by self-managed super funds, given the large share of fund assets linked to property. He warned that funds must report gross rental income correctly and keep evidence for decisions such as whether building work is a repair or an improvement, although taxpayers remain responsible for their claims.
ticker_line: ATO scrutiny stays focused on SMSF property income
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: IFPA launches AI technical facility
summary: The Institute of Financial Professionals Australia has launched Thomas, an AI tool that helps members find answers to tax and superannuation questions, including about SMSFs. It provides links to sources for checking answers, lets users choose where it searches and removes identifying details from client documents before upload; IFPA says it supports, rather than replaces, professional judgement.
ticker_line: IFPA launches AI tool for tax and super questions
author: Jason Spits
heading: AI

title: QBE's Houghton exits ICA board as Groves takes her seat
summary: Sue Houghton left the Insurance Council of Australia board on 31 October, and Jonathan Groves joined on 1 November as he takes over as QBE Australia Pacific chief executive. The change keeps QBE represented on the industry body, which works on issues including insurance affordability, disaster resilience and industry rules; Houghton remains with QBE until the end of December.
ticker_line: Groves replaces Houghton on ICA board for QBE
author: Stephen Owens
heading: General Insurance

title: RBA delivers another hike in split decision
summary: The RBA raised the cash rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.85%, but the decision was split six votes to three, with some board members concerned about the impact on growth, housing and jobs. Economists disagree on what comes next: Commonwealth Bank expects rates to stay on hold for now, while Betashares says another rise in February 2027 remains possible as the RBA tries to curb inflation.
ticker_line: RBA lifts cash rate to 4.85% in split vote
author: Eliza Bavin
heading: Economy

title: ART gathers govt, business leaders to close super gap
summary: Australian Retirement Trust has brought together Queensland government, business and community leaders to discuss practical ways to narrow the gender super gap. Women retire with average super balances about 23% lower than men at age 60, or around $50,000 less, with career breaks, caring duties and lower earnings among the factors contributing to the difference.
ticker_line: ART brings leaders together to tackle gender super gap
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Superannuation

title: Bushfire claims surged 20-fold at major Victorian insurer
summary: RACV Insurance says bushfire-related claims rose 20-fold year on year, with last summer’s fires making up more than 80% of its bushfire claims over the past five years. With parts of Victoria facing higher fire risk and insurers potentially restricting new cover as summer approaches, households and businesses are being urged to review their insurance early; many bushfire-exposed commercial risks are already difficult to insure fully.
ticker_line: RACV bushfire claims surge as summer risks rise
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: Cyber costs surge as Australian businesses lag on crisis readiness
summary: Australian businesses face rising cyber costs, but many are not ready to manage and recover from major attacks. At a Sydney event hosted by QBE and CYGNVS, leaders highlighted that although 99% of organisations surveyed had a cyber resilience strategy, only 20% had formally documented and tested it; the average reported cost of cybercrime reached $80,850 per incident.
ticker_line: Cyber costs rise as businesses leave plans untested
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: ASIC Daily News round-up - 4 November 2026
summary: ASIC has issued infringement notices to 22 large private companies over alleged failures to lodge financial reports. The notices total more than $4.3 million and are part of ASIC’s ongoing checks on reporting compliance.
ticker_line: ASIC issues $4.3 million in notices to 22 companies
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Three legal teams, one insurer, no deal: WA court's silica ruling
summary: The Supreme Court of Western Australia refused Vero insurer AAI Limited’s request to use separate legal teams for three employers in a worker’s silica exposure case, finding that insurer disputes should be resolved outside the worker’s claim. The worker alleges exposure across 11 employers and has serious health problems; mediation is scheduled for the following week, with a trial provisionally set for April and May 2027 if the case does not settle.
ticker_line: WA court rejects insurer’s bid for separate legal teams
author: Elaine Abasta
heading: General Insurance

title: ASIC issues over $4.3 million in infringement notices to 22 companies for alleged failure to lodge financial reports
summary: ASIC has issued infringement notices totalling more than $4.3 million to 22 large private companies over alleged late lodgement of their audited financial reports for the 2025 financial year. The allegations have not been established.
ticker_line: ASIC fines 22 companies over late financial reports
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: East coast storm losses reach $1.62 billion in final estimate
summary: PERILS has finalised insured losses from east coast storms in October and November 2025 at $1.62 billion, 8% above its previous estimate. Queensland accounted for 94% of the losses, with property damage making up 87% of the total.
ticker_line: East coast storm losses finalised at $1.62 billion
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: Airline data breaches trace back to single vendor failure
summary: Breaches at booking technology providers Amadeus and RMS Cloud exposed customer information and booking details at airlines and Australian holiday parks, highlighting how attacks on one supplier can affect many businesses. An ESET survey found 27% of organisations hit by a major cyber incident in the past year traced it to a supplier, while insurers are increasingly checking controls such as multi-factor authentication and whether policies cover losses caused by vendors.
ticker_line: Supplier breaches expose gaps in Australian cyber cover
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: SA road fatalities surpass annual ceiling before October
summary: South Australia recorded 84 road deaths and 681 serious injuries in the first nine months of 2026, already exceeding the state’s full-year targets of 70 deaths and 591 injuries; the death toll reached 88 by late October. Cyclists and motorcyclists were among the hardest hit, while the RAA called for safety upgrades on major highways including the Sturt and Augusta.
ticker_line: SA road deaths exceed annual target before October
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: Payday Super teething issues recognised
summary: The ATO says about 40,000 employer super contributions were returned in July because SMSFs did not have an active electronic service address (ESA) set up to receive contributions. Trustees should keep their ESA subscription and bank details current, check payments arrive, and lodge annual returns on time, as a return more than two weeks late can affect the fund’s status and make it harder for employers to contribute.
ticker_line: ATO flags SMSF errors as Payday Super begins
author: Darin Tyson-Chan
heading: Superannuation

title: Trustee education should avoid ATO modules
summary: The SMSF Association has urged the government not to rely solely on the ATO’s existing education modules for proposed training of people setting up self-managed super funds, saying the modules focus on correcting non-compliance rather than helping people decide if an SMSF suits them. It says education should come early, cover basic roles and responsibilities, and take less than the three hours Treasury has suggested.
ticker_line: SMSF body questions ATO role in trustee education
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: Documents key to LRBA grandfathering
summary: Documents will be important for super funds seeking to keep older residential property borrowing arrangements under grandfathering rules, DBA Lawyers principal Dan Butler says. A binding purchase contract in place before 10 August is a key starting point, while evidence such as a bare trust, loan approval or discussions with a lender may also help, particularly for off-the-plan properties.
ticker_line: Pre-change contracts key to LRBA grandfathering
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: SMC again supports no super changes
summary: The Super Members Council has backed Liberal MP Garth Hamilton’s call for no changes to how super is invested, taxed or accessed, saying it should be kept for retirement. Hamilton’s position differs from a previous Coalition proposal to let first-home buyers use some super for a home; SMC cited research showing 89 per cent of seniors want super saved for retirement.
ticker_line: SMC backs Hamilton’s call to leave super unchanged
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: Macquarie AM launches venture growth fund
summary: Macquarie Asset Management and Wellington Management have launched an Australian fund giving wholesale investors access to late-stage private companies before they list on a stock exchange. It requires a minimum $25,000 investment, targets net returns of 13–15% a year and allows quarterly withdrawals from 1 January 2030, subject to available cash.
ticker_line: Macquarie and Wellington launch private growth fund
author: Matthew Wai
heading: Investments

title: Consistent climate disclosures matter: ASFA, ACSI
summary: ASFA, ACSI and four other investment groups are urging Australia to maintain clear, consistent and comparable climate reporting, saying it helps financial institutions assess risks, spot opportunities and make investment decisions. They say mandatory reporting is already improving the information available, and a credible, proportionate framework will support better decisions and Australians’ long-term retirement outcomes.
ticker_line: Investment groups back consistent climate disclosures
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Superannuation

title: Update from the Treasury
summary: The Treasury has published its Commonwealth Climate Disclosure for 2025–26. The alert provides no further details about the report’s findings.
ticker_line: Treasury publishes 2025–26 climate disclosure
author: The Treasury <noreply@treasury.gov.au>
heading: Treasury

title: ASIC Daily News round-up - 3 November 2026
summary: The Federal Court upheld key findings, penalties and a disqualification order challenged by iSignthis Ltd, now called Southern Cross Payments Ltd, and its former director and CEO Nickolas John Karantzis. The case includes $11 million in penalties.
ticker_line: Court upholds $11 million in iSignthis penalties
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Parliamentary inquiry puts SME cyber insurance gap under scrutiny
summary: Marsh cyber chief Brylee Jaghbir told a federal inquiry that cyber insurance is affordable for small businesses, despite only 3.7% of surveyed Australians holding a policy in 2025. The inquiry also heard that cybercrime costs are rising and that access can be limited by insurance exclusions and security requirements; its final report is due by March 31, 2027.
ticker_line: Inquiry examines small business cyber insurance gap
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: Federal Court upholds $11 million in penalties and disqualification against iSignthis and former director and CEO Nickolas John Karantzis
summary: The Full Federal Court upheld $11 million in penalties and a director disqualification involving iSignthis, now Southern Cross Payments, and its former CEO Nickolas John Karantzis. ASIC said it successfully defended the key findings and penalties challenged by the company and Karantzis.
ticker_line: Court upholds $11 million penalties against iSignthis
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Inquiry finds late information requests drove avoidable TPD claims delays
summary: A Life Code Compliance Committee review found insurers should have requested information earlier in 42 of 67 TPD claims and 45 of 116 income protection claims, contributing to avoidable delays. The findings add to pressure on life insurers to improve claims handling, as regulators review the sector and the committee calls for earlier, coordinated information requests and checks for customers who may have been disadvantaged.
ticker_line: Inquiry finds late requests delayed life insurance claims
author: https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/au/authors/roxanne-sanjose/
heading: Life Insurance

title: Brokers gain new capacity as Munich Re Specialty enters Australia
summary: Munich Re Specialty began writing primary insurance in Australia on November 2, 2026, giving brokers another option for mid-sized commercial clients across property, construction and engineering, mining, and surety. The Sydney-based team has local underwriting authority and is led by Chris Mackinnon, as insurers compete for business in a market with growing capacity.
ticker_line: Munich Re Specialty launches Australian insurance operation
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: EML Group finalises 80% stake in Guild Insurance
summary: EML Group has completed its purchase of an 80% stake in Guild Insurance, with the Pharmacy Guild of Australia retaining 20%. EML will manage Guild’s workers compensation business, while Guild continues as a standalone general insurer under its existing management; the companies say the deal creates a national workers compensation offering.
ticker_line: EML completes 80% purchase of Guild Insurance
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: Vendor cyber risk in focus as Amadeus breach hits airlines globally
summary: A breach of travel technology provider Amadeus exposed booking details belonging to customers of Qantas, Cathay Pacific, Japan Airlines and Malaysia Airlines, although the airlines said their own systems were not compromised and no payment data was involved. The incident highlights uncertainty over whether cyber insurance covers breaches at suppliers, especially when access goes undetected for years.
ticker_line: Amadeus breach puts airline vendor cyber cover under scrutiny
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: Classic car insurer joins industry push to share fraud intelligence
summary: Enthusiast Motor Insurance will share claims data with the Insurance Council of Australia’s fraud detection system, which compares information across insurers to spot suspicious patterns. The move aims to help tackle organised insurance fraud and limit costs passed on to honest customers, though claims may involve extra checks.
ticker_line: Enthusiast joins national insurance fraud data network
author: https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/au/authors/roxanne-sanjose/
heading: General Insurance

title: Auditor review process inconsistent, unclear
summary: Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, CPA Australia and the Institute of Public Accountants have urged the ATO to make its reviews of SMSF auditors clearer, more consistent and faster. They want defined review steps and timeframes, better communication and public reporting, and say the ATO should not impose its own strict interpretations of auditing standards that rely on professional judgment.
ticker_line: Accounting bodies seek clearer ATO auditor reviews
heading: Superannuation

title: ATO raids dentist over early access
summary: The ATO, with help from the Australian Federal Police, searched a Melbourne dental practice linked to a former health practitioner accused of helping lodge 1,178 false applications for early super access, releasing more than $36.4 million. The investigation is ongoing; since 1 July 2025, the ATO has reviewed or audited more than 160 suspected cases and imposed penalties of over $1.5 million.
ticker_line: ATO searches dental practice over $36.4m super scheme
heading: Superannuation

title: ASIC issues 'wake-up call' to trustees on member complaints
summary: ASIC has warned super funds to do more to spot wider problems through member complaints, after finding that five of 10 funds it reviewed identified no systemic issues between January 2024 and June 2025. The regulator said AFCA identified systemic issues at almost twice the rate of trustees and warned it may take regulatory action if funds fail to fix weaknesses that put members at risk.
ticker_line: ASIC warns super funds to act on member complaints
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Superannuation

title: Aware Super expands Challenger partnership for lifetime income solution
summary: Aware Super has agreed to work with annuity provider Challenger to develop a lifetime income product for its more than 1.3 million members, giving retirees the option of income designed to last for life while keeping flexibility over their savings. The $250 billion fund says the product will add to its retirement options and support its obligations under the federal Retirement Income Covenant.
ticker_line: Aware Super and Challenger plan lifetime income product
author: Vinny Vucago
heading: Superannuation

title: ASIC Daily News round-up - 2 November 2026
summary: The CDPP has discontinued its case against Clive Palmer over allegations he helped Palmer Leisure Coolum breach takeover laws in 2012. ASIC also urged super fund trustees to improve their oversight of member complaints after a review found weaknesses that could expose Australians to avoidable harm.
ticker_line: ASIC flags super complaint gaps as Palmer case ends
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Australia a ‘standout’ for climate threat to insurers
summary: Moody’s says Australia is especially exposed to rising climate-related insurance losses because insurers cover a large share of weather damage, while floods, hail and bushfires are becoming more severe and costly. Strong capital, higher premiums and reinsurance help insurers manage the risk, and APRA’s revised rules taking effect on January 1 will make it easier for general insurers to use catastrophe bonds and other reinsurance options.
ticker_line: Moody’s flags rising climate risks for Australian insurers
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: Tax-free ACT takes top spot in duty ranking
summary: The ACT ranked first for the lowest insurance duties in the Business Council of Australia’s annual business-cost report because it charges no insurance duty. South Australia has the highest rates at 11%, while Victoria is cutting duty on non-motor business insurance by one percentage point a year until it is abolished in 2033; Queensland has the lowest workers’ compensation premiums.
ticker_line: ACT tops insurance duty ranking with no tax
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: Industry calls on Queensland to strengthen planning reforms
summary: The Insurance Council of Australia has urged Queensland to strengthen its draft planning policy, calling for clearer rules on acceptable risk, regular reviews and accountability for planning decisions. It also wants climate risks across all hazards considered, projections to extend to at least 2075, and new housing built to protect people and property; Queensland accounted for more than half of over 400,000 home damage claims from declared disasters since 2022.
ticker_line: Insurers urge Queensland to strengthen planning rules
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: Insurer mis-sold funeral cover and harassed customer, AFCA finds
summary: AFCA found Hannover Life Re unfairly sold funeral cover to a 34-year-old single mother with multiple sclerosis, made it difficult for her to cancel and contacted her 40 times about missed payments. The insurer must refund her premiums with interest and pay $2,000 for the distress caused.
ticker_line: AFCA orders insurer to refund premiums and pay compensation
author: Insurance News
heading: Life Insurance

title: CDPP discontinues aiding and abetting charge against Clive Palmer for PLC takeover law breach
summary: The Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions has discontinued proceedings against Clive Palmer over an allegation that he helped Palmer Leisure Coolum breach takeover laws in 2012. The brief notice does not give a reason for the decision.
ticker_line: CDPP drops Clive Palmer takeover law proceedings
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Media release: Sharetea pays penalties for alleged breaches of the Franchising Code
summary: Sharetea Australia has paid $39,600 in penalties after the ACCC issued two infringement notices over alleged breaches of the Franchising Code of Conduct. The ACCC alleged the bubble tea franchisor’s agreements made franchisees pay Sharetea’s costs for settling disputes with them.
ticker_line: Sharetea pays $39,600 over alleged franchise code breaches
author: ACCC Media <do-not-reply@accc.gov.au>
heading: ACCC

title: ASIC calls out super trustees for blind spots in overseeing member complaints
summary: ASIC is urging superannuation trustees to take greater responsibility for overseeing issues raised in member complaints. A review found weaknesses that could leave Australians exposed to avoidable harm.
ticker_line: ASIC flags gaps in super complaint oversight
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Youpla directors breached duties over related-party insurer, court finds
summary: The Federal Court found former Youpla chief executive Bryn Jones and director Ronald Pattenden breached their duties over insurance arrangements with Crown Insurance Services, a Vanuatu company owned and controlled by Pattenden and another director. Pattenden was fined $250,000 and barred from managing companies for 15 years; penalties for Jones are yet to be decided, while rulings on three other former directors are pending.
ticker_line: Youpla directors breached duties over related-party insurer
author: Camille Joyce Lisay
heading: Regulation

title: Struggling international students understand their health cover least, Medibank finds
summary: A Medibank and Nous Group report found that one in four international students surveyed struggle with their health and wellbeing, and those doing worst often understand their Overseas Student Health Cover least. The report says students need clearer, timely information about what cover excludes, upfront costs and how to claim, while noting its survey of 2,296 students at six universities may not represent all international students in Australia.
ticker_line: Struggling students know least about health cover
author: Camille Joyce Lisay
heading: Health Insurance

title: PHP2Shell shutdowns test cyber policy triggers
summary: PHP2Shell flaws have prompted precautionary shutdowns, making cyber insurance cover for business interruptions a key concern, even as confirmed breaches were initially limited. Evidence of exploitation has since grown, and Marsh Re warns that losses could rise, particularly for smaller businesses that take longer to patch affected systems.
ticker_line: PHP2Shell puts cyber shutdown cover under scrutiny
author: Jonalyn Cueto
heading: General Insurance

title: ASIC opens new probe into adviser qualification records
summary: ASIC has launched a new review to check whether qualifications and training recorded for financial advisers on its register meet the required standard. Licensees must ensure adviser records are accurate; advisers who do not meet the standard cannot give personal advice to retail clients on relevant financial products.
ticker_line: ASIC checks advisers’ qualifications on register
author: Jonalyn Cueto
heading: Regulation

title: Australia, UK partner to procure well-regulated financial markets
summary: Australia and the UK agreed to share information and work together on risks in private markets, including how super funds value and govern their investments. They also discussed AI in financial advice, cyber risks and cross-border investment, with their next regulatory forum due in 2027.
ticker_line: Australia and UK deepen cooperation on financial market risks
author: Matthew Wai
heading: Regulation

title: Audit quality continues to fall short: ASIC
summary: ASIC says companies and auditors need to improve financial reporting and audit quality, after finding some failed to properly challenge key judgements on revenue, asset values and impairment.
