Ten companies agreed to improve disclosures or accounting, while the six largest audit firms must assess their problems and prepare action plans that ASIC will monitor.
ticker_line: ASIC demands lasting improvements in audit quality
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Regulation

title: ASFA names new board members
summary: ASFA has appointed Australian Retirement Trust chief executive Kathy Vincent and Brighter Super chief executive Kate Farrar to its board, with both starting in December 2026. Chair Linda Elkins said their experience would help ASFA support the super sector through demographic and economic challenges.
ticker_line: ASFA appoints two super fund chief executives to board
author: Karren Vergara
heading: Superannuation

title: Former Youpla Group CEO Bryn Jones and director Ronald Pattenden found to have breached their duties as directors
summary: Former Youpla Group chief executive Bryn Jones and director Ronald Pattenden were found to have breached their duties as directors of Youpla Group companies. ASIC’s notice links to a full media release but does not provide further details.
ticker_line: Former Youpla leaders found to have breached director duties
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: ASIC Daily News round-up - 30 October 2026
summary: ASIC’s 30 October round-up says former Youpla Group CEO Bryn Jones and director Ronald Pattenden were found to have breached their duties. ASIC also announced a review of market operators’ financial resources rules, said it is not convinced retail prediction markets are in the public interest, launched court action over alleged failures involving First Guardian super investments, and began checking advisers’ qualifications.
ticker_line: ASIC targets director duties, super investments and advice
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Update from the Treasury
summary: The Treasury alert links to a joint statement from the 2026 UK–Australia Joint Financial Regulatory Forum, dated 29 October 2026. The alert does not include details of the statement’s decisions or outcomes.
ticker_line: Treasury publishes UK–Australia regulatory forum statement
author: The Treasury <noreply@treasury.gov.au>
heading: Treasury

title: Brave broker, Zurich help NIBA Convention raise record $177,000
summary: NIBA raised a record $177,000 for Ovarian Cancer Australia at its annual convention, including a $40,000 contribution matched by the Z Zurich Foundation. The charity will use the funds for nursing, counselling and support for women and families, as well as advocacy and research; broker Taylor Burstow championed the cause after his mother died from ovarian cancer in 2023.
ticker_line: NIBA raises record $177,000 for ovarian cancer support
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: Premium growth slows amid claim cost challenges
summary: Finity’s Optima report says Australian insurers’ premium growth slowed to 3% last financial year, its lowest in a decade, as claim costs rose and commercial insurers faced tougher competition. Growth is forecast to reach 5% this year, but profitability is expected to ease, with personal insurance premiums rising faster than commercial premiums.
ticker_line: Insurer premium growth slows as claim costs rise
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: Antipodean wins Lloyd's paper to chase the risks insurers overlook
summary: Sydney-based Antipodean Underwriting has become a Lloyd’s-approved coverholder, allowing it to offer insurance backed by Lloyd’s syndicates to Australian small businesses. The five-person agency says online systems will reduce paperwork for brokers, while its underwriting decisions remain subject to the limits and capacity set by the syndicates that carry the risk.
ticker_line: Antipodean targets small businesses with Lloyd’s backing
heading: General Insurance

title: Just 29% would claim for work-related mental harm, EML finds
summary: EML research found only 29% of workers would be likely to claim compensation if work seriously harmed their mental health, while many take leave, work through distress or leave their jobs without telling employers why. EML says employers should address workplace risks early; serious mental health claims have risen 169% in a decade, and NSW inspectors can act on unmanaged hazards even when no one has made a claim.
ticker_line: Most workers unlikely to claim for mental harm
author: Camille Joyce Lisay
heading: General Insurance

title: ASIC consults on financial resources requirements for market operators
summary: ASIC is seeking feedback on proposals to make its guidance clearer on the financial resources licensed market operators in Australia must hold. The media release does not provide further details about the proposals.
ticker_line: ASIC seeks feedback on market operator financial rules
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Painting at dawn: how surveillance sank a 17% PTSD claim
summary: A NSW Personal Injury Commission review panel cut a CTP claimant’s psychiatric impairment rating from 17% to 7%, rejecting PTSD and finding an adjustment disorder after reviewing surveillance footage of him working full days at construction sites. The decision may limit his entitlements because adjustment disorder is classed as a threshold injury under NSW’s motor accident law.
ticker_line: Surveillance cuts claimant’s psychiatric impairment rating
author: Elaine Abasta
heading: General Insurance

title: ASIC sues Falcon Capital directors David Anderson and Simon Selimaj alleging First Guardian failures
summary: ASIC has started Federal Court proceedings against Falcon Capital directors David Anderson and Simon Selimaj over alleged failures linked to the First Guardian Master Fund. ASIC alleges hundreds of millions of dollars in Australians’ superannuation were exposed to high-risk, undocumented and conflicted investments.
ticker_line: ASIC sues Falcon Capital directors over First Guardian
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Wettest El Niño year on record? ICA urges sum-insured checks before storm season
summary: The Insurance Council of Australia says 2026 is on track to be the wettest El Niño year on record, despite El Niño usually bringing drier conditions to eastern Australia. It urges households to check their home, contents and landlord cover and make sure their insured amounts reflect rebuilding or replacement costs, as insurers may restrict new policies or cover increases when severe weather is imminent.
ticker_line: ICA urges households to check cover before storms
author: Camille Joyce Lisay
heading: General Insurance

title: IAG reshapes CGU, WFI leadership as Gallagher exits
summary: IAG has changed the leadership of its CGU and WFI insurance businesses, effective October 30, as it continues a $180 million technology upgrade. Damien Gallagher is leaving after 15 years; Dustin Bartley will lead customer and growth, while Chloe Porges takes over workers’ compensation.
ticker_line: IAG reshapes CGU and WFI leadership
author: Camille Joyce Lisay
heading: General Insurance

title: Young travellers drop credit card cover as banks cut benefits, survey finds
summary: Only 9% of insured Australians aged 18 to 29 used automatic credit card travel insurance on their last overseas trip, down from 20% in 2024, as banks cut or restrict the benefit. Young travellers should check whether their cover applies when travelling alone, needs to be activated or excludes their destination; 25% of young travellers said they would go without insurance on their next trip.
ticker_line: Young travellers turn away from credit card cover
author: Camille Joyce Lisay
heading: General Insurance

title: APRA releases Monthly Authorised Deposit-taking Institution Statistics for September 2026
summary: APRA has released its Monthly Authorised Deposit-taking Institution Statistics for September 2026. The publication is available on APRA’s website.
ticker_line: APRA publishes September 2026 banking statistics
author: APRA web updates <subscriptions@apra.gov.au>
heading: APRA

title: Media release: H&M pays penalties over absent and inaccurate fire safety warnings on kids' nightwear
summary: H&M Australia has paid $138,600 in penalties after allegedly selling more than 4,000 items of children’s clothing without required fire safety warning labels, or with warnings that were not accurate. The ACCC says this breached the Australian Consumer Law.
ticker_line: H&M pays $138,600 over children’s clothing warnings
author: ACCC Media <do-not-reply@accc.gov.au>
heading: ACCC

title: Markel's underwriting profit surges 55% as specialty insurer strips out reinsurance exit
summary: Markel’s insurance business lifted underwriting profit 55% to $462.6 million in the nine months to September 30, 2026, with a 92% combined ratio, showing it made a profit from its insurance operations. Adjusted premium volume rose 10% after excluding its exited reinsurance business and a change to how its Hagerty collector-car business is reported; group adjusted operating income was down 2% over the nine months.
ticker_line: Markel underwriting profit jumps 55% as core premiums grow
author: Paul Lucas
heading: General Insurance

title: AXIS Capital grows premiums 11% but acquisition costs rise
summary: AXIS Capital’s insurance premiums rose 13% in the third quarter of 2026, but higher commissions and other acquisition costs helped push its combined ratio up to 94% and cut net income by 32% to US$202 million. Its new AXIS Capacity Solutions unit is driving growth while using third-party capital, but brings higher costs; reinsurance recorded its 11th straight profitable quarter.
ticker_line: AXIS premiums grow as acquisition costs weigh on profit
author: Mark Rosanes
heading: General Insurance

title: A delay in paying SMSF death benefits is acceptable to the ATO as long as it was caused by external factors beyond the trustee’s control.read more
summary: The ATO may accept delays in paying SMSF death benefits beyond the usual six-month guide when events outside trustees’ control are responsible, such as court disputes or difficulty finding beneficiaries. Poor internet access was not accepted as a valid reason for a delay of about five years, and trustees should document delays and seek advice from their fund auditor or the ATO.
ticker_line: ATO accepts some delays in SMSF death benefit payments
author: Darin Tyson-Chan
heading: Superannuation

title: Non-lodging funds create tax gap
summary: The ATO estimates unpaid tax in the small super funds sector reached $104 million in 2023/24, equal to 4.1% of the $2.54 billion in tax payable. It linked the rising gap to more SMSFs failing to lodge annual returns: 65,566 funds, or 10.8% of registered SMSFs, were not lodging, up from 812 in 2018.
ticker_line: ATO links rising SMSF tax gap to unlodged returns
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: Aware Super elevates data and AI with new promotions
summary: Aware Super has appointed Murray Keir to the newly created role of head of investment innovation and promoted Ganesh Suntharam to head of systematic, effective immediately. The $248 billion fund says the changes will help it use data, technology and AI across investment decisions, including its systematic equities platform, which manages more than $25 billion.
ticker_line: Aware Super promotes leaders to expand data and AI
author: Vinny Vucago
heading: Superannuation

title: ASIC proposes extending tax advice exemption for licensees
summary: ASIC proposes extending the tax advice exemption for financial services licensees and their representatives for five years, beyond its scheduled expiry on 1 April 2027. The exemption lets them give limited comments on tax implications of products outside their authorisation, provided they warn clients in writing that they are not authorised to give that advice and suggest seeking authorised advice; submissions are open until 25 November.
ticker_line: ASIC proposes five-year extension to tax advice exemption
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Regulation

title: Super funds lend voice to tokenisation
summary: The RBA and Digital Finance CRC have formed an advisory group, including AustralianSuper, Aware Super and Australian Retirement Trust, to guide the use of tokenised assets and digital money in wholesale financial markets. It follows Project Acacia, which estimated tokenisation could bring $24 billion in annual economic gains, and will focus on turning trials into practical use.
ticker_line: Super funds join push to scale financial tokenisation
author: Vinny Vucago
heading: Superannuation

title: Update from the Treasury
summary: The Treasury has opened consultations on draft standards for the Consumer Data Right. The proposals cover minimum authentication requirements and alignment with FAPI 2.0, a technical standard for secure online access.
ticker_line: Treasury seeks feedback on Consumer Data Right standards
author: The Treasury <noreply@treasury.gov.au>
heading: Treasury

title: ASIC Daily News round-up - 29 October 2026
summary: ASIC’s 29 October round-up lists three items: Chair Sarah Court’s remarks on access, efficiency and resilience in Australia’s capital markets; findings that financial reporting and audit quality are still falling short; and her opening statement to a Senate committee’s supplementary budget estimates hearing. ASIC called on companies preparing financial reports and their auditors to improve the basics.
ticker_line: ASIC flags weak reporting and audit quality
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: NIBA says evidence, not argument, settled the fee disclosure fight
summary: NIBA says evidence supported its decision not to require brokers to disclose their pay upfront to every client. The 2027 Code, starting on 1 January, lets any client ask for the amount in dollars and requires automatic disclosure for strata insurance, but critics still want broader upfront disclosure.
ticker_line: NIBA Code requires disclosure on request, not upfront
author: Daniel Wood
heading: General Insurance

title: Most Australian liquidations return nothing to creditors, ASIC finds
summary: An ASIC review of 26,664 Australian liquidations from July 2021 to June 2025 found that 88.1% of completed cases paid ordinary unsecured creditors nothing, while only 5.3% paid any dividend. ASIC urged directors to act early when finances worsen, as company insolvencies remain high and the simplified liquidation process is rarely used.
ticker_line: ASIC finds most liquidations return nothing to creditors
author: Jonalyn Cueto
heading: Regulation

title: ASIC surveillance shows financial reporting and audit quality continues to fall short
summary: ASIC says its latest review found companies preparing financial reports and their auditors are still making basic mistakes. It has called for both groups to improve the quality of financial reporting and audits.
ticker_line: ASIC says financial reporting and audit basics still fall short
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Cyclone pool passes $1bn in claims, but strata mitigation discounts total just $1,716
summary: The Cyclone Reinsurance Pool has paid more than $1 billion in claims since 2022, after nine declared cyclones in 2025–26, without needing the Commonwealth’s $10 billion guarantee. But mitigation discounts remain scarce: they cut strata premiums by just $1,716 in total and SME premiums by nothing, so brokers are urged to check eligible building upgrades are recorded and note that SME discounts began on 1 April 2026.
ticker_line: Cyclone pool pays $1bn, but discounts barely reach strata
author: Camille Joyce Lisay
heading: General Insurance

title: ASD wants security before uptime, but cyber policies may not pay for the downtime
summary: Australia’s cyber agency says organisations should put security ahead of keeping services running, and be ready to take systems offline. But cyber insurance may not cover lost income from a voluntary shutdown, especially if no attack is underway, so businesses should check their policy wording.
ticker_line: Cyber shutdowns may leave businesses without cover
author: Camille Joyce Lisay
heading: General Insurance

title: Second FRRR round targets Alfred and Queensland flood communities as insurers' grants stay small
summary: The Foundation for Rural & Regional Renewal has opened a second $250,000 Suncorp-funded grant round for community groups affected by Cyclone Alfred and western Queensland floods, offering up to $25,000 per group. Applications close on November 26, with grants due in February 2027; the article notes that such programs can support local recovery but are small compared with insurers’ disaster losses.
ticker_line: Second Suncorp grant round targets flood-hit communities
author: Camille Joyce Lisay
heading: General Insurance

title: Kill the kickback: Victoria comes for strata insurance commissions
summary: Victorian Labor has pledged to ban owners corporation managers from receiving commissions or other payments that could influence purchases, including building insurance, if it wins the November 28, 2026 election. The government also plans to examine broker commissions, which are governed by federal rules; the proposed ban would affect more than 500,000 strata-managed properties.
ticker_line: Victoria pledges to ban strata insurance kickbacks
author: Elaine Abasta
heading: General Insurance

title: APRA publishes Chair John Lonsdale's Opening Statement to the Senate Economics Legislation Committee - October 2026
summary: APRA has published Chair John Lonsdale’s opening statement to the Senate Economics Legislation Committee for October 2026. The notice does not provide details of what he said; it links to the full statement.
ticker_line: APRA publishes Lonsdale’s Senate committee statement
author: APRA web updates <subscriptions@apra.gov.au>
heading: APRA

title: Supplementary Budget Estimates, Opening Statement, 29 October 2026
summary: ASIC Chair Sarah Court delivered an opening statement to the Senate Economics Legislation Committee’s Supplementary Budget Estimates hearing on 29 October 2026. The notice links to the full statement but does not provide details of what she said.
ticker_line: ASIC chair opens Senate budget estimates hearing
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Valuation evidence has 90-day relevance
summary: SMSF legal specialist Bryce Figot says trustees should give auditors valuation evidence, such as comparable sales, that is no more than three months old—ideally close to 30 June. He says this is based on his experience with ATO audits, not a formal ATO rule, and auditors should ask clients to explain older evidence and record their reasoning.
ticker_line: Figot urges SMSF trustees to use recent valuation evidence
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: Call for all MISs to be registered
summary: The Financial Advice Association Australia has urged the government to require every managed investment scheme to register and give ASIC a role in checking high-risk schemes before they are offered to investors. It supports stronger data collection and oversight, saying the extra costs would be justified if they help prevent collapses such as Shield and First Guardian; the FAAA also announced three directors will be appointed at its 23 November annual meeting.
ticker_line: FAAA calls for all investment schemes to register
author: Jason Spits
heading: Regulation

title: Inflation hits 4.3%, RBA says it remains 'too high'
summary: Australia’s annual inflation rose to 4.3% in September, while underlying inflation increased to 3.6%, keeping both above the RBA’s 2% to 3% target range for 14 months. RBA deputy governor Andrew Hauser said inflation was still too high; housing and fuel costs were key contributors, and MLC economist Bob Cunneen warned borrowers to prepare for a possible rate rise as early as 3 November.
ticker_line: Inflation rises to 4.3%, keeping rate rise fears alive
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Economy

title: Cbus creates new role for legal operations
summary: Cbus has appointed Tim Sutton to the newly created role of group head of legal operations and strategy. Sutton has more than 15 years’ experience in legal and regulatory roles, including at ASIC, APRA and Colonial First State; the fund is also preparing for Joshua Parisotto to join as chief member officer this month.
ticker_line: Cbus appoints legal operations and strategy chief
author: Matthew Wai
heading: Superannuation

title: Update from the Treasury
summary: Treasury published an opening statement to the Economics Legislation Committee on 28 October 2026. The alert does not include the statement’s contents.
ticker_line: Treasury publishes opening statement to committee
author: The Treasury <noreply@treasury.gov.au>
heading: Treasury

title: ASIC Daily News round-up - 28 October 2026
summary: ASIC is proposing to renew an instrument that lets some financial licensees provide tax advice without a separate tax agent registration. The proposed changes are minor and would not alter how the exemption works.
ticker_line: ASIC proposes to renew tax advice exemption for licensees
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Tourism operators seek ‘right brokers’ amid coverage struggle
summary: The Queensland Tourism Industry Council is setting up a panel of specialist brokers to help tourism and events businesses find insurance suited to their risks, as premiums rise and cover becomes harder to secure. Applications close on December 22; the council’s report also calls for changes including a larger cyclone reinsurance pool property cap, a state insurance tax overhaul and national public liability reform.
ticker_line: Queensland tourism council seeks specialist insurance brokers
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: One data error, $12 million overcharged: NRMA Insurance penalised eight times over
summary: NSW regulator SIRA fined NRMA Insurance $479,500 over eight CTP pricing and data failures, including an address error that overcharged about 41,564 policyholders by an estimated $12.2 million. The insurer must still review and remediate affected policies, including large groups of renewal customers, and comply with special licence conditions.
ticker_line: NRMA fined $479,500 over eight CTP pricing failures
author: Elaine Abasta
heading: General Insurance

title: NSW CTP benefit indexation to push Green Slip premiums higher
summary: NSW CTP benefits rose from 1 October 2026, lifting caps for weekly payments to $3,853 and non-economic loss damages to $521,000. Higher claim costs may put further pressure on Green Slip premiums, as fund levies have also increased and a scheme that previously helped reduce premiums is no longer reclaiming insurer profits.
ticker_line: NSW CTP benefit increases add pressure to Green Slip prices
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: AFCA’s expanded scam powers raise new questions for insurance brokers
summary: ASIC is consulting on changes to its guide for overseeing AFCA ahead of new scam complaint powers starting on 31 March 2027, initially covering banks, phone companies and digital platforms. Insurance is not yet included, but could follow; brokers should watch for changes and check whether clients’ policies cover scam losses, as AFCA’s new process may allow complaints against several firms and raise the cap on direct scam-loss claims to $1.263 million.
ticker_line: AFCA scam powers put insurance brokers on alert
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: Regulation

title: Queensland disaster insurance claims top $11bn as planning policy faces overhaul
summary: Queensland accounted for more than 214,000 of Australia’s 400,000-plus disaster insurance claims from 2022 to 2026, costing insurers $11.3 billion nationally. The Insurance Council of Australia wants Queensland’s planning rules to use consistent, up-to-date hazard maps and account for future climate risks, warning that building in high-risk areas can increase damage, repair delays and insurance costs.
ticker_line: ICA urges stronger hazard rules in Queensland planning
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: Two-thirds of recovered stolen cars contain hidden hazards
summary: IAG says almost two-thirds of recovered stolen cars it assessed in 2025-26 contained potential hazards, including drug items, biological contamination or weapons, highlighting risks beyond visible vehicle damage. Its report also points to rising repair complexity and costs as cars adopt more advanced safety technology and electric vehicles become more common.
ticker_line: IAG flags hidden hazards in recovered stolen cars
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: Booking platform hack exposes third-party cyber risk across Australian tourism sector
summary: A breach at booking software provider RMS Cloud exposed genuine guest booking details, which scammers used to send fake payment requests to guests at Australian holiday parks and accommodation providers. The affected parks are warning customers, while the incident raises concerns about reputational damage, privacy obligations and whether cyber insurance covers breaches at third-party suppliers.
ticker_line: RMS Cloud breach exposes holiday guests to phishing scams
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: MIS reforms must avoid added burdens
summary: The SMSF Association has urged Treasury to make managed investment scheme data reforms place reporting duties on the firms and platforms that hold the information, not on SMSF trustees. It supports better data collection to help regulators spot risks and act early, while warning that collecting data must lead to timely action and not create unnecessary burdens for SMSF investors.
ticker_line: SMSF body urges MIS reforms without trustee burdens
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: SMSFs not suited to holding a business
summary: Superannuation lawyer Phil Broderick says an SMSF can legally run a business, but restrictions on borrowing, using assets as security and dealings with related parties make it difficult in practice. He says SMSFs are better suited to standard investments such as shares, property and cash, which can receive concessional tax treatment, particularly for people below the $3 million and $10 million super balance thresholds.
ticker_line: Lawyer warns SMSFs are a poor fit for running businesses
author: Darin Tyson-Chan
heading: Superannuation

title: Crypto qualifications need clear process
summary: SMSF auditors should assess separately whether crypto holdings require a Part A qualification for the fund’s financial report and a Part B qualification for breaches of superannuation rules, says Tactical Super director Jacob Kewley. Missing audit reports from crypto exchanges may support a Part A qualification, but do not automatically require Part B; auditors should document their reasoning and decide whether to report a breach.
ticker_line: Crypto audits require separate, documented qualification decisions
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: Smarter SMSF provides new AI tool
summary: Smarter SMSF has launched Smartie AI, a tool for professionals that answers technical questions across six areas of self-managed super funds using the company’s own reference material and showing sources for each answer. Available from 18 November and licensed per firm, it is designed to speed up research; Smarter SMSF says it does not use personal client data and has security controls in place.
ticker_line: Smarter SMSF launches sourced AI assistant for professionals
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: ASIC issues another stop order for private credit fund
summary: ASIC has temporarily stopped the Murdoch Clarke Mortgage Fund from offering, issuing, selling or transferring investments, saying its product disclosure statement may not clearly explain related-party dealings, fees, risks and withdrawal terms. The $573.2 million fund says it has sent ASIC an amended statement and is working to have the order lifted; ASIC may make the order final if its concerns are not addressed in time.
ticker_line: ASIC halts Murdoch Clarke fund over disclosure concerns
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Regulation

title: Queensland wants to build around flood risk. Insurers, however, want it to build away from it
summary: Queensland’s government wants to simplify planning rules and manage flood risk through how homes are designed, while the Insurance Council of Australia says development should be steered away from high-risk areas. Insurers want consistent, up-to-date flood maps and clear rules on acceptable risk, warning that flood damage adds to rebuilding costs and competes with new housing for workers and materials.
ticker_line: Insurers urge Queensland to steer homes from flood risk
author: Matthew Sellers
heading: General Insurance

title: Treasury floats changes to banking, estate payment limits
summary: Treasury is consulting on banking changes, including lifting the limit on covered bonds from 8% to 12% of a bank’s assets and reducing reporting requirements for smaller banks. It also proposes doubling the amount families can withdraw from a deceased person’s account without probate or letters of administration, from $15,000 to $30,000, and allowing court filing fees to be paid; submissions close on 30 October and 30 November, with changes planned from later this year.
ticker_line: Treasury proposes higher bank funding and estate limits
author: Karren Vergara
heading: Banking

title: Palmer Leisure Coolum Pty Ltd convicted and fined $10,000 for breaching takeover law
summary: Palmer Leisure Coolum Pty Ltd was convicted and fined $10,000 for breaching takeover laws in connection with a proposed takeover of The President’s Club Ltd. ASIC’s notice does not provide further details of the breach.
ticker_line: Palmer Leisure Coolum fined $10,000 over takeover breach
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: ASIC Daily News round-up - 27 October 2026
summary: ASIC published a report and data on how insolvent liquidations work and what they mean for creditors, employees, directors and liquidators. It is also consulting on updated guidance for overseeing AFCA under the incoming Scams Prevention Framework.
ticker_line: ASIC reviews insolvency outcomes and AFCA scam oversight
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Insurance News conference launches with Shark Tank star and broking chiefs
summary: The Insurance News Outlook 2027 conference will be held in Sydney on March 11, with Shark Tank entrepreneur Nick Bell and senior leaders from Marsh, Gallagher and Arch Insurance among the speakers. The full-day event will cover market trends, industry challenges and topics including technology risks, motor, strata and rural insurance; early bird tickets are now on sale.
ticker_line: Insurance Outlook 2027 names speakers and opens ticket sales
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: IAG fined $479k over CTP failings
summary: NSW’s insurance regulator fined IAG $479,500 over eight failures in NRMA Insurance’s compulsory third party (CTP) systems, including incorrect pricing that affected almost 42,000 policies and led to estimated overcharges of $12.2 million. NRMA says it identified and reported the issues, is paying affected customers back with interest, and has moved to a new system; it can seek a review of the penalty.
ticker_line: IAG fined $479,500 over NRMA CTP system failures
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: The AI tool Australian insurers deploy could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity"
summary: Anthropic’s IPO filing warned that its AI could pose catastrophic risks and said it is uncertain where liability lies when its systems cause harm. The article says this raises concerns for Australian insurers and businesses using AI, with regulators urging stronger oversight and underwriters facing pressure to review policy cover and exclusions.
ticker_line: Anthropic filing sharpens AI liability concerns for insurers
author: Paul Lucas
heading: General Insurance

title: How specialising in tradie insurance fuelled ProTrades Insurance's rapid growth
summary: Melbourne-based ProTrades Insurance says its focus on tradies and construction businesses has helped it grow quickly, earning a place among Australia and New Zealand’s fastest-growing brokerages in 2026 and ranking seventh in Insurance Business Australia’s Top Brokerages. The firm says it asks detailed questions about clients’ work to find suitable cover, while using technology to speed up service without losing personal contact.
ticker_line: ProTrades grows by specialising in tradie insurance
author: Chris Sweeney
heading: General Insurance

title: ASIC review provides insight into insolvent liquidation process and outcomes
summary: ASIC has published a report and data on how insolvent liquidations work and what outcomes they produce for creditors, employees, company directors and liquidators. The media release does not include further details about the findings.
ticker_line: ASIC publishes report on insolvent liquidation outcomes
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: APRA responds to consultation on amendments to superannuation data collections
summary: APRA has released its response to consultation on moving superannuation data collections from Direct to APRA (D2A) to APRA Connect. It is updating reporting standards to make them consistent with other APRA Connect collections; the response, submissions and final standards are available on APRA’s website.
ticker_line: APRA finalises standards for super data move
author: APRA web updates <subscriptions@apra.gov.au>
heading: APRA

title: Most brokerages experimenting with AI lack a formal policy to govern it, NIBA research finds
summary: A NIBA survey found 91% of Australian brokerages have tried or adopted AI, but only about one-third of those have a formal policy and more than one in five have no AI-specific safeguards. The report says firms with a detailed technology plan are more likely to use AI in core operations, as regulators increase their focus on governance, privacy and risk.
ticker_line: Most brokerages using AI lack formal policies
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: Marsh creates captive strategy role as global premiums top US$79 billion
summary: Marsh has appointed Sydney-based Shawn Willis to a new role advising clients across the Pacific on captive insurance, as demand for these arrangements grows. Marsh-managed captives wrote US$79.1 billion in premiums in 2025, while 118 new captives were formed, up from 92 in 2024, despite commercial insurance prices falling.
ticker_line: Marsh names Pacific captive strategy leader as premiums grow
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: The hidden headlines in the AFCA Annual Review
summary: AFCA received 19% more complaints in 2025–26 and paid or secured $834.2 million in compensation and refunds. General insurance complaints rose 5% overall, but claims disputes jumped about 30% as a sharp fall in consumer credit insurance complaints masked increases in claim denials, delays and disputes over payouts; complaints about life cover held through super also rose sharply.
ticker_line: Claims disputes surge despite modest rise in complaints
author: Matthew Sellers
heading: General Insurance

title: Workers compensation fraud conviction as NSW regulator ramps up enforcement
summary: Christopher Halligan was convicted in NSW for falsely claiming workers compensation while working full-time and submitting fraudulent pharmacy invoices. SIRA says it has pursued 11 fraud or non-insurance cases to court outcomes since January 2024, as it also steps up employer audits and recovers unpaid premiums amid pressure on workers compensation costs.
ticker_line: NSW regulator steps up workers compensation fraud enforcement
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: Mega breaches nearly triple as health sector tops Australia’s data breach count
summary: The OAIC received 667 data breach reports in the first half of 2026, with breaches affecting more than one million people rising to 11 from four in the previous period. Health providers reported the most breaches, while the growing size of incidents and tighter privacy rules are prompting calls for businesses and brokers to review cyber insurance cover and how much personal data they keep.
ticker_line: Mega data breaches surge as health sector leads reports
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: Motor insurance distraction risk may be double what crash data shows
summary: Allianz research found distraction was a definite or possible factor in 67% of crashes reported by Australian drivers who said they caused or partly caused a collision—about twice the rate usually captured in official data. The findings point to risks from both phone use and complex touchscreen controls, with potential implications for motor insurance pricing, fleet risk assessments and vehicle design.
ticker_line: Allianz study finds distraction in two-thirds of reported crashes
author: Roxanne Sanjose
heading: General Insurance

title: Association calls for balanced compliance
summary: The SMSF Association has urged the Australian National Audit Office to assess whether the ATO responds quickly to serious misconduct while treating minor, unintentional errors proportionately. It also wants clearer, up-to-date ATO guidance for self-managed super funds, as the sector now holds more than $1 trillion in retirement savings.
ticker_line: SMSF Association urges balanced ATO compliance approach
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: Early access needs peak standards applied
summary: Accurium’s Mark Ellem says SMSF trustees should get certificates from two qualified doctors before releasing super early under the permanent incapacity rules. The tax law requires these certificates for tax concessions, and Ellem says they would also help show auditors and the ATO that the release was lawful.
ticker_line: Trustees urged to meet stricter early access test
author: Darin Tyson-Chan
heading: Superannuation

title: Property alternative requires discipline
summary: SMSFs may still invest in residential property through a unit trust after restrictions on using limited recourse borrowing to buy residential property took effect on 10 August. Auditors Institute ambassador Graeme Colley warned that the structure needs careful oversight: actions that leave the trust with debt can trigger the 5 per cent limit on related-party assets and create compliance problems.
ticker_line: Unit trust property option demands careful SMSF oversight
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: AustralianSuper rolls out new investment data platform
summary: AustralianSuper has introduced a new platform that brings investment positions, transactions and risk information into one shared record, giving its teams a more consistent, up-to-date view of the portfolio. The fund says it should reduce manual data work, improve oversight and support faster analysis as it grows; AustralianSuper manages nearly $438 billion for more than 3.8 million members.
ticker_line: AustralianSuper brings investment data into one platform
author: Vinny Vucago
heading: Superannuation

title: AIA names regional chief executive for key markets
summary: AIA has appointed former HSBC insurance chief Edward Moncreiffe as regional chief executive for Australia, New Zealand, India and Sri Lanka, effective 2 November 2026. Based in Hong Kong, he will report to AIA group chief executive Lee Yuan Siong and work with local leaders to grow the businesses.
ticker_line: AIA appoints Moncreiffe to lead four key markets
author: Matthew Wai
heading: Life Insurance

title: ASIC Daily News round-up - 26 October 2026
summary: ASIC has temporarily stopped Murdoch Clarke Mortgage Management Ltd from making offers under the disclosure document for its registered mortgage investment scheme. The notice does not explain why ASIC took this action.
ticker_line: ASIC temporarily halts Murdoch Clarke mortgage scheme offers
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Worker mental illness costs tipped to spiral without strategy overhaul
summary: Workplace mental health claims are rising by 10.6% a year, more than twice the rate of other work-related illnesses and injuries. A report warns that mental health could account for 40% of workplace illness and injury absences by 2041-42, costing the economy more than $27 billion a year, and calls for a co-ordinated focus on prevention.
ticker_line: Workplace mental health costs could top $27 billion
author: Insurance News
heading: Life Insurance

title: Ombudsman sees no let-up in funeral cover complaints
summary: Funeral insurance complaints to AFCA rose to 127 in 2025-26, up from 105 the year before, with concerns including rising premiums and policies costing more than their benefit. AFCA supports proposed changes such as guaranteeing a minimum payout linked to premiums paid, while the life insurance industry will consider the recommendations next year and ASIC plans to review providers in 2026-27.
ticker_line: Funeral insurance complaints rise as AFCA backs reforms
author: Insurance News
heading: Life Insurance

title: Service calls used to push funeral policy upgrades, AFCA finds
summary: AFCA found TAL Life did not mis-sell a funeral policy when it sold it by phone in 2014, so it does not have to refund the premiums. But TAL unfairly pressured the man to increase his cover in yearly calls from 2015 to 2020, despite his request to stop the calls, and must pay him $1,500 for stress and inconvenience.
ticker_line: TAL ordered to pay $1,500 over funeral policy calls
author: Insurance News
heading: Life Insurance

title: Insurance, risk reduction key to north Australia growth plans, Canberra told
summary: The Insurance Council of Australia told federal MPs that affordable, available insurance is essential for developing northern Australia’s critical minerals and renewable energy industries. It said the cyclone reinsurance pool has helped moderate premiums but cannot address wider cost pressures or reduce physical risks, and called for stronger protection of homes, businesses and infrastructure.
ticker_line: Insurance and risk reduction vital to northern growth
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: Law association names annual award winners
summary: The Australian Insurance Law Association named former president Sue Vidler its 2026 life member and Andrew Sharpe the winner of its insurance law prize. Rural Affinity underwriter Tanya Ponggun won the young professionals speaking competition, ahead of Zara Jays and Will Hodgman.
ticker_line: AILA honours insurance law leaders and rising talent
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: ASIC halts offers in mortgage scheme managed by Murdoch Clarke Mortgage Management Ltd
summary: ASIC has temporarily stopped Murdoch Clarke Mortgage Management Ltd from making offers under the product disclosure statement for its registered managed investment scheme. The notice does not explain why ASIC made the order or how long it will last.
ticker_line: ASIC temporarily halts Murdoch Clarke mortgage scheme offers
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Media release: Perfection Fresh admits to fixing the price of vegetables sold to ALDI
summary: Perfection Fresh has admitted to fixing prices for vegetables sold to ALDI, agreeing with the ACCC to ask the Court to impose a $12 million penalty for nine breaches and one attempted breach. It has also agreed to set up a competition law compliance program; the Court will decide later whether the proposed penalty and other orders are appropriate.
ticker_line: Perfection Fresh admits vegetable price fixing
author: ACCC Media <do-not-reply@accc.gov.au>
heading: ACCC

title: Brokers now choosing networks for culture over compliance, NIBA research reveals
summary: NIBA research says Australian insurance brokers are increasingly choosing authorised representative networks for their culture, accessible leaders and peer support, not just licensing and compliance. The 10 largest networks reported $4.79 billion in premiums in FY2025, up about 316% in a decade, and the report says continued growth must be matched by strong supervision, technology and broker support.
ticker_line: Broker networks grow as culture drives broker choices
author: Roxanne Libatique
heading: General Insurance

title: Low catastrophe losses drive Munich Re guidance raise ahead of soft renewal
summary: Munich Re lifted its 2026 profit target from €6.3 billion to €6.6 billion after making about €1.7 billion in the third quarter, helped by lower-than-usual catastrophe claims and strong investment income. The result comes as the company cuts back on reinsurance business amid falling prices, with further price declines expected at January 2027 renewals if major losses remain low.
ticker_line: Low catastrophe claims lift Munich Re profit target
author: Mark Rosanes
heading: General Insurance

title: Perth tops motor insurance risk index for driving weather across Australasia
summary: Perth ranked as Australasia’s highest-risk city for driving weather, scoring 61.9 out of 100 in a study of 138 cities, with the region’s highest heat and wet or windy weather scores. The findings come as extreme weather claims and motor insurance costs rise: insured losses reached $4.8 billion in Australia in 2025, while motor premiums rose more than 42% from 2019 to 2024.
ticker_line: Perth tops Australasia’s driving weather risk ranking
author: Roxanne Libatique
heading: General Insurance

title: Gold tier losses accelerate with mental health costs driving downgrades
summary: Nearly 900,000 fewer Australians have Gold private health cover than six years ago, with the share of insured people on Gold falling from about 40% in late 2019 to 28% in late 2025. HCF warns that rising mental health costs could push more people to downgrade, making it harder to access private psychiatric care; it is calling for reforms that expand care outside hospitals.
ticker_line: Gold health cover falls as mental health costs rise
author: Roxanne Libatique
heading: Health Insurance

title: El Niño puts Australian insurers on bushfire watch as global disaster losses hit seven-year low
summary: Global insured disaster losses reached US$92 billion in the first nine months of 2026, the lowest for that period since 2019, largely because few disasters caused very large insured losses. Australian insurers are watching a potentially record El Niño, which can raise bushfire risk: fire authorities have flagged several regions, and WFI reported 73 haystack fire claims, more than double its five-year average, although El Niño does not guarantee higher losses.
ticker_line: El Niño puts Australian insurers on bushfire alert
author: Matthew Sellers
heading: General Insurance

title: ASIC ups thresholds for NTA requirements
summary: ASIC will raise minimum net tangible asset requirements for managed investment scheme operators, IDPS operators and directors of retail CCIVs from 1 July 2027, with thresholds including the $150,000 minimum increasing to $200,000 and the $10 million requirement rising to $14 million. The thresholds, unchanged since 2013, will be adjusted for inflation each year, and ASIC has updated its guidance to reflect the changes.
ticker_line: ASIC lifts financial thresholds for investment scheme operators
author: Karren Vergara
heading: Regulation

title: Insurance Code leaves expert independence gaps, ACIL warns
summary: The Australian Consumers Insurance Lobby says the revised General Insurance Code does not clearly prevent insurers’ commercial arrangements or instructions from compromising the independence of experts who assess claims. The Insurance Council says its expert-report standard requires objective findings; ASIC will assess the draft Code, whose key insurer obligations are proposed to become legally enforceable by customers.
ticker_line: Consumer group flags gaps in expert independence rules
author: Daniel Wood
heading: General Insurance

title: Update from the Treasury
summary: The Treasury listed three consultations dated 23 October 2023: implementing parts of its better regulation measures, the Banking Regulation 2026, and reforms to the bankruptcy system. The alert provides no details about the proposals or how to respond.
ticker_line: Treasury opens consultations on banking and bankruptcy reforms
author: The Treasury <noreply@treasury.gov.au>
heading: Treasury

title: ASIC Daily News round-up - 23 October 2026
summary: ASIC is seeking permission to appeal a NSW Supreme Court ruling that former Rex directors John Sharp, Siddharth Khotkar and Lincoln Pan did not breach their duties over a 2023 profit forecast. The regulator also cancelled financial adviser Evan Byrnes’ registration for two and a half years and accepted auditor Benjamin Peters’ request to cancel his registration after raising concerns about his audit work.
ticker_line: ASIC challenges Rex ruling and takes action against adviser, auditor
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Financial Services and Credit Panel cancels registration of NSW financial adviser Evan Byrnes for two and a half years
summary: The Financial Services and Credit Panel has cancelled NSW financial adviser Evan James Byrnes’ registration. He cannot be registered as a financial adviser for two and a half years.
ticker_line: Panel bars NSW adviser Evan Byrnes for 2.5 years
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: ‘Consistency is key’: ICA backs Victoria’s property flood risk reform
summary: The Insurance Council of Australia supports Victoria’s new mandatory flood-risk ratings, which will guide where homes can be built and the standards they must meet. It says councils must apply the rules consistently and share updated flood maps with insurers, helping reduce future disaster losses and support affordable insurance.
ticker_line: Victoria makes flood-risk ratings mandatory for planning
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: Regulator urged to consult on code before approval call
summary: Consumer groups are urging ASIC to seek public feedback before deciding whether to approve the Insurance Council of Australia’s revised code of practice, saying it still falls short on claims handling and the use of experts. The ICA says the changes improve customer outcomes while keeping insurance affordable and accessible; a consultants’ group sees progress, but the consumers’ lobby says key protections remain unresolved.
ticker_line: Consumer groups urge ASIC to consult on insurance code
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: IAG’s $12.4 billion claims bill signals what brokers face at renewal
summary: IAG paid $12.4 billion in claims and responded to 109 weather events in FY26, while its net natural disaster claims came close to its budget, highlighting the pressure severe weather can put on insurance costs. Broker-sold premiums grew just 1.1%, compared with 17.8% growth in direct sales, although IAG says competition and slower commercial markets—not a retreat from brokers—explain the gap; it expects overall premium growth of 5% to 8% in FY27.
ticker_line: IAG’s claims bill highlights pressure on broker renewals
author: Roxanne Libatique
heading: General Insurance

title: ASIC seeks leave to appeal NSW Supreme Court decision against former Rex non-executive directors
summary: ASIC is seeking permission to appeal a NSW Supreme Court ruling that former Rex directors John Sharp, Siddharth Khotkar and Lincoln Pan did not breach their duties over a profit forecast issued on 28 February 2023. The court’s decision will stand unless ASIC is granted leave to appeal and succeeds.
ticker_line: ASIC seeks appeal over former Rex directors’ duties
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Victoria’s flood risk ratings to reshape development rules and premium pricing
summary: Victoria has introduced mandatory flood-risk ratings that will limit development in the most flood-prone areas and give councils clearer rules. Insurers may use better flood maps to set more accurate premiums, but examples from Wagga Wagga show that flood protection does not always lead to cheaper insurance.
ticker_line: Victoria makes flood planning rules mandatory
author: Roxanne Libatique
heading: General Insurance

title: ASIC accepts cancellation of company auditor Benjamin Peters’ registration after audit surveillance
summary: ASIC has accepted Benjamin Alfred Peters’ application to cancel his registration as a company auditor. The decision followed concerns raised by ASIC about his work as lead auditor and engagement partner on the audit of a large private company.
ticker_line: ASIC accepts auditor Benjamin Peters’ registration cancellation
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: APRA consults on confidentiality of data collected under SRS 604.0 RSE Licensee Profile
summary: APRA is seeking feedback on whether specified data collected under reporting standard SRS 604.0 should be treated as confidential. The data is already included in APRA’s 2025 and earlier superannuation publications, and APRA says it is not proposing to change what is published or how; submissions close on 6 November 2026.
ticker_line: APRA seeks feedback on super data confidentiality
author: APRA web updates <subscriptions@apra.gov.au>
heading: APRA

title: Insurers face legally binding Code obligations for first time under revised Code of Practice
summary: The Insurance Council of Australia has sent ASIC a revised General Insurance Code that would make key insurer promises legally enforceable through policies, courts, AFCA or the Code Governance Committee. It includes automatic acceptance of some home and motor property claims after 12 months without a decision, stronger support for vulnerable customers and clearer rules on delays and cash settlements; ASIC must approve the Code before it takes effect.
ticker_line: Revised insurance code makes key promises enforceable
author: Roxanne Libatique
heading: General Insurance

title: Insurance complaints surge for fifth year as claims issues mount
summary: AFCA received 36,022 general insurance complaints in 2025-26, up 5% for the fifth year in a row, with motor and home building insurance complaints rising sharply. Delays were the most common issue, while complaints about denied claims also jumped; AFCA says insurers must keep customers informed and resolve problems earlier.
ticker_line: Insurance complaints rise for fifth straight year
author: Roxanne Libatique
heading: General Insurance

title: HDI Global promotes Sheena Williams to lead sport, leisure and entertainment globally
summary: HDI Global has promoted Sheena Williams to global head of sport, leisure and entertainment, tasking her with linking expertise across its international offices and growing its sports personal accident, film and entertainment insurance business. The move comes as insurers face rising demand for specialist cover for complex events and competition from global rivals.
ticker_line: HDI Global appoints Williams to lead specialist insurance
author: Mark Rosanes
heading: General Insurance

title: Retirement income and health insurance bundled in AIA-Allianz Retire+ deal
summary: AIA Australia and Allianz Retire+ have formed a partnership combining AIA’s health and wellbeing programs with Allianz’s guaranteed lifetime income product, AGILE, to support Australians approaching or in retirement. It is not a bundled product; the companies will work with super funds, advisers and other providers, as more than 2.8 million Australians are expected to retire over the next decade.
ticker_line: AIA and Allianz join forces on retirement support
author: Roxanne Libatique
heading: Superannuation

title: Critical global website flaw sparks alerts across Asia-Pac as attacks begin
summary: Two critical PHP flaws that can let attackers take control of web servers or read sensitive data from memory have prompted urgent warnings across Australia and Asia-Pacific, with security firms reporting active attacks and fixes now available for supported versions. The flaws may affect websites even if their own code is secure, raising the risk of data breaches and costs for organisations and cyber insurers.
ticker_line: PHP flaws trigger urgent warnings as attacks emerge
author: Matthew Sellers
heading: General Insurance

title: Update from the Treasury
summary: The Treasury has published its Annual Report for 2025–26. The subscriber alert provides no further details about the report.
ticker_line: Treasury publishes its 2025–26 annual report
author: The Treasury <no-reply@treasury.gov.au>
heading: Treasury

title: AFCA warns on AI submissions as complaints surge to new record
summary: AFCA received a record 119,949 complaints in 2025–26, including more than 36,000 about general insurance; motor insurance led with 14,430. It warned that AI-written complaints can be too long or contain inaccurate claims, and urged insurers to improve communication, explain delays and handle claims fairly and promptly.
ticker_line: AFCA records complaints surge and warns on AI submissions
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: Soft market bypasses bushfire zones, warns veteran NSW broker
summary: Veteran NSW broker Barry Sonter says a soft insurance market is bringing lower prices and more cover for lower-risk properties, but bushfire-exposed clients in the Snowy Mountains still struggle to get the cover they need. One Finsura client pays about $300,000 a year yet can secure only 40% of its required bushfire cover, and Sonter warns affordability and access may worsen when the market tightens.
ticker_line: Soft market leaves bushfire risks short of cover
author: Daniel Wood
heading: General Insurance

title: APRA publishes Deputy Chair David Bradbury’s speech to FSC Retirement Summit
summary: APRA has published Deputy Chair David Bradbury’s speech to the 2026 FSC Retirement Summit in Sydney. He said the super system must prepare for about 2.5 million people moving into retirement over the next decade, guard against major risks such as cyber attacks, and address weaknesses in how trustees oversee investments.
ticker_line: APRA flags retirement, cyber and investment governance risks
author: APRA web updates <subscriptions@apra.gov.au>
heading: APRA

title: Pacific rates fall 12%, but not every client gets the cut
summary: Pacific commercial insurance rates fell 12% in the third quarter of 2026, marking 11 straight quarters of declines, with property down 14%, casualty down 11%, financial and professional lines down 8% and cyber down 8%. The cuts were not shared evenly: exposure growth, US risks, poor claims records and weather exposure could limit savings or push premiums up, while strong competition and well-planned renewals helped some clients secure better terms.
ticker_line: Pacific insurance rates fall, but savings vary
author: Rod Bolivar
heading: General Insurance

title: Strata, SME properties slip out of the cyclone pool as homes keep their savings
summary: The Cyclone Reinsurance Pool continues to lower home insurance premiums in high-risk areas, but fewer strata and small business properties are covered by it. The pool recorded a $701 million surplus in 2025–26, while proposed rates would lift its annual premiums by 2.9% from July 2027.
ticker_line: Cyclone pool helps homeowners as strata cover falls
author: Camille Joyce Lisay
heading: General Insurance

title: Insurance moves: Chubb, Gallagher, DUAL
summary: Chubb has appointed former AIG Australia chief executive Kathleen Warden to lead its property and casualty business in Australia and New Zealand. Gallagher Australia has named John Mutton to head its affinity division from early 2027, while DUAL Australia has hired Jane Makin as a senior liability underwriter.
ticker_line: Chubb, Gallagher and DUAL announce senior insurance hires
author: Camille Joyce Lisay
heading: General Insurance

title: Saudi Arabia's "Do not travel" deepens a travel insurance exclusion that started in July
summary: Australia raised its travel advice for Saudi Arabia to “Do not travel” on October 19, warning people to postpone trips and noting insurance and consular help may be limited. But insurance exclusions may already apply to policies bought from July 21, when advice was raised to Level 3; cover depends on when the policy was purchased and its wording, including for people leaving by road.
ticker_line: Saudi travel warning sharpens insurance cover risks
author: Camille Joyce Lisay
heading: General Insurance

title: 485 strikes and counting: AFCA drops its first non-compliance hit list
summary: AFCA has published its first list of financial firms that failed to meet binding complaint rulings, naming 15 firms across 16 entries and recording 592 reports. Dixon Advisory accounts for 485 reports; Drive Lah Australia is the only general insurer listed, with one case. Being named is not a finding of misconduct or a breach of law, but AFCA’s new rule allows it to publicly identify firms that do not comply.
ticker_line: AFCA names firms that failed to follow rulings
author: Elaine Abasta
heading: Regulation

title: Annual Review 2025-26: AFCA reports continued rise in complaints
summary: AFCA received almost 120,000 complaints in 2025–26, its highest number on record, with banking and finance disputes accounting for 66,971. Complaints also rose sharply about superannuation, insurance and financial hardship; AFCA says firms should resolve problems earlier, while its Australian Scams Ombudsman service is due to start taking complaints on 31 March 2027.
ticker_line: AFCA complaints hit record high of almost 120,000
author: Medianet Press Release <medianet@releases.medianet.com.au>
heading: AFCA

title: Auditor number decline continues
summary: ASIC data shows the number of SMSF auditors fell to 3,596 at the end of 2025–26, down nearly 300 in a year and about 30% from five years earlier. ASIC says the decline partly reflects auditors leaving SMSF work; it took action against 64 auditors during the year, with more than two-thirds barred from practising.
ticker_line: SMSF auditor numbers fall 30% in five years
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: Asset ownership proof an audit issue
summary: The ATO says SMSF audit files often lack enough independent evidence to prove listed investments and crypto-assets exist and belong to the fund. Auditors should also check data feeds and service providers’ controls, using other evidence or qualifying their audit report when they cannot get a Type 2 report.
ticker_line: ATO flags gaps in SMSF asset audit evidence
author: Darin Tyson-Chan
heading: Superannuation

title: Premature action undermining deductions
summary: MLC technical expert Scott Quinn warns that delays in lodging a notice of intent to claim a tax deduction for personal super contributions can cost members the deduction. Starting a pension, making a partial rollover or withdrawal, or lodging a tax return before the fund acknowledges the notice may prevent the claim, so members should check the timing carefully.
ticker_line: Delays to super deduction notices can cost members
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: Australian retirement system graded A
summary: Australia’s retirement income system received an A for the first time in the 2026 Marsh CFA Institute Global Pension Index, rising to 80.6 from 77.6 in 2025. The report praised strong superannuation coverage, pension assets and protections, but said the system could better focus on retirement income and adjust the age pension assets test.
ticker_line: Australia’s retirement system earns top global grade
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: Heat storms: the climate peril Australian insurers still aren't counting
summary: A Reuters analysis finds that large, long-lasting heat events have become far more common, but their costs are often missed because they fall across workplace injuries, crop losses, power bills and business disruption rather than declared disasters. Australian insurers face growing heat-related risks: heat costs the economy about $8.7 billion a year in lost labour productivity, while regulators warn overall weather losses could more than double by 2050.
ticker_line: Heat risks grow as insurance losses go uncounted
author: Stephen Owens
heading: General Insurance

title: ASIC investigates potential $138m scam
summary: ASIC is investigating whether oversight and compliance failures linked to Trade Prime, formerly MGF Capital, allowed investors to lose access to at least $138 million. The regulator is examining whether companies acting for MGF Capital provided services to retail investors, even though its licence covered wholesale clients only, and says it may take enforcement action if it finds serious misconduct.
ticker_line: ASIC probes potential $138 million investor scam
author: Eliza Bavin
heading: Regulation

title: Brighter Super changes up investment, insurance fees
summary: Brighter Super cut investment fees and transaction costs on most options from 1 October, including reducing its MySuper investment fee from 0.75% to 0.50% a year. It also raised insurance premiums by an average of 6% for death and total and permanent disability cover and 5.6% for income protection, while extending the terminal illness claim window from 12 to 24 months and adding two low-cost indexed share options.
ticker_line: Brighter Super cuts investment fees, raises insurance costs
author: Karren Vergara
heading: Superannuation

title: Acenda Life launches investment bond
summary: Acenda Life has launched an Investment Growth Bond for long-term investing, wealth transfer and goals such as education funding. Earnings in the bond are taxed at a maximum of 30%; the launch also includes changes to its Fixed Term Annuity to give customers more flexibility and predictable returns.
ticker_line: Acenda Life launches bond and updates annuity
author: Vinny Vucago
heading: Life Insurance

title: Gas transition to take 'decades rather than years': UniSuper
summary: UniSuper chief investment officer John Pearce says natural gas is likely to remain part of the energy mix for decades as governments weigh reliable, affordable energy alongside emissions cuts. The $175 billion fund will report climate figures for the whole fund under Australia’s new mandatory standard from the 2027 financial year; its emissions intensity was 19.9 tonnes of CO₂-equivalent per $1 million invested at 30 June 2026, across 75% of its portfolio.
ticker_line: UniSuper says gas transition will take decades
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Superannuation

title: ASIC Daily News round-up - 21 October 2026
summary: ASIC reported four regulatory actions on 21 October 2026. It cancelled Walker Stores’ credit licence after two compensation payments by the Compensation Scheme of Last Resort, and cancelled NSW adviser Kyle Clifford Frost’s financial services licence, effective 15 October. Twenty-one Visy and Pratt group companies paid $4.158 million in infringement notices over late financial reports, while a new rule will raise responsible entities’ net tangible assets requirement from 1 July 2027.
ticker_line: ASIC reports licence cancellations, fines and new requirements
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: ASIC cancels Australian credit licence of Walker Stores Pty Ltd (in Liquidation) (Receivers and Managers Appointed)
summary: ASIC has cancelled the Australian credit licence of Walker Stores Pty Ltd, which is in liquidation and has receivers and managers appointed. The cancellation followed two compensation payments by the Compensation Scheme of Last Resort.
ticker_line: ASIC cancels Walker Stores’ Australian credit licence
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Top & Fastest-Growing Brokerages 2026: proving value beyond price
summary: The 20 insurance brokerages ranked by Insurance Business for 2026 recorded median revenue growth of 20.5% over the past year, despite falling commercial insurance rates and stronger price competition. The results highlight how brokerages are growing by offering advice, risk management help and strong client relationships, not just the lowest-priced cover.
ticker_line: Top brokerages grow by proving value beyond price
author: Insurance Business
heading: General Insurance

title: Too small to target? Email fraud leads SME cyber claims
summary: Email scams and payment redirection are driving a growing share of cyber claims for small businesses: business email compromise made up 55% of claims under Emergence’s SME policies in Australia and New Zealand so far in 2026, and the average cost rose 22%. Yet cover can be limited or excluded under cyber policies, while cyber insurance remains uncommon among SMEs; insurers are beginning to offer specific protection for social engineering and related fraud.
ticker_line: Email fraud drives SME cyber claims as cover gaps persist
author: Rod Bolivar
heading: General Insurance

title: Uninsurable WHS fines meet tougher psychosocial enforcement
summary: Mental health conditions made up 12% of Australia’s 147,200 serious work injury claims in 2024–25, while NSW and Victoria have tightened rules requiring employers to address workplace psychological risks. NSW has added 51 safety inspectors and increased penalties, but businesses cannot insure WHS fines in five jurisdictions; insurance may still cover the cost of defending a prosecution.
ticker_line: Tougher psychosocial rules put employers under scrutiny
author: Rod Bolivar
heading: General Insurance

title: Central Australia storm: 400 claims lodged, but much of the damage sits outside the count
summary: About 400 insurance claims were lodged in Alice Springs after a 12 October storm with winds up to 96km/h, but much damage in remote outstations and town camps is being repaired by governments or residents and is not reflected in the claims count. Four public housing homes were uninhabitable, and eligible households may receive up to $16,901 for essential structural repairs not covered by insurance.
ticker_line: Storm claims miss damage across remote Central Australia
author: Camille Joyce Lisay
heading: General Insurance

title: Visy and Pratt companies pay over $4.1 million in infringement notices for failing to lodge financial reports on time
summary: Twenty-one companies in the Visy/Pratt group have paid a total of $4.158 million in infringement notices. ASIC issued the notices over the companies’ alleged failure to lodge financial reports for the year ended 30 June 2025 on time.
ticker_line: Visy and Pratt companies pay $4.158m over late reports
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: ASIC cancels AFS licence of Kyle Clifford Frost
summary: ASIC cancelled NSW financial adviser Kyle Clifford Frost’s Australian financial services licence, number 543780. The cancellation took effect on 15 October 2026.
ticker_line: ASIC cancels financial adviser Kyle Clifford Frost’s licence
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: ATO releases updated LRBA guidance
summary: The ATO has updated six guidance documents after changes to the law took effect on 10 August, restricting SMSF limited recourse borrowing arrangements to business real property and excluding residential property. Two draft rulings are open for consultation until 27 November; the other updates clarify how the new rules apply.
ticker_line: ATO updates SMSF borrowing guidance after law change
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: Offshore members have contribution pathways
summary: People who lived overseas can still build up unused concessional super contribution limits and may use them for catch-up contributions after returning to Australia, provided their total super balance was below $500,000 at the previous 30 June. MLC specialists also said Australians overseas may be able to claim a tax deduction for personal super contributions funded by Australian rental income, potentially reducing tax on that income.
ticker_line: Overseas members can use super contribution strategies
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: Advisory practices lacking in AI policy
summary: Intelliflo’s survey of 101 Australian financial advice professionals found 81% of firms use AI, but only 44% have a formal policy and approved tools. Advisers most often use AI for file notes, while inaccurate results and data privacy are their main concerns.
ticker_line: Most advice firms use AI without formal policies
author: Jason Spits
heading: AI

title: Premium pain is everyone's problem, say two of Australia's top brokers
summary: Top Australian brokers Alison Gemmell of Aon and Brooke Tarr of KBI say tackling insurance affordability is a shared responsibility. Gemmell points to laws and government schemes that affect cover and prices, while Tarr says businesses can help by improving risk management and working with brokers and insurers; cyclone pool data shows relief for some high-risk customers, but not across the market.
ticker_line: Brokers say affordability needs action across insurance industry
author: Daniel Wood
heading: General Insurance

title: Corporate, governance issues fuel whistleblower tipoffs: ASIC
summary: ASIC received nearly 2,000 whistleblower tip-offs in the last financial year, up 183% from the year before; 74% concerned companies and governance, including unpaid employee entitlements and insolvent trading. ASIC said about 94% needed no further action, while Treasury is reviewing whistleblower laws; the report also said victims of the Shield and First Guardian collapses have received $421 million of the $1.1 billion owed.
ticker_line: ASIC whistleblower tip-offs surge as Treasury reviews laws
author: Karren Vergara
heading: Regulation

title: HUB24 platform inflows drop 23% to $4bn in Q1
summary: HUB24’s platform net inflows fell 23% to $4 billion in the September quarter, compared with $5.2 billion a year earlier, and have stayed near that level for three quarters. Funds under administration rose 3% to $143.7 billion, while 211 advisers joined, bringing the total to 5,860; HUB24 said tax changes and economic conditions may affect short-term flows but expects long-term growth in superannuation.
ticker_line: HUB24 inflows fall 23% as funds under administration rise
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Superannuation

title: Aussie dealfest – are more insurance buyouts on the way?
summary: More insurance takeovers in Australia look likely, driven by Japanese insurers and private investors with money to spend, but deals are expected to come in bursts rather than a steady stream. Buyers face hurdles including high prices, competition checks and foreign investment approvals; recent examples include the blocked IAG–RAC Insurance deal and a failed bid for AUB Group.
ticker_line: Insurance takeovers likely, but deals face hurdles
author: Stephen Owens
heading: General Insurance

title: ASIC Daily News round-up - 20 October 2026
summary: The NSW Supreme Court disqualified former Rex chief executive and executive chair Lim Kim Hai from managing companies for four years and ordered him to pay an $800,000 penalty over directors’ duties and disclosure breaches. Panacea Capital director Brian Creigh has also been charged with allegedly running a financial services business without a licence and dealing with proceeds of crime.
ticker_line: Former Rex chief fined, Panacea director charged
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Former Rex director Lim Kim Hai disqualified for 4 years and ordered to pay $800,000 penalty for directors’ duties and continuous disclosure contraventions
summary: The NSW Supreme Court has barred former Rex chief executive and executive chair Lim Kim Hai from managing companies for four years. It also ordered him to pay an $800,000 penalty over Rex’s continuous disclosure breaches and his failure to meet directors’ duties.
ticker_line: Former Rex chief Lim Kim Hai fined $800,000
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: NIBA's new strata broker rules win over consumer groups
summary: Three consumer groups have welcomed changes to NIBA’s broker code, starting on 1 January 2027, that require clearer disclosure of payments to strata managers and checks that owners corporations have approved their broker. The changes follow an investigation that found problems in broker relationships with strata representatives; the groups say more work is still needed on complex business arrangements and conflicts of interest.
ticker_line: New broker rules strengthen strata insurance protections
author: Mav Rodriguez
heading: General Insurance

title: Budget Direct opens Adelaide service hub, with room for 300 staff by 2027
summary: Auto & General has opened a Budget Direct customer service centre in Adelaide with about 50 staff, and plans to move to a permanent site that can hold up to 300 people in early 2027. The expansion will create local jobs as the company faces an ASIC court case over allegedly misleading online discounts, an issue it says it self-reported and has addressed with more than $3.8 million in payments to about 39,000 customers.
ticker_line: Budget Direct plans Adelaide hub for 300 staff
author: Camille Joyce Lisay
heading: General Insurance

title: Life insurance council announces grant winners
summary: The Council of Australian Life Insurers has awarded Aisha Elnour and Kristen Agius $2,000 each to attend the FAAA Congress in Melbourne from November 24-26. Its expanded 2026 ReCALIbrate program has ten places: two Congress grants and eight spots in a new 12-month development program for women in life insurance, with those recipients to be announced in November.
ticker_line: CALI expands development program for women advisers
author: Camille Joyce Lisay
heading: Life Insurance

title: Media release: ACCC releases guidance on business emissions claims to consumers
summary: The ACCC has released guidance to help Australian businesses make accurate and credible claims about their greenhouse gas emissions. It says businesses should use trusted, science-based methods, clearly explain any purchased carbon credits and consider what an average consumer would understand their claims to mean.
ticker_line: ACCC issues guidance on business emissions claims
author: ACCC Media <do-not-reply@accc.gov.au>
heading: ACCC

title: Panacea Capital director Brian Creigh charged with criminal offences
summary: Panacea Capital director Brian Jacques Creigh, from Moreton Bay, Queensland, has been charged with running a financial services business without an Australian Financial Services licence and dealing with the proceeds of crime. The charges are allegations; the ASIC notice provides no further details.
ticker_line: Panacea Capital director charged over financial services offences
