author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: Consumer protection measures questioned
summary: The SMSF Association has raised concerns about two proposed super reforms: requiring SMSFs to have uniquely identifiable bank accounts, and letting the ATO help trustees compare fund performance. It supports performance comparisons but says the ATO should not act on low-balance funds in their first year, as some grow quickly; it suggests checking from year three instead.
ticker_line: SMSF body questions proposed consumer protection measures
author: Darin Tyson-Chan
heading: Superannuation

title: Insurance deduction has tax trap
summary: SMSF members can use the future service deduction to claim a larger tax deduction for life insurance premiums when a benefit is paid, but the choice is permanent and prevents future premiums for fund members from being deductible. If a member dies before 65 and a lump-sum benefit goes to a non-tax dependant, such as an adult child, part of the benefit may face tax at 30 per cent, so the immediate saving should be weighed against possible costs for beneficiaries.
ticker_line: Insurance tax deduction may increase beneficiaries’ tax bill
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation

title: TPD claims drive insurance disputes
summary: APRA and ASIC data for the year to 30 June 2026 shows Australian life insurers accepted most claims, but total and permanent disability (TPD) claims had lower acceptance rates and took an average 3.9 months to finalise. Disability income and TPD claims also generated many disputes, while most disputes were resolved and policy eligibility rules were the main reason TPD claims were declined.
ticker_line: TPD claims remain a major source of insurance disputes
author: Vinny Vucago
heading: Life Insurance

title: Australian firms face growing outage losses their insurance may not cover
summary: Telstra’s July outage showed how Australian businesses can lose sales when phone or internet services fail, yet standard business interruption and cyber insurance may not cover outages without physical damage or a malicious attack. Allianz data points to rising losses from downtime and supplier failures, while new rules are prompting businesses to map key services and keep records that can support insurance claims.
ticker_line: Outages expose gaps in business insurance cover
author: Matthew Sellers
heading: General Insurance

title: Car insurance premiums: why motor claims costs keep climbing in Australia
summary: Australian car insurance premiums have risen sharply, driven mainly by higher repair bills, more expensive cars and parts, and delays caused by a shortage of mechanics. ASIC says insurers are not clearly explaining individual price rises, while its research found many customers renew without comparing prices; some who ask their insurer for a better deal get a discount.
ticker_line: Rising repair costs push car insurance premiums higher
author: Matthew Sellers
heading: General Insurance

title: Update from the Treasury
summary: Treasury has opened a consultation on raising the reporting threshold for large proprietary companies. The alert gives no details about the proposed threshold or how the change could affect companies.
ticker_line: Treasury consults on higher company reporting threshold
author: The Treasury <no-reply@treasury.gov.au>
heading: Treasury

title: ASIC Daily News round-up - 19 October 2026
summary: ASIC’s 2025–26 annual report says it secured $830 million in court-ordered civil penalties and helped obtain more than $580 million in repayments and refunds for consumers and investors. ASIC also cancelled the credit licence of liquidated lender MWL Financial Services after a payment by the Compensation Scheme of Last Resort, and expanded its dashboard of reported breaches to cover two full financial years.
ticker_line: ASIC reports $830m in penalties and expands breach data
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: ASIC's annual report outlines strong enforcement and consumer outcomes
summary: ASIC’s 2025–26 annual report says the regulator secured court orders for $830 million in civil penalties. It also helped secure more than $580 million in repayments and refunds for consumers and investors.
ticker_line: ASIC reports $830 million in penalties and $580 million returned
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: ASIC cancels Australian credit licence of MWL Financial Services Pty Ltd (In Liquidation)
summary: ASIC has cancelled the Australian credit licence of MWL Financial Services Pty Ltd, which is in liquidation. The cancellation followed a payment by the Compensation Scheme of Last Resort.
ticker_line: ASIC cancels credit licence of MWL Financial Services
author: "ASIC Media Unit" <media@newsletters.asic.gov.au>
heading: ASIC

title: MLC Super adds leadership roles targeting growth
summary: MLC Super has appointed Lisa Croudace as general manager of portfolio delivery to oversee its change program, and Nerique Paterson as general manager of employer superannuation from January 2027. Paterson will lead efforts to grow and retain employer clients, while Croudace will coordinate the fund’s change projects and delivery priorities.
ticker_line: MLC Super appoints leaders to drive change and growth
author: Adrian Suljanovic
heading: Superannuation

title: Private assets offer potential retirement savings boost
summary: CFA Institute research found that a 10% allocation to private equity in a target-date fund could lift the average retirement balance by 13% over 40 years compared with investing only in public shares and bonds, while venture capital also improved average outcomes. Private debt, infrastructure and property mainly reduced swings in results; the report says outcomes depend on fees, liquidity, fund design and how investments are managed.
ticker_line: Private equity could lift long-term super balances
author: Adrian Suljanovic
heading: Superannuation

title: Robeco expands Australian equities offering for super
summary: Robeco has launched an Australian shares strategy for super funds and other institutions seeking returns above the S&P/ASX 300 while staying close to the index and limiting risk. Available as a tailored mandate, it is expected to hold about 150 stocks and aims to reduce reliance on the market’s large banks and miners.
ticker_line: Robeco launches lower-risk Australian shares strategy
author: Adrian Suljanovic
heading: Superannuation

title: Challenger receives takeover bid from TAL Daiichi Life
summary: TAL Daiichi Life Australia has made a conditional, non-binding offer to buy the 79.5% of Challenger it does not already own, at $11.80 a share through a scheme of arrangement. Challenger’s board is considering the offer, which is subject to due diligence, regulatory approvals and other conditions.
ticker_line: TAL Daiichi Life offers $11.80 a share for Challenger
author: Laura Dew
heading: Life Insurance

title: Early warning signs can trigger insurance notification duties
summary: Lockton says organisations with claims-made insurance should assess and notify insurers about warning signs, such as complaints or internal investigations, before a formal claim arrives. The advice follows a court ruling that the Uniting Church’s delayed notification of information about historical claims linked to Knox Grammar School meant it could not rely on later cover for those claims.
ticker_line: Lockton urges early insurance notifications after court ruling
author: https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/au/authors/jonalyn-cueto/
heading: General Insurance

title: Why AI scams make people the last line of defence
summary: Suncorp cyber security chief Keith Howard says AI is making scams faster, more targeted and harder to recognise, so people remain a key line of defence alongside technology. He urged people to use multi-factor authentication, unique passphrases and updated software, as Australian scam losses reached $554.1 million in the first half of 2026.
ticker_line: Suncorp says people remain key defence against AI scams
author: https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/au/authors/jonalyn-cueto/
heading: General Insurance

title: IBCCC hits brokers with record six sanctions
summary: The Insurance Brokers Code Compliance Committee found 17 breaches and imposed a record six sanctions in 2025–26, after brokers reported 5,417 breaches affecting 14,824 clients and a financial impact of $5.848 million. Renewal delays and poor communication remained key concerns, while a revised Code taking effect on 1 January 2027 will require brokers to give clients at least 28 days’ notice before renewal.
ticker_line: Insurance watchdog imposes record six broker sanctions
author: https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/au/authors/jonalyn-cueto/
heading: General Insurance

title: One in six older Aussies may cancel health cover: report
summary: An iSelect survey found 17% of respondents aged 61 and over might cancel private health cover if planned rebate cuts go ahead, while 20% would consider downgrading. The changes would remove higher rebates for older members from April 2027, but the bill’s future is uncertain after it was reintroduced in Parliament; the survey measured intentions, not actual decisions.
ticker_line: Older Australians weigh cancelling cover over rebate cuts
author: https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/au/authors/jonalyn-cueto/
heading: Health Insurance

title: Youi names Australia’s riskiest driving hour
summary: Youi’s survey of 2,334 drivers found 3pm was the most stressful time to drive, with 55% naming it the peak pressure point and 24% reporting an incident during the afternoon rush in the past year; Youi says its claims data also shows more incidents around that hour than any other. The survey counted near misses and loss of vehicle control as incidents, not just crashes, and found fatigue and rushing were common concerns; Youi says planning ahead and allowing extra travel time can help.
ticker_line: Youi identifies 3pm as the riskiest driving hour
author: https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/au/authors/jonalyn-cueto/
heading: General Insurance

summary: ASIC has banned former MWL Financial Services adviser Pardeep Singh from providing financial services for four years. It is also seeking feedback on a proposed remake of the rules that set out what internal dispute resolution information financial firms must report to ASIC.
ticker_line: ASIC bans former adviser and seeks IDR reporting feedback

title: ‘Exorbitant’ insurance demands hamper right to protest, campaigners say
summary: The Australian Democracy Network and Deakin University say council insurance and traffic-management demands are making it harder for people to hold protests, including a tractor rally in Tasmania that was cancelled after organisers could not get cover. Their report calls for insurance requirements to be scrapped, while the NSW Council for Civil Liberties says some people have been asked to pay councils more than $2,000 for extra cover.
ticker_line: Campaigners say insurance demands are blocking protests
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

summary: Aon's report predicts that Australian employer medical plan costs will rise by 4.9% in 2027, exceeding inflation by 1.7%. This increase is slightly lower than the previous year's forecast, but ongoing healthcare costs remain a challenge for employers.

summary: Howden Insurance Brokers Australia has appointed Catherine Osborne as its new head of technical & claims, bringing extensive experience from her previous role as chief claims officer at Marsh Pacific. Osborne aims to enhance client support and strengthen Howden's claims services.

title: ATO to update existing LRBA guidance
summary: The ATO will soon release updated guidance on limited recourse borrowing arrangements (LRBAs) for self-managed super funds (SMSFs), including existing rulings and new information for trustees. This update aims to clarify the rules around using LRBAs to acquire business real property.

title: SMSF loans to other funds questionable
summary: An SMSF can lend to another SMSF under certain rules, but both funds must ensure it benefits their members and complies with regulations. Key issues include the sole purpose test, in-house asset limits, and ensuring the loan terms are fair and justifiable.

Its superannuation and investment business had net outflows of $138 million, down from $241 million a year earlier, while assets under management rose to $62.7 billion; AMP also won an employer super contract due to start in early 2027.

summary: ASIC is seeking feedback until 27 November 2026 on draft rules and guidance for digital asset platforms and tokenised custody platforms, ahead of new laws taking effect on 8 April 2027. heading: Regulation

summary: ASIC has started consulting on new rules for digital asset platforms and token custody services, which will take effect on 8 April 2027.

title: Exclusions scupper ANZ class action claim
summary: ANZ Bank has lost a court case to make insurers cover its costs from settling two class actions. The court ruled that exclusions in the insurance policies meant ANZ could not claim for these costs.

summary: The ACCC is taking Kmart to court for selling cosmetic nail glue without proper warnings and button battery products that don't meet safety standards. This action claims Kmart violated Australian Consumer Law.

summary: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) will release findings on the Big Four audit firms, including KPMG, by the end of 2026. This comes amid ongoing investigations into KPMG's handling of confidential information and the fallout from a whistleblower scandal, which has led to major clients like ANZ and Insurance Australia Group seeking new auditors.
ticker_line: ASIC to release audit findings by year-end

title: Genetic testing ban for life insurers now in force, with penalties of up to $1.65m
summary: A new federal law bans life insurers from using genetic test results in underwriting, effective October 8, 2026. Insurers face penalties up to $1.65 million for breaches, while consumers can now seek help from the Australian Financial Complaints Authority for disputes related to this issue.
ticker_line: Life insurers banned from using genetic test results

summary: The ACCC is asking Australians for their opinions on mobile coverage and services as part of its Mobile Services Inquiry. Consumers and businesses can share their views through an online survey or by submitting feedback on a discussion paper.

summary: State Super members are limiting retirement spending due to worries about future health and aged care costs, despite the security of their defined benefit pensions. Rising living expenses and family financial support are also affecting their retirement plans.

heading: Superannuation

title: MLC retirement income product reaches $1.2bn FUM
summary: MLC's Retirement Boost product has reached $1.2 billion in funds under management just one year after its launch, reflecting a shift in focus from saving for retirement to generating income from those savings. The product allows clients to move between superannuation and pension phases, potentially increasing their retirement income significantly.

author: Adrian Suljanovic

summary: ASIC has started consulting on new rules for digital asset platforms and token custody, set to begin on 8 April 2027.

title: APRA and RBNZ complete joint bank stress test to promote trans-Tasman resilience
summary: APRA and RBNZ have completed their first joint stress test since 2017, showing that banks in Australia and New Zealand can handle severe economic downturns while continuing to support credit for households and businesses. The test examined risks from geopolitical tensions, oil price shocks, and a deep recession, highlighting the importance of cooperation between the two regulators.
ticker_line: APRA and RBNZ complete joint bank stress test

title: APRA welcomes Basel endorsement of Australia’s bank leverage ratio framework
summary: The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) has received confirmation from the Basel Committee that Australia's bank leverage ratio rules meet international standards. This framework helps limit how much debt banks can take on compared to their capital, ensuring stronger financial stability.
ticker_line: APRA's bank leverage rules get Basel approval

summary: The SMSF Association warns that changes to the rules on limited recourse borrowing arrangements (LRBAs) could lead to unintended problems, particularly affecting how properties are classified and limiting investment options for self-managed super funds (SMSFs). Concerns were raised that these changes might restrict SMSF members from investing in residential properties, which could impact their investment strategies.
ticker_line: SMSF sector faces challenges from LRBA rule changes

title: Fund control can exist in two countries
summary: An SMSF can have its central management and control in both Australia and overseas if trustees actively participate from both locations, according to DBA Lawyers. This allows trustees who move abroad to remain involved without needing to resign.

heading: Superannuation

title: Caution needed on premium payment change
summary: SMSF members can pay life insurance premiums from any account, but must ensure it's fair and does not disadvantage other members or beneficiaries. Changes to where premiums are deducted should be carefully documented to avoid issues, especially in complex family situations.
ticker_line: Caution urged on life insurance premium payments
heading: Superannuation

title: IMF sees inflation above RBA target through 2027
summary: The IMF expects Australian inflation to ease from 3.9% this year to 3.1% in 2027, still above the RBA’s 2% to 3% target. It also forecasts growth to slow to 1.6% next year, and says interest rates may need to stay restrictive or rise further to bring inflation under control.
ticker_line: IMF expects inflation to remain above target in 2027
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Economy

title: 'Flawed' CSLR model needs to be redesigned: SMC
summary: The Super Members Council warns that the government's proposed changes to the Compensation Scheme as a Last Resort (CSLR) unfairly shift costs onto everyday Australians, rather than holding high-risk financial sectors accountable for their failures. They call for a redesign that better aligns costs with the sources of consumer harm.
ticker_line: CSLR changes unfairly burden everyday Australians
author: Matthew Wai
heading: Superannuation

title: ASIC flags gaps in super fund valuations
summary: ASIC found weaknesses in how some super funds and auditors value unlisted investments, including heavy reliance on external managers and inadequate checks. It warned that inaccurate values can affect members’ balances, returns and fees, and will widen its reviews in 2026–27 to cover 20 super funds and 20 managed investment schemes.

heading: Superannuation

The Code, which is still awaiting approval from ASIC, could take effect by 2028 and includes new protections for vulnerable customers and automatic claim acceptance after 12 months.

heading: General Insurance

Improved control measures like the Wolbachia bacteria have reduced local outbreaks, but travel insurance policies may not cover dengue-related claims if an outbreak is declared at a travel destination.
ticker_line: Dengue risk rises, but cases mostly from travel

Last year's top areas for claims included Manly West in Queensland and Werribee in Victoria, while WA had more consistent patterns.
ticker_line: Suncorp reveals changing storm damage hotspots
author: Insurance News
heading: General Insurance

title: Hail and bushfire risk collide this spring as IAG warns of a stormy fortnight
summary: IAG warns that eastern Australia will see more storms and a higher bushfire risk this spring due to El Niño. Recent severe storms in South Australia caused damage and power outages, while IAG advises customers to prepare for potential claims from hail and wind damage.
ticker_line: IAG warns of storms and bushfire risks ahead
author: Camille Joyce Lisay
heading: General Insurance

summary: Arch Insurance Australia has promoted Andrew Whitlock to head of casualty, while Acenda Life has appointed Ross Miller as chief commercial officer and PPS Mutual has hired Maria Repac as business development manager for New South Wales. These changes aim to strengthen their operations and support for advisers in the insurance sector.

summary: ASFA and Super Consumers Australia are joining a national effort with 26 organisations to combat financial abuse of older Australians. ticker_line: New tax affects super balances over $3 million
heading: Superannuation

title: Macquarie shareholders question its climate change commitment
summary: Macquarie Group shareholders are questioning the company's commitment to climate change goals ahead of its annual meeting on July 23, particularly regarding its fossil fuel financing. A resolution has been proposed to ensure Macquarie's financing aligns with the Paris climate goals, as shareholders express concerns over its recent investment trends.
ticker_line: Macquarie faces shareholder scrutiny over climate goals
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Banking

title: Behavioural constraint is costing retirees greatly: Allianz Retire+
summary: Allianz Retire+ reports that many retirees are missing out on better financial outcomes due to hesitance in making spending decisions, costing them significant amounts from their superannuation. The report highlights the need for financial advisers to help clients manage their uncertainty and encourage more confident spending in retirement.
ticker_line: Retirees lose out due to decision hesitance
author: Matthew Wai
heading: Superannuation

title: APRA sharpens oversight, flags tech and geopolitical risks
summary: APRA is increasing its supervision of banks, insurers, and superannuation funds due to rising global risks from technology and geopolitical issues. The regulator emphasizes the need for better risk management and has introduced new rules to improve operational resilience starting July 1, 2026.
ticker_line: APRA boosts oversight amid global risk concerns
author: Vinny Vucago
heading: Regulation

title: Super tax appeal grows after budget backlash, survey reveals
summary: Investor confidence has dropped sharply after the 2026 Federal Budget, with many Australians now seeing superannuation as a more attractive and tax-efficient investment option. A recent survey shows that nearly 80% of investors view proposed capital gains tax changes negatively, leading to a significant shift towards superannuation.
ticker_line: Investors shift focus to superannuation post-Budget
author: Adrian Suljanovic
heading: Superannuation

title: AUSTRAC steps in on suspected AML weaknesses at NSW club
summary: AUSTRAC has ordered Bankstown District Sports Club to hire an external auditor to check its anti-money laundering controls, amid concerns they may be too weak to prevent criminal activity linked to poker machines.
ticker_line: AUSTRAC orders audit for Bankstown sports club
publication: Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre
heading: AUSTRAC

title: Asset valuation guide released
summary: Super Clarity has released a new guide to help auditors and practitioners understand market valuation for assets in self-managed super funds (SMSFs). It outlines standards, documentation tips, and common mistakes to avoid when valuing assets.
ticker_line: New guide simplifies asset valuation for SMSFs
heading: Superannuation

title: Hub24 releases lifetime super solution
summary: Hub24 has teamed up with TAL to launch a new lifetime super account that helps retirees access better Centrelink benefits when buying a lifetime pension. This account offers a lower assessed asset value, which can lead to increased government support for those eligible.
ticker_line: Hub24 launches new lifetime super account
heading: Superannuation

title: CFS plots 'largest' retirement product expansion with new alliance
summary: Colonial First State (CFS) is launching a major expansion of its retirement products through partnerships with Challenger, Generation Life, and BlackRock. This new approach aims to provide Australians with better lifetime income solutions and will start rolling out in August 2026.
ticker_line: CFS expands retirement products with major alliance
author: Matthew Wai
heading: Superannuation

title: Government to fast track low-risk foreign investments
summary: The Australian government is speeding up the approval process for low-risk foreign investments to attract more capital while increasing scrutiny on higher-risk proposals. Starting next year, low-risk applications will be decided within 30 days, and some approval requirements will be removed to reduce regulatory burdens.
ticker_line: Government fast tracks low-risk foreign investments
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Investments

title: CALI calls for government to help fund CSLR
summary: The Council of Australian Life Insurers (CALI) is urging the government to help fund the Compensation Scheme of Last Resort (CSLR) to ease financial pressure on risk advisers, who face high levies. CALI's CEO, Christine Cupitt, argues that the burden should be shared across the financial sector to support the sustainability of risk advice services.
ticker_line: CALI seeks government support for CSLR funding
author: Matthew Wai
heading: Regulation

title: Cbus warns employers still unprepared for Payday Super
summary: Cbus Super warns that many small businesses are unprepared for the upcoming Payday Super reforms, which require superannuation payments to be made with wages starting July 1. Employers are seeking guidance on compliance and managing payroll changes as the deadline approaches.
ticker_line: Cbus warns small businesses unprepared for Payday Super
author: Adrian Suljanovic
heading: Superannuation

title: Cyber threats pressure super funds to strengthen member protections
summary: Australia's superannuation sector is under pressure to improve cyber security and fraud protections as attacks on member accounts increase. KPMG's report highlights the need for funds to enhance digital capabilities and governance to protect members and meet rising expectations.
ticker_line: Super funds urged to boost cyber protections
author: Adrian Suljanovic
heading: AI

title: Mulino backs stronger scrutiny of retail MISs
summary: Financial Services Minister Daniel Mulino announced increased funding for ASIC to improve oversight of managed investment schemes (MISs) to protect retail investors and prevent large-scale collapses. The government is also working on broader reforms related to consumer protection and financial outcomes following recent investment scheme failures.
ticker_line: Government boosts ASIC funding for investment scheme oversight
author: Laura Dew
heading: Regulation

title: Plan for Armageddon outcomes in funds
summary: SMSF trustees should prepare for worst-case scenarios in their funds, including estate planning and potential changes to trust documents, according to legal expert Michael Hallinan. He emphasizes the importance of having clear strategies and updated trust deeds to manage crises effectively.
ticker_line: Prepare SMSFs for worst-case scenarios
heading: Superannuation

title: Retirees leave 90% of pension unspent: AMP Super
summary: AMP Super's Ben Hillier revealed that retirees are leaving about 90% of their pension unspent when they die. He suggests that financial advisers help clients plan their retirement spending more effectively to avoid regret and ensure they can enjoy their savings.
ticker_line: Retirees leave 90% of pension untouched, says AMP
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Superannuation

title: AI can give fundies an edge over the market: Invesco
summary: Invesco's Scott Bennett shared at a Sydney event that using advanced data and AI can help fund managers gain an advantage in the market. By analysing daily credit card transactions and management communication, Invesco aims to predict company earnings more accurately.
ticker_line: Invesco uses AI for market advantage
author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: AI

title: ASIC furthers simplification with regulatory roadmaps
summary: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) is working to simplify regulations by creating sector-based roadmaps and improving digital services. Over the next six months, ASIC will collaborate with other regulators to streamline data requests and enhance company registration processes.
ticker_line: ASIC aims to simplify regulations for businesses
author: Eliza Bavin
heading: Regulation

title: ASFA joins Finance Industry Council of Australia
summary: The Association of Superannuation Funds Australia (ASFA) has joined the Finance Industry Council of Australia (FICA), marking the first time the superannuation sector is represented in this key financial body. This inclusion aims to ensure superannuation issues are part of important policy discussions affecting Australia's $4.5 trillion financial system.
ticker_line: ASFA joins FICA to boost superannuation representation
author: Vinny Vucago
heading: Superannuation

title: Tokenisation could inject $24bn annually: Project Acacia
summary: Project Acacia, led by the Reserve Bank of Australia, has shown that tokenisation could boost Australia's economy by $24 billion each year. The project explored new ways to improve financial markets using digital assets and highlighted the need for better industry coordination and regulatory support.
ticker_line: Tokenisation could boost economy by $24 billion
author: Matthew Wai
heading: AI

title: Super funds get ahead of proposed minimum service standards: KPMG
summary: A KPMG report shows that superannuation funds are proactively improving their services ahead of new government standards set for 2028, focusing on accountability and better member experiences after facing significant fines for delays in benefit payments.
ticker_line: Super funds enhance services before new standards
author: Karren Vergara
heading: Superannuation

title: APRA calls for input on insurance claims database confidentiality rules
summary: The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) is asking for industry feedback on changes to how it publishes insurance data, including plans to report cyber insurance and management liability separately. The consultation period runs until June 16, 2026.
ticker_line: APRA seeks input on insurance data changes
author: Roxanne Libatique
heading: AI

title: Home premiums in top cyclone risk areas down sharply since pool launched
summary: Home insurance premiums in Australia's cyclone risk areas have dropped by 37% since the government’s reinsurance scheme started in October 2022. The number of available insurance policies in these areas also increased by 27%, showing the scheme's positive impact on affordability and access to coverage.
ticker_line: Cyclone insurance premiums drop 37% in risk areas
author: Roxanne Libatique
heading: General Insurance

title: Super funds rebound as global markets recover through April

author: Adrian Suljanovic
heading: Superannuation

title: Inflation and the Impact of the Middle East Conflict
summary: Sarah Hunter from the RBA discussed how the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, particularly rising oil prices, is affecting inflation in Australia. She explained that while the RBA aims for a 2-3% inflation rate, external factors like global oil prices can influence costs and prices domestically.
ticker_line: RBA addresses inflation amid Middle East conflict
heading: RBA

title: NIBA backs TasInsure plan
summary: The National Insurance Brokers Association supports the Tasmanian Government's new insurance authority, TasInsure, aimed at improving insurance affordability. They also stress the need for consistent rules on how brokers disclose their earnings.

author: Jonalyn Cueto
heading: General Insurance

title: Sword of Damocles falls: How insurer cooperation is finally cracking fraud

This cooperation has already uncovered around $300 million in fraudulent claims, shifting the focus from simply denying claims to prosecuting fraudsters.
ticker_line: Insurers unite to crack down on fraud
author: Daniel Wood
heading: General Insurance

title: TR 2013/5 solution still being sought

heading: Superannuation

ticker_line: Queensland lifts cap on SMSF members to six
heading: Superannuation

ticker_line: ASIC flags issues in climate report disclosures
author: Vinny Vucago
heading: Regulation

title: ACCC approves Zurich's ClearView takeover
summary: The ACCC has approved Zurich Financial Services' takeover of ClearView Wealth for 65 cents per share, valuing the deal at about $425 million. The merger is expected to have a low impact on competition in the life insurance market in Australia.
ticker_line: ACCC approves Zurich's ClearView acquisition
author: Karren Vergara
heading: Life Insurance

heading: Superannuation

ticker_line: New law helps abuse survivors access superannuation
author: Adrian Suljanovic
heading: Superannuation

title: RBA and DFCRC Release Findings From Project Acacia
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia and the Digital Finance Cooperative Research Centre released findings from Project Acacia, which explored how digital money and tokenised assets can improve Australia's wholesale financial markets. The project identified benefits and challenges of tokenisation and proposed a new program to support innovation in the financial sector.
ticker_line: RBA and DFCRC unveil Project Acacia findings

heading: Banking

New fees and changes to TPD benefits will also be introduced, along with updates to investment risk labels and allocation strategies.

author: Riddhima Talwani
heading: Superannuation

title: New trust tax may impact estate planning

While testamentary trusts created before the budget announcement will be exempt, uncertainties remain about future implications and potential opportunities for self-managed super funds (SMSFs).
ticker_line: New tax rules may change estate planning strategies

heading: Superannuation

author: Daniel Croft
heading: AI

author: Adrian Suljanovic
heading: Superannuation

title: Australians back tougher crackdown on super switching advertisements

author: Adrian Suljanovic
heading: Superannuation

author: Adrian Suljanovic
heading: Superannuation

author: Adrian Suljanovic
heading: Superannuation

title: Digital ID program gets $650M for expansion in Australian federal budget

This funding will enhance the Australian Government Digital ID System and improve data sharing and security measures.

heading: Economy

title: High Street's restructure bets against the agency roll-up model

author: Daniel Wood
heading: General Insurance

title: A win delivered for super members

The proposed 'MyIncome' initiative would facilitate the transition of superannuation funds into pension phase, ensuring members begin drawing income by age 75.
