summary: Westpac has seen a 20% drop in housing investor loan applications following proposed federal budget changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax. The bank expects house prices to fall further, while it aims to attract younger customers and improve its retail banking strategy.
ticker_line: Westpac's investor loans fall 20% amid tax changes
author: James Eyers
heading: Banking

title: One in five taking drugs for mental health treatment
summary: Nearly 20% of Australians are now prescribed mental health drugs, with ADHD treatments for boys tripling in the last decade. Experts are concerned about the ease of access to these medications and the lack of proper follow-up assessments.
ticker_line: Surge in mental health drug prescriptions raises concerns
author: Michael Smith | Health
heading: Health Insurance

title: AI safety ignored in sprint to go public, critics warn
summary: Australian super funds are investing heavily in AI companies like Anthropic and OpenAI as they prepare for IPOs, but critics warn that safety concerns about AI technology are being overlooked in the rush for profits. Recent developments, including Anthropic's new model launch, raise questions about the balance between innovation and safety.
ticker_line: Super funds chase AI IPO profits amid safety concerns
author: Paul Smith
heading: Investments

title: Westpac tips shift in home lending
summary: Westpac is changing its home lending strategy due to a drop in applications after the government's budget changes. The bank expects more interest-only loans as it aims to improve customer service and increase its share of the mortgage market.
ticker_line: Westpac shifts home lending strategy post-budget changes
author: David Ross
heading: Banking

title: Regulations stifling growth, says ANZ boss
summary: ANZ CEO Nuno Matos says Australia's strict regulations are slowing economic growth and urges a more entrepreneurial approach. He also anticipates a decline in home lending due to recent government tax changes.
ticker_line: ANZ CEO warns of growth limits from regulations
author: David Ross
heading: Economy

title: Mums’ desperate calls highlight housing crisis
summary: A charity in Northland reports a rise in calls from mothers needing emergency housing to avoid living under bridges with their children. New research shows over 33,000 children in New Zealand face severe housing issues, with many in Northland living in overcrowded or unsafe conditions.
ticker_line: Northland mothers face housing crisis for kids
author: Yolisa Tswanya
heading: Economy

title: Insurance brokers in apartment sector reported to watchdog
summary: Two insurance brokers have been reported to the Australian Securities and Investments Commission for not disclosing conflicts of interest related to profit-sharing with strata managers. This follows a review that found all seven brokers investigated violated the industry's code of practice, raising concerns about transparency in the growing apartment sector.
ticker_line: Insurance brokers face scrutiny over conflicts of interest
author: Sarah Petty
heading: Regulation

title: Lifetime Economy Runs at Half-Speed for Country's Young
summary: Australia's economy is struggling, with low growth and falling real wages affecting young people the most. Economists warn that this could lead to the longest period of low living standards since the 1990s recession.
ticker_line: Australia faces longest economic slowdown in decades
author: Luke Kinsella
heading: Economy

title: The Maverick: Houses and banks are about to tank
summary: Australia's housing market is declining, with home values in Melbourne and Sydney dropping significantly. The government's new tax policies and rising interest rates could further impact property prices and the banking sector.
ticker_line: Aussie housing market faces steep decline
author: Christopher Joye
heading: Economy

title: Political promises: One Nation's cost-of-living policies may top $90b
summary: One Nation's cost-of-living policies could exceed $90 billion, raising concerns about their funding and potential impact on the federal budget, with economists doubting the party's proposed savings. The policies include tax cuts and increased welfare support, but critics warn they could worsen the national debt and economic stability.
ticker_line: One Nation's $90 billion cost-of-living plan questioned
author: Michael Read
heading: Economy

title: How to boost a super nest egg
summary: Superannuation contribution caps have increased, allowing Australians to boost their retirement savings significantly. Individuals can contribute up to $1.4 million over five years, with various strategies available to maximise tax benefits.
ticker_line: Superannuation caps rise, boost retirement savings potential
author: Anthony Keane
heading: Superannuation

title: Age pension may be next on the hit list
summary: The government may change age pension access rules to promote fairness, potentially including the family home in means tests. A report suggests this could save $10 billion and affect many retirees who currently receive the pension despite having significant assets.
ticker_line: Government considers changes to age pension access
author: James Kirby
heading: Economy

title: Artificial intelligence: OpenAI targets booming Aussie market with ChatGPT upgrade
summary: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT Work, a new version of its AI tool designed to automate work tasks and integrate with popular applications like Gmail and Slack. This upgrade aims to help users complete projects more efficiently, reflecting the growing demand for AI in Australian workplaces.
ticker_line: OpenAI unveils ChatGPT Work for Aussie market
author: Jessica Yun
heading: AI

title: SMSF curbs 'will shake confidence across spectrum'
summary: New rules limiting self-managed super funds (SMSFs) from borrowing for residential property are expected to reduce Australia's housing supply by 2,500 homes. This change has shaken buyer confidence and could impact both new home building and commercial property investments.
ticker_line: New SMSF rules threaten housing supply and confidence
author: Michael Bleby | Deputy property edi
heading: Superannuation

title: Royal commission aims to stop AI going rogue
summary: South Australian Premier Peter Malinauskas has announced a royal commission into artificial intelligence to prevent potential dangers from unchecked AI. The commission will start on October 1 and report by July 2027, aiming to ensure AI technology benefits society.
ticker_line: South Australia launches royal commission on AI safety
author: Simon Evans and Paul Smith
heading: Regulation

title: RBA believes it is done hiking interest rates, but Michele Bullock doesn't want us to think that
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) is not planning to raise interest rates for now, but Governor Michele Bullock warns that future hikes are still possible if inflation does not improve as expected. She highlighted various risks that could affect inflation, including global economic growth and energy prices.
ticker_line: RBA keeps interest rates steady but warns of hikes
author: business Michael Janda
heading: Economy

title: Labor’s home support scheme panned
summary: State governments are critical of Labor's new aged care home support scheme, citing long wait times and a lack of flexibility in assessments. The program has left many elderly Australians, including those with complex needs, waiting for services, while the removal of private health insurance rebates for seniors could worsen the aged care crisis.
ticker_line: State governments criticize Labor's aged care scheme
author: NOAH YIM
heading: Health Insurance

title: Private health insurers access patients' full medical records in 'aggressive' audits
summary: Private health insurers, like Bupa, are facing criticism for demanding excessive access to patients' full medical histories during audits, raising concerns about patient privacy and legality. Hospitals and health providers report aggressive practices that may violate patient rights and confidentiality laws.
ticker_line: Insurers face backlash over patient privacy violations
author: business Alison Branley
heading: Health Insurance

title: Bendigo Bank to pay APRA penalty
summary: Bendigo Bank will pay an $8 million penalty to the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) for cyber security failures and breaches of the Banking Act from 2020 to 2023. The bank is also facing additional costs and has committed to improving its technology systems after a major cyber leak in 2023.
ticker_line: Bendigo Bank hit with $8 million APRA penalty
author: David Ross
heading: Regulation

title: Mortgage revelations put banks in the spotlight
summary: Westpac's recent report shows a significant drop in mortgage applications, causing its stock to fall and raising concerns about future housing credit growth. Other banks will soon report to see if they face similar challenges.
ticker_line: Westpac's mortgage drop shakes bank stocks
author: David Rogers, Exchange
heading: Banking

title: Big banks drag after gloomy outlook
summary: The sharemarket fell on Monday due to a poor outlook for mortgages, with major banks like Westpac seeing significant drops in their share prices. Despite this, gains in healthcare and mining stocks helped offset some of the losses.
ticker_line: Major banks decline amid mortgage concerns
heading: Banking

title: ASIC wades in after car insurance goes up 50% in six years
summary: Car insurance premiums in Australia have risen by 50% over six years, prompting ASIC to criticise insurers for not clearly explaining these increases. Many customers could save money by negotiating with their insurers, but most do not shop around for better deals.
ticker_line: ASIC challenges insurers over rising car premiums
author: Elias Visontay | National consumer
heading: General Insurance

title: Insurers told to lift their game
summary: Australia's insurance regulator, ASIC, has warned car insurers to improve how they communicate with customers after finding many do not explain premium changes clearly. Premiums have risen 42% since 2019, and customers often miss out on discounts by not switching providers.
ticker_line: ASIC demands better clarity from car insurers
author: David Ross
heading: General Insurance

title: NDIS boss calls for a separate watchdog
summary: The head of NDIS provider Aruma, Martin Laverty, is calling for an independent watchdog and an appeals process for the NDIS as the government plans major changes that could cut costs by $38 billion and remove 241,000 participants. Concerns are growing that automation in decision-making may leave people with disabilities without proper support and appeal options.
ticker_line: NDIS chief demands independent watchdog for reforms
author: Elizabeth Pike
heading: Regulation

title: ‘Rogue’ AI agents roaming undetected through networks
summary: Australian companies are losing track of AI agents in their networks, raising concerns about data security. Okta's Eric Kelleher warns that these agents can operate without oversight, increasing the risk of cyber attacks and breaches.
ticker_line: AI agents pose new security risks for firms
author: Jared Lynch
heading: AI

title: Jim Chalmers is going for broke. Will we end up a poorer country?
summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers is set to unveil a significant budget aimed at tax reform amidst rising inflation and economic challenges, with proposals that may impact intergenerational equity and investment strategies.
author: Matthew Cranston
heading: Economy

title: AusSuper frustrated with Link as death benefits mess escalated
summary: AustralianSuper is frustrated with Link, its administrative provider, over delays in paying death benefits, which could lead to fines of up to $30 million. The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) found that families waited too long for payments, with some waiting up to four years, and noted that the super fund's management was aware of the issues but did not act quickly enough.
ticker_line: AusSuper faces $30 million fines over delays
author: Joseph Carbone
heading: Superannuation

title: Vic tops car theft, home invasion stakes
summary: New data shows Victoria has the highest rates of car theft and home break-ins in Australia, with 12,300 car theft claims worth $244 million and 3,900 home invasion claims worth $56 million last financial year. This rise in crime is becoming a major issue ahead of the state election on November 28.
ticker_line: Victoria leads Australia in car theft and home invasions
author: Patrick Durkin
heading: General Insurance

title: Sydney crime syndicate allegedly defrauded banks of up to $600 million, police say
summary: NSW Police have charged several individuals linked to a crime syndicate that allegedly defrauded Australian banks of over $600 million through fraudulent loans and fake documents. The investigation revealed the group targeted luxury car financing and property loans, leading to significant losses for major banks.
ticker_line: Sydney crime syndicate defrauds banks of $600 million
heading: Banking

title: Rebates for long GP consults should be increased, long-awaited Medicare review says
summary: A government review recommends increasing Medicare rebates for longer GP appointments, especially for women with complex health needs, as current rates unfairly favour shorter visits. The report suggests changes to the rebate system and bulk-billing incentives to better support longer consultations.
ticker_line: Medicare review calls for higher GP rebates
author: national health Stephanie
heading: Health Insurance

title: KPMG client Westpac says trust key in audit business
summary: Westpac has stressed the importance of trust in auditors during a parliamentary inquiry into KPMG's misconduct, which involved sharing confidential documents. Former KPMG partner Kim Lawry was removed from Westpac's audit after breaching confidentiality, while KPMG faces ongoing scrutiny and a hiring ban from the federal government.
ticker_line: Westpac highlights trust amid KPMG audit scandal
author: Tansy Harcourt
heading: Banking

title: Exclusive: Experts push for debate on super
summary: Experts are calling for a debate on using superannuation savings for housing and wage support, as One Nation proposes allowing people to cash out part of their super. The Coalition is divided on how to respond, with some suggesting more radical changes to the superannuation system.
ticker_line: Debate on superannuation use heats up
author: Paul Sakkal | Chief political corre
heading: Superannuation

title: Roads in disrepair as state’s crime soars
summary: Victoria has the highest rates of car and home theft in Australia, while nearly half of its state-owned roads are in poor condition. The government is under pressure to address both crime and road repairs ahead of the upcoming election.
ticker_line: Victoria faces rising crime and road repair issues
author: Lily McCaffrey
heading: General Insurance

title: AI’s early job signs are good, but ‘only just’ and not for all
summary: A new analysis shows that AI is creating more early job opportunities in some fields like engineering and marketing, while reducing jobs in areas like software programming and HR. The impact of AI on the job market is still developing, with positive effects currently outweighing the negatives, according to SEEK's chief economist.
ticker_line: AI boosts early job opportunities in some fields
author: EWIN HANNAN
heading: AI

title: Exclusive: Anger over $1.5b West Gate data centre as AI minister issues warning to sector
summary: A $1.47 billion data centre proposed in Spotswood has faced local opposition due to its high power demand and potential impact on the community. The state government is planning new rules for data centres to address these concerns and ensure they do not burden local infrastructure.
ticker_line: Local anger over $1.5b data centre proposal
author: Clay Lucas and Kieran Rooney
heading: Regulation

title: Technology: Banks urge sovereign AI capacity
summary: Australia's largest banks are urging the government to develop local AI capabilities to ensure economic benefits stay in the country, rather than flowing overseas. They argue that investing in Australian data centres is crucial for national security and economic resilience, especially after recent AI-related security incidents.
ticker_line: Banks push for local AI development in Australia
author: James Eyers
heading: AI

title: Investment: Aware Super warns of runaway AI hype after float collapse
summary: Aware Super, one of Australia's largest super funds, is cautious about investing in AI companies after the failed float of Firmus. While they see potential in AI, they will avoid untested plans and focus on spreading their investments wisely.
ticker_line: Aware Super cautious on AI investments after float failure
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Investments

title: CDC in warning on bad AI behaviour
summary: CDC Data Centres has ended its partnership with Firmus due to concerns over its approach to data centre development, highlighting issues of bad behaviour in the growing AI sector. Firmus also cancelled its planned public listing after failing to attract enough investor interest.
ticker_line: CDC ends deal with Firmus amid AI concerns
author: Jared Lynch
heading: AI

title: Australia considers world-first criminal charges for AI companies that fail to prevent harm
summary: The federal government will consider a new crime for AI companies that fail to take reasonable steps to prevent their models causing harm, as well as a watchdog with power to issue large fines. The proposals follow the September OpenAI Medicare data hack; experts say criminal charges could deter serious misconduct, but proving a company was at fault may be difficult.
ticker_line: Australia weighs criminal penalties for unsafe AI companies
author: national AI Cam Wilson
heading: AI

title: Banks: Home loan stress climbs as ANZ posts $7.6b profit
summary: ANZ reported annual cash profit of $7.6 billion, up 31 per cent, helped by lower costs; excluding one-off items, profit rose 10 per cent. The bank said more home loan customers were falling behind on repayments, with 90-day-plus delinquencies rising to 0.95 per cent, and forecast Australian economic growth of no more than 2 per cent this year.
ticker_line: ANZ profit rises as home loan stress increases
author: Millie Muroi and Clancy Yeates
heading: Banking

title: Chalmers leaks must end, says ally of PM
summary: Environment Minister Murray Watt has called for leaks and criticism targeting Treasurer Jim Chalmers to stop, saying he is doing an excellent job in difficult economic conditions. The dispute comes as Labor faces pressure to cut spending and tackle inflation, while economists warn Australia could enter recession next year and the government promises to find savings in its December budget update.
ticker_line: Watt calls for leaks targeting Chalmers to stop
author: Paul Sakkal
heading: Economy

title: Insurers warn of battery fire crisis
summary: Australian insurers say claims linked to lithium-ion battery fires nearly doubled between 2023 and 2026, as cheap products, unsafe charging and older buildings add to the risk. They warn premiums may rise and urge people to buy from reputable sellers, follow safety instructions and tell their insurer about e-bikes or e-scooters, which may not be covered if modified or non-compliant.
ticker_line: Insurers warn battery fires could lift premiums
author: Jared Lynch, Technology , EXC
heading: General Insurance

title: AI could force rates up but jobs look safe for now: RBA
summary: RBA chief economist Sarah Hunter says the global AI investment boom could keep interest rates higher as businesses compete for funding, while data centre construction and energy demand may also push up costs. AI has not yet reduced overall Australian employment, though hiring may be weaker for young workers in some exposed roles; the RBA expects $115 billion to be invested in Australian data centres by 2028.
ticker_line: AI boom could keep rates higher, RBA warns
author: Shane Wright
heading: AI

title: Commonwealth Bank shareholders go to High Court seeking damages for inflated share prices
summary: Commonwealth Bank shareholders are in the High Court seeking damages for inflated share prices due to the bank's failure to report over 53,000 large transactions properly. They argue that this lack of transparency led to them paying too much for their shares, while the bank claims the shareholders have not proven their losses.
ticker_line: CBA shareholders seek damages over share price inflation
heading: Banking

title: Stocks recover ground after early dive
summary: The Australian sharemarket recovered from a sharp opening drop, with the S&P/ASX 200 closing down 20.9 points at 8604.2. Strong performances from telecommunications and supermarket stocks helped offset losses in the materials sector, particularly iron ore producers.
ticker_line: ASX recovers after early losses on Tuesday
author: CAMERON MICALLEF, EQUITIES
heading: Investments

title: ASIC blasts super fund payout delays
summary: The Australian Securities & Investments Commission (ASIC) is concerned about superannuation funds delaying death benefit payments to grieving members. Despite some improvements, many trustees are still not meeting their responsibilities, and ASIC may take legal action if the situation does not improve.
ticker_line: ASIC warns super funds on death benefit delays
author: Angelica Snowden
heading: Superannuation

title: Climate change costs residents
summary: A report shows that climate change has cost NSW residents about $20,000 each per year, with future impacts expected to worsen household budgets through job losses and higher grocery prices. By 2070, the economy could shrink by $1.5 trillion if climate change continues unchecked.
ticker_line: NSW residents face $20,000 annual climate cost
author: Caitlin Fitzsimmons | Climate and e
heading: Economy

title: Labor slammed on NDIS cutbacks
summary: Labor's proposed changes to the NDIS are facing strong backlash from Paralympians, doctors, and disability advocates, who warn that the reforms could reduce support for disabled Australians and force parents to medicate their children to access the scheme. A Senate inquiry revealed no support for the changes, with calls for the government to either scrap or significantly amend the bill before it is passed.
ticker_line: Labor's NDIS reforms face major backlash
author: Sarah Ison, Senior political report
heading: Regulation

title: ‘The window is now’: Microsoft pitches solution to AI grid crisis
summary: Microsoft plans to invest $25 billion in Australia over three years, urging the government to create an 'AI in Energy Fund' to address rising electricity demand from data centres. The company warns that without changes to the power grid, Australia could face supply issues and increased costs for consumers.
ticker_line: Microsoft pushes for energy fund amid AI boom
author: Perry Williams
heading: Investments

title: Westpac brings forward RBA rate cut forecasts, after one more hike
summary: Coles is in talks to buy Greencross, a pet-care business, from TPG Capital for about $4 billion. This move could impact investors by limiting their ability to invest in standalone pet care companies, raising concerns about competition in the market.
ticker_line: Coles eyes $4bn Greencross acquisition
author: David Rogers, Valerina Changarathil
heading: Investments

title: UniSuper to snub Firmus float over lack of detail
summary: UniSuper, Australia's fourth-largest pension fund, will not invest in Firmus Technologies due to concerns over a lack of information about the company's business. Firmus, valued at $15.5 billion and backed by Nvidia, is facing skepticism about its planned IPO and ambitious revenue targets.
ticker_line: UniSuper doubts Firmus Technologies' IPO plans
author: Lucas Baird, Jenny Wiggins and Alex
heading: Investments

title: Stock picking: Aussie AI trade at risk from overcrowding
summary: Australian fund managers are increasingly investing in smaller tech companies that support AI infrastructure, but this trend may be risky as the market becomes overcrowded. Despite some recent declines in stock prices, experts believe the demand for AI-related services will continue to grow, especially in the resources sector like copper.
ticker_line: Aussie fund managers chase crowded AI stocks
author: Alex Gluyas
heading: Investments

title: Hanson offers an ‘eternity of pain’
summary: Angus Taylor, the Liberal leader, warns that a One Nation government would worsen Australia's economy, increasing inflation and debt. He criticizes their policies as unfunded and potentially harmful, while Senator Hanson’s team dismisses his claims as ineffective.
ticker_line: Taylor warns of economic pain under One Nation
author: GREG BROWN, Chief Political Corresp
heading: Economy

title: Zurich’s Australian P&C profit dips
summary: Zurich's Australian property and casualty profit fell to $US70 million in the first half of 2026, down from $US81 million last year, due to higher loss ratios. However, the overall Asia-Pacific P&C business saw a profit increase, and the life insurance sector performed better with a profit of $US70 million.
ticker_line: Zurich's Australian P&C profit declines in H1 2026
heading: General Insurance

title: Inquiry reviews PI options for solicitors
summary: A NSW parliamentary committee is looking into ways to increase competition in the market for solicitors' professional indemnity insurance, currently dominated by Lawcover. The inquiry will assess pricing differences and the potential for new providers to enter the market, following concerns that NSW solicitors pay more than those in Victoria.
ticker_line: NSW committee explores competition in legal insurance
heading: Regulation

title: Calvary Health Care considers new Launceston hospital at aged care site
summary: Calvary Health Care is considering building a new private hospital in Launceston, Tasmania, at its aged care site, after previously cancelling a $130 million project. This comes amid concerns over the aging infrastructure of its existing hospitals in the area.
ticker_line: Calvary plans new hospital in Launceston
author: investigative Emily Smith
heading: Health Insurance

title: Is pet insurance worth it?
summary: Pet insurance can help cover high vet bills, but many pet owners find it expensive and complex. Alternatives like saving for pet expenses directly may be a better option for some.
ticker_line: Is pet insurance worth the cost?
author: Kellie Scott
heading: General Insurance

title: Bulk billing on the rise as 1400 GP clinics ditch patient fees
summary: Bulk billing rates for GP visits have increased to 84.1% as over 1400 clinics switch to this model, thanks to the Albanese government's Medicare incentives. However, some practices still struggle with costs, and concerns have been raised about pressure on clinics to bulk bill.
ticker_line: Bulk billing rises as 1400 clinics go fee-free
author: Michelle Griffin | Federal bureau c
heading: Health Insurance

title: AFR Property Summit 2026: RBA sees housing slump but no 'recession'
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia's Sarah Hunter says the housing market slump is affecting the economy but won't lead to a recession. Despite falling home values and a potential interest rate rise, she believes consumer spending will only slow slightly.
ticker_line: RBA warns of housing slump impact on economy
author: John Kehoe | Economics with
heading: Economy

title: Budget to be $15b better due to super: Chalmers
summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers announced that Australia's budget will save $15 billion a year due to more people funding their own retirements through superannuation. He warned that proposed changes to the compulsory super rate could harm future generations, as both One Nation and the Coalition consider policies to allow early access to super funds.
ticker_line: Chalmers warns against changes to superannuation
author: Phillip Coorey | Political
heading: Superannuation

title: Firefighter challenges super fund benefit 'error'
summary: Firefighter Grant Williams is challenging the ESSSuper pension fund, claiming it has made errors in calculating retirement benefits for emergency service workers, potentially costing them significant money. He is seeking greater transparency and has taken the issue to a tribunal after raising concerns about inaccuracies in the fund's data and calculations.
ticker_line: Firefighter disputes retirement benefit calculations
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Superannuation

title: Taylor’s $4bn plan sits on shelf
summary: Angus Taylor has a $4 billion plan to allow Australians to access part of their superannuation for home ownership, but it has been put on hold after he replaced Sussan Ley as leader. The plan aimed to help fund tax cuts and was designed to avoid criticism of being a 'raid on super'.
ticker_line: Taylor's $4bn superannuation plan on hold
author: Geoff Chambers, Political , E
heading: Superannuation

title: Big stick to tame Big Tech
summary: New laws in Australia will require online platforms to protect users under 18 from harmful content and give them choices about their social media feeds. Companies that fail to comply could face fines over $200 million, and the eSafety Commissioner will gain new powers to take down harmful sites.
ticker_line: Australia introduces strict rules for online safety
author: Ellen Ransley
heading: Regulation

title: Chalmers steps in: ATO credit card ban delayed after business uproar
summary: The Australian Taxation Office's ban on credit card payments has been delayed until June 2027 after Treasurer Jim Chalmers intervened due to strong opposition from businesses. The government will provide additional funds to cover transaction costs while allowing more time for consultation with small businesses.
ticker_line: ATO credit card ban delayed amid business backlash
author: Nick Newling
heading: Regulation

title: In-house super fund teams cost more and return less, study finds
summary: A study shows that superannuation funds managing investments in-house have performed worse and cost more than those using external managers. This trend raises concerns about the effectiveness of internal management in the $4.7 trillion super sector.
ticker_line: In-house super funds cost more, return less
author: Lucas Baird and Jonathan Shapiro
heading: Superannuation

title: Insurance giant Hollard fined $2m after claim delays leave house uninhabitable
summary: Hollard Insurance has been fined $2 million for delays in processing a home insurance claim, which left a couple's house in regional Victoria uninhabitable. The delays included poor communication and ignoring expert advice, leading to significant damage that required the home to be demolished.
ticker_line: Hollard fined $2 million for claim delays
author: business Adelaide Miller
heading: General Insurance

title: Labor ministers on different pages over credit card ban
summary: Labor ministers are divided over the ATO's decision to stop accepting credit card payments for tax bills, which has upset small businesses. The ATO argues it cannot absorb the fees, while some ministers urge for more consultation with affected businesses.
ticker_line: Labor ministers clash over ATO credit card ban
author: Brittany Busch
heading: Regulation

title: ASIC issues stop orders against trio of private-lending funds
summary: The Australian Securities & Investments Commission (ASIC) has stopped three private-lending funds managed by Australian Secure Capital Fund due to concerns that retail investors were misled about loan portfolios and exit costs. The funds, which manage about $250 million, are now prohibited from selling or transferring interests until further notice.
ticker_line: ASIC halts three private-lending funds over investor concerns
author: Cliona O’Dowd
heading: Regulation

title: ANZ stands up an 'enterprise AI control plane'
summary: ANZ has introduced an enterprise AI control plane to oversee how staff and AI agents use models, tools and platforms, with limits designed to keep people in control. CEO Nuno Matos said the bank is targeting AI projects with clear benefits, including in customer service and engineering; ANZ reported a cash profit of $7.59 billion for the year to 30 September, up 31 per cent.
ticker_line: ANZ sets central controls as it expands AI use
author: Ry Crozier
heading: AI

title: ASIC turns up heat on cold callers targeting super
summary: ASIC found 15 advice firms collected $9.8 million in upfront fees from 7,639 clients referred by cold callers between early 2025 and mid-2026, with clients agreeing to another $4.5 million in annual fees. The regulator warned that callers made potentially misleading claims and sometimes gave advice without a licence, as the government considers banning unlicensed lead generators and consumer advocates call for a ban on lead generation for super switching.
ticker_line: ASIC warns over cold callers steering super switches
author: Cliona O’Dowd
heading: Superannuation

title: Regulation: ASIC warns of super lead generation sale scams
summary: ASIC has warned Australians about lead generators who use calls and social media ads to persuade people to review or switch their super, sometimes directing them to risky investments. In a review of 15 financial services licensees, more than 7,600 new clients invested nearly $680 million after lead-generation referrals in the first half of 2025; ASIC says people should be wary of pressure to move their super and seek advice from a qualified professional they contact themselves.
ticker_line: ASIC warns Australians about super switching scams
author: Millie Muroi
heading: Superannuation

title: Three times the rebate, way above inflation: the medical specialties with sky-high fees
summary: Grattan Institute says specialist fees rose 4 per cent faster than inflation over the past year, with some patients paying sharply higher charges; more than 800,000 Australians skip or delay specialist care each year because of the cost. It wants the government to review Medicare fees and make the small group of specialists charging extreme fees repay their rebates, while the Australian Medical Association says years of government underfunding have contributed to the problem.
ticker_line: Grattan urges action on soaring specialist fees
author: Brittany Busch | Federal political
heading: Regulation

title: NSW at the highest risk in looming bushfire season
summary: NSW has eight of Australia’s 10 highest-risk bushfire hotspots, with Batemans Bay, Gosford, Wyong and Shoalhaven ranked as the top four, according to insurer GIO. Forecasters warn the 2026–27 summer could be exceptionally hot as El Niño raises fire danger in eastern Australia, and say hot, dry and windy weather could quickly increase local risks.
ticker_line: NSW dominates national bushfire hotspot rankings
author: Elliott Stewart
heading: General Insurance

title: AAMI driver app could drop claims by $4.2m
summary: Suncorp says its AAMI driving app campaign could cut motor insurance claims by $4.2 million a year, after attracting nearly 140,000 app downloads and 500,000 website visits. The app gives drivers feedback and rewards safer habits; early results show the biggest improvements among people with the lowest scores, while Suncorp plans to keep tracking behaviour and expand the program.
ticker_line: AAMI app targets $4.2m annual claims reduction
author: Danielle Long
heading: General Insurance

title: Cooks River AI data centre axed after outcry
summary: Stockland has removed a proposed AI data centre from its Kogarah Golf Course redevelopment plan after strong community opposition. The revised plan will focus on a logistics hub; the proposal drew 593 objections among 665 submissions, amid wider concern about the power, water and noise demands of data centres.
ticker_line: Stockland drops Cooks River AI data centre plan
author: Eryk Bagshaw with Jessica McSweeney
heading: AI

title: Aussies slugged for woke studies
summary: The Daily Telegraph reports that the Albanese government has spent more than $10 million through Australian Research Council fellowships on studies covering topics such as AI and spirituality, ethical influencers and the political right. Coalition spokesman Tony Pasin called some projects wasteful, while the ARC said grants undergo a rigorous, competitive assessment process and support research across many fields.
ticker_line: Coalition questions $10m in research grants
author: Linda Silmalis
heading: Economy

title: Ad giant reveals new AI road map
summary: WPP’s Australian leaders say businesses are nearing a turning point in AI use, with its WPP Open system combining data, creative, media and technology to find new customers and support growth—not just cut costs. They say trust, poor integration between the many AI tools and the need for useful, engaging customer communications remain key challenges.
ticker_line: WPP says AI can help brands find new customers
author: Danielle Long
heading: AI

title: Next RBA move will be rate cut, but timing’s uncertain: NAB
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook announced new AI features for Siri at his last Worldwide Developers Conference, but shares fell nearly 2% as no major surprises were revealed. The new Siri will have enhanced capabilities and a new look, but some features will be limited by cost and geography.
ticker_line: Apple unveils new Siri features, shares drop
author: Valerina Changarathil
heading: AI

title: CBA scrambles, new $1.4 trillion bombshell
summary: The AI industry is buzzing as OpenAI and Anthropic take steps to go public, which is causing a surge in interest from Australian investors, overwhelming Commonwealth Bank’s CommSec platform. This comes as SpaceX prepares for a historic IPO that could create many new billionaires.
ticker_line: AI frenzy sparks investor rush in Australia
author: Ben Graham
heading: Investments

title: Medical imaging provider to investigate improper Medicare billing allegations
summary: Integral Diagnostics will investigate claims of improper Medicare billing at Kalgoorlie Health Campus after concerns were raised about incorrect practices. The WA health minister has referred the matter to the state's corruption watchdog for further examination.
ticker_line: Investigation into Medicare billing practices launched
heading: Health Insurance

title: ‘Gut punch’ warning over the new rates reality
summary: Australian mortgage holders face permanently higher interest rates due to ongoing economic shocks, according to Oxford Economics. Despite recent inflation drops, the Reserve Bank is expected to keep rates steady for now as the economy slows.
ticker_line: Mortgage holders brace for higher interest rates
author: Cameron Micallef
heading: Economy

title: Minister on board to slow AI juggernaut
summary: The Australian government supports Anthropic's call for a global pause in AI development to address safety concerns, as the company warns of risks from advanced AI that can improve itself. Assistant Minister Andrew Charlton emphasizes the need for careful regulation and safety measures as AI technology rapidly evolves.
ticker_line: Government backs Anthropic's AI safety push
author: Jared Lynch
heading: AI

title: Should older workers still be expected to do night shifts?
summary: The article discusses whether older hospital workers should be exempt from night shifts due to the increasing demands of after-hours work. Experts suggest balancing fairness and safety, advocating for a management approach that considers age without stereotyping abilities.
ticker_line: Debate on night shifts for older hospital workers
author: Jonathan Rivett
heading: Health Insurance

title: A $565 insurance saving in the regions could sting rich households
summary: NSW plans to save flood-prone households $565 a year on insurance by shifting costs to high-value properties, which could lead to richer households paying more. The Insurance Council supports this change to a fairer land tax system.
ticker_line: NSW proposes insurance savings for flood-prone areas
author: Paul Karp
heading: General Insurance

title: Super funds told to get behind Indian growth
summary: Billionaire Robin Khuda urges Australia's $4.5 trillion superannuation sector to invest more in India, highlighting its rapid economic growth and potential. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Melbourne aims to strengthen business ties between Australia and India.
ticker_line: Super funds encouraged to invest in India
author: Patrick Durkin
heading: Investments

title: Angus Taylor says One Nation policies would bring 'eternity of pain' to economy
summary: Opposition leader Angus Taylor criticises One Nation's economic plan, claiming it could cost Australia a trillion dollars and lead to higher interest rates and national debt. He warns that if Pauline Hanson gains power, it would result in significant economic pain for Australians.
ticker_line: Taylor warns One Nation policies could harm economy
author: political Holly Tregenza
heading: Economy

title: Industry urges Albanese government to relent on its ban on SMSF loans
summary: The Albanese government faces pressure to reconsider its ban on new self-managed super fund (SMSF) loans for residential property, which could negatively impact the housing market and construction projects. Industry experts argue that the ban contradicts the government's goals for increasing housing supply and may lead SMSFs to invest more in established properties instead of new developments.
ticker_line: Pressure mounts on government over SMSF loan ban
author: Harrison Astbury
heading: Superannuation

title: ‘Don’t pick winners’: Future Fund reveals blueprint for AI investing
summary: The Future Fund, Australia's $330 billion investment manager, is cautious about investing in AI, choosing to diversify its portfolio across various tech sectors instead of picking specific winners. CEO Raphael Arndt warns that while AI presents significant opportunities, it is too volatile and uncertain to make high-stakes bets at this time.
ticker_line: Future Fund diversifies AI investments amid uncertainty
author: Eric Johnston
heading: Investments

title: Labor ‘knew of negative equity risks in 5pc plan’
summary: Internal Treasury documents show that the Albanese government's 5% home deposit scheme may expose first-home buyers to higher risks of negative equity due to high loan-to-value ratios. Critics argue this could worsen the housing market and lead to financial strain for borrowers if property prices fall.
ticker_line: Treasury warns of risks in 5% deposit scheme
author: GEOFF CHAMBERS, NOAH YIM
heading: Economy

title: Domestic inflation ‘a key risk’ for RBA
summary: Domestic inflation is a major concern for the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) as local cost pressures rise, despite a stronger Australian dollar making imports cheaper. Economists warn that inflation remains above the RBA's target, with housing costs and wages contributing to ongoing inflation risks.
ticker_line: RBA faces rising domestic inflation risks
author: Matthew Cranston
heading: Economy

title: Cold calling at top of Mulino’s super hit list
summary: The federal government is set to announce reforms on August 19 to protect Australians from bad superannuation practices, including a ban on cold calling and changes to a compensation scheme for victims of financial misconduct, following a $1 billion scandal affecting over 11,000 people.
ticker_line: Government to ban cold calling in superannuation
author: Cliona O’Dowd
heading: Superannuation

title: True scale of Labor’s public service expansion revealed
summary: The Labor government has significantly increased the number of public servants since 2022, focusing on regulation while being slow to adopt artificial intelligence, leading to concerns about productivity and efficiency. Opposition parties are calling for cuts to what they see as wasteful bureaucracy.
ticker_line: Labor expands public service amid productivity concerns
author: GEOFF CHAMBERS
heading: Regulation

title: More than 15.5 million Australians will have no say in who inherits their superannuation
summary: More than 15.5 million Australians have not set up a legally binding nomination for their superannuation, which can lead to disputes over who inherits the funds. A recent case highlights the confusion and emotional stress when super funds decide payouts based on their own rules rather than the deceased's wishes.
ticker_line: Millions lack binding superannuation nominations
author: business Nassim Khadem
heading: Superannuation

title: Super-sized political battle: Chalmers issues warning on ‘existential threat’
summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers warns that the next election will be crucial for the future of superannuation, as he reveals that the cost of the age pension will decrease even with 9 million people retiring in the next 40 years. He argues that Australia's superannuation system is helping to keep pension costs low compared to other countries.
ticker_line: Chalmers warns of superannuation's future at election
author: Shane Wright
heading: Superannuation

title: ‘Top priority’: RBA signals more rate hikes needed
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) plans to raise interest rates again before Christmas to combat rising inflation, with a potential hike expected in November. This comes as the ASX 200 falls and consumer confidence declines amid increasing oil prices and a struggling housing market.
ticker_line: RBA signals more rate hikes ahead
author: David Rogers
heading: Economy

title: ‘Speed, ecstasy, and marijuana. Ice is not on that list’: Pickering details drug use
summary: One Nation's Barnaby Joyce faced tough questions about a plan to let renters and mortgage holders access part of their superannuation early. Economists warn this could worsen inflation and cost-of-living issues.
ticker_line: Joyce grilled over superannuation access plan
author: David Tanner, Thomas Henry, Aris Sc
heading: Superannuation

title: Choosi misled customers on insurer range, Federal Court rules
summary: The article text is unavailable, so the details of the Federal Court’s ruling and its consequences cannot be confirmed. The headline says the court found Choosi misled customers about the range of insurers it offered.
ticker_line: Court finds Choosi misled customers on insurer range
author: Gladys Jalipa
heading: General Insurance

title: Parts crunch writes off cars early, jacks up premiums
summary: Delays in getting car parts are causing insurers to write off easily repairable cars, leading to higher insurance premiums for all drivers. The situation is worsened by the complexity of modern vehicles and the lack of timely access to replacement parts.
ticker_line: Parts shortages drive up car insurance costs
author: Elias Visontay | National consumer
heading: General Insurance

title: How Big Tech is likely to respond
summary: The Australian government is considering a new digital duty-of-care bill that could change how social media algorithms work, potentially leading to paid subscriptions or lower quality content. Experts warn that an 'opt-in' model might not effectively protect vulnerable users, especially children.
ticker_line: Government plans changes to social media algorithms
author: JARED LYNCH TECHNOLOGY
heading: Regulation

title: RBA 'caught off guard' by inflation
summary: Former RBA board member Ian Harper said the Reserve Bank of Australia was surprised by rising inflation last year. He warned that interest rates could increase again before the end of 2026 as the bank adjusts its approach to short-term inflation expectations.
ticker_line: RBA may raise rates again amid inflation concerns
author: Lea Jurkovic
heading: Economy

title: Australia exposed to economic shocks: S&P
summary: S&P Global warns that Australia's high government spending and ongoing budget deficits make the economy vulnerable to shocks, like falling mining revenues. The report highlights concerns over rising debt costs and reduced state revenue from the housing market slump.
ticker_line: S&P warns Australia faces economic vulnerabilities
author: John Kehoe
heading: Economy

title: Banks propose regional hubs to kill levy threat
summary: Australia's major banks plan to create regional banking hubs in up to 10 towns without branches to maintain face-to-face services and avoid a government levy. The Australian Banking Association seeks approval from the ACCC for this initiative, which aims to support regional communities amid declining bank branches.
ticker_line: Banks propose hubs to avoid regional levy threat
author: Jack Derwin
heading: Banking

title: Locally run AI models could do 90pc of tasks for cheaper: inquiry
summary: Tech leaders say Australia could use cheaper, locally trained AI models for up to 90% of tasks, but the country is lagging in investment compared to others. They urge the government to support local AI development instead of relying on foreign companies.
ticker_line: Australia urged to boost local AI investment
author: Ronald Mizen | Political correspond
heading: AI

title: 'Group of individuals' impacted by data breach at SA hospital
summary: St Andrew's Hospital in Adelaide has reported a data breach affecting some individuals, with personal information downloaded from its servers. The hospital is working with authorities to investigate and improve security measures.
ticker_line: Adelaide hospital reports personal data breach
heading: Health Insurance

title: Australia outlines plans to make AI companies prove their safety systems work
summary: Australia plans new laws requiring AI companies to prove their safety systems work, similar to regulations in banking and aviation. This move comes after incidents highlighting the risks of AI, aiming to ensure companies can effectively manage and prevent harm.
ticker_line: Australia to enforce AI safety regulations
author: chief digital political corresponde
heading: Regulation

title: Questionable sales tactics prompting Aussies to switch super
summary: ASIC found that unlicensed telemarketers helped 15 financial advice firms attract 7,639 clients between January 2025 and June 2026, leading to about $678 million being switched or invested—around 90 per cent from super savings. The regulator said some lead generators used misleading or high-pressure tactics and went beyond referrals, while several firms lacked proper controls; ASIC warned it may take enforcement action where consumers were seriously harmed.
ticker_line: ASIC flags risky super switching and sales tactics
author: business Nassim Khadem
heading: Superannuation

title: Australians less satisfied with life than during pandemic as financial pressures mount
summary: Australians are feeling less satisfied with life now than during the COVID-19 pandemic, mainly due to rising financial pressures. Data shows life satisfaction dropped from 7.2 out of 10 in 2020 to 7.1 last year, with many struggling to manage costs and save money.
ticker_line: Australians report lower life satisfaction amid financial stress
author: business Daniel Ziffer
heading: Economy

title: Long delays leave Tasmanians waiting for surgery amid worries about $700m in health cuts
summary: Tasmania's elective surgery waitlist has reached about 9,500 people, with many waiting years for procedures. The state government plans to cut $702 million from health services over four years, raising concerns about the impact on patient care and service delivery.
ticker_line: Tasmania faces health cuts amid surgery delays
author: state political Josh Dugga
heading: Health

title: Data centre boom towns ride the economic wave, but can it last?
summary: Victoria and NSW are experiencing a massive data centre boom, investing nearly $300 billion, surpassing the previous mining boom. However, experts warn that this growth may not lead to long-term economic benefits for Australians and could face challenges ahead.
ticker_line: Data centre boom surpasses mining investment in Australia
author: Shane Wright | Senior economics cor
heading: Economy

title: Westpac extends ‘DIDO’ banking
summary: Westpac is expanding its drive-in-drive-out banking service to six new towns in Queensland, aiming to provide in-person banking in areas without branches. The bank will also invest $10 million to improve branches in regional Queensland.
ticker_line: Westpac expands DIDO banking to Queensland towns
author: David Ross
heading: Banking

title: NEW RESEARCH REVEALS HIDDEN SCALE OF CHILD HOMELESSNESS
summary: New research shows over 33,000 children in Aotearoa face severe housing deprivation, leading to higher risks of school absence, illness, and contact with the justice system. The Coalition to End Women’s Homelessness highlights the need for housing solutions, especially for mothers, to support these vulnerable children.
ticker_line: Over 33,000 children face severe housing issues
author: Amelia Wade
heading: General Insurance

title: Data centres an inflation threat: RBA
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia is worried that the rapid growth of data centre investments could lead to competition for workers and resources, making it harder to control inflation and keep interest rates down. With tech companies investing heavily, including a $21.6 billion plan by Anthropic for data centre capacity, the RBA fears this could worsen existing skills shortages and capacity issues in the economy.
ticker_line: RBA warns data centres may fuel inflation
author: Luke Kinsella and Ronald Mizen
heading: Economy

title: Sharp fall in living standards
summary: A new OECD report shows Australians' living standards have sharply declined since the pandemic, with real wages down 5.1% since March 2021. High inflation is expected to cause further wage declines this year, complicating the government's economic recovery efforts.
ticker_line: Australians face sharp decline in living standards
author: Michael Read
heading: Economy

title: Banks still falling short, charging dead people, says watchdog
summary: A report by the Banking Code Compliance Committee found that three Australian banks are still not properly handling accounts of deceased customers, asking families for account details instead of searching their systems. If these banks do not improve, they may be reported to the corporate regulator.
ticker_line: Banks still charging fees to deceased customers
author: David Ross
heading: Banking

title: Downbeat Deloitte’s dire outlook
summary: Deloitte Access Economics predicts Australia's economy will face its longest period of low growth since the 1990s, with GDP expected to rise only 1.3% this financial year due to high inflation and interest rates. Business leaders warn that government policies are hurting investment and productivity, leading to concerns about future economic performance.
ticker_line: Deloitte warns of prolonged economic downturn
author: Thomas Henry, Perry Williams, Rosie
heading: Economy

title: Labor push for RBA to keep rates lower
summary: Labor party members are pushing to change the Reserve Bank's role to keep interest rates lower, as they face pressure from voters shifting to One Nation. Treasurer Jim Chalmers is managing this proposal ahead of the party's conference, while maintaining support for the bank's independence.
ticker_line: Labor seeks to lower interest rates amid voter shift
author: Paul Sakkal | Chief political corre
heading: Economy

title: Overlooked reason CBA’s share price keeps defying the sceptics
summary: Commonwealth Bank's share price remains high despite many analysts recommending to sell, as active fund managers are buying to avoid underperformance. The upcoming results on August 12 could impact future valuations and investor sentiment.
ticker_line: CBA's share price defies analyst skepticism
author: CHRIS BRYCKI, ANALYSIS
heading: Banking

title: Spike in Cats’ indemnity bill in year of player pact
summary: The Geelong AFL club's insurance costs for protecting directors nearly doubled to $80,319 in 2024, coinciding with a controversial waiver signed by player Jake Kolodjashnij regarding concussion risks. The AFL will not penalise Geelong, which has since cancelled the secret agreement.
ticker_line: Geelong AFL club faces scrutiny over insurance costs
author: Joseph Carbone
heading: General Insurance

title: Employment: Coles to outsource several hundred jobs to India
summary: Coles plans to outsource several hundred back-office jobs to India as part of a cost-cutting deal with Accenture. This move is part of a trend among Australian companies to manage costs amid digital changes, but it will not affect store staff.
ticker_line: Coles to outsource hundreds of jobs to India
author: Jessica Yun
heading: Economy

title: ‘Disastrous’: Inflation warnings on Hanson’s early access super plan
summary: One Nation's plan to let renters and mortgage holders access part of their superannuation early could inject $26 billion into the economy, but economists warn it will worsen inflation and hurt retirement savings. Critics argue the policy is poorly targeted and will not effectively address cost-of-living issues.
ticker_line: Hanson's super access plan sparks inflation fears
author: Thomas Henry
heading: Superannuation

title: Australia to export AI compute as data centre demand surges
summary: Australia is set to export AI computing power as demand for data centres grows, mainly driven by American tech companies. Local leaders stress the importance of ensuring that communities benefit from these developments, including job creation and tax revenue.
ticker_line: Australia to boost AI compute exports amid demand surge
author: Jenny Wiggins
heading: AI

title: Insurance Advisernet reveals award winners
summary: Insurance Advisernet held its first combined conference in Sydney, announcing award winners for Australia and New Zealand. Zurich was named Australian insurer of the year, while Market Lane topped the agency category, and over $200,000 was raised for charity during the event.
ticker_line: Insurance Advisernet announces award winners in Sydney
heading: General Insurance

title: SRG training scheme casts wider net in hunt for talent
summary: Specialist Risk Group has started a 12-week training program to attract professionals from consulting, legal, audit, and accounting backgrounds into insurance broking. The program includes formal study and practical experience, aiming to develop brokers who understand clients' businesses better.
ticker_line: SRG launches new training program for brokers
heading: General Insurance

title: Strata agency, Allianz strengthen tie-up
summary: Allianz Australia has extended its distribution agreement with Strata Community Insurance until at least 2036, showing its commitment to the growing strata insurance market. This partnership aims to improve insurance solutions for strata communities across Australia.
ticker_line: Allianz extends strata insurance partnership to 2036
heading: General Insurance

title: AFCA backs insurer on hardship help, policy cancellation
summary: The Australian Financial Complaints Authority ruled that Hannover Life Re lawfully cancelled a death and funeral insurance policy due to unpaid premiums. The insurer had provided multiple chances for the policyholder to reinstate the policy before her death in December 2023.
ticker_line: AFCA supports insurer's policy cancellation decision
heading: Life Insurance

title: ‘Worst own goal’: No Labor modelling of SMSF property ban
summary: Labor's decision to ban self-managed super funds from borrowing for property has raised concerns about its impact on housing supply, with critics calling it a major mistake. The government did not assess how this policy would affect the housing market before implementing it, leading to warnings of reduced home building and higher rents.
ticker_line: Labor's SMSF property ban sparks housing supply fears
author: Greg Brown
heading: Superannuation

title: Pauline’s super easy pitch to households
summary: One Nation, led by Pauline Hanson, proposes a policy allowing Australians to divert 25% of their super contributions into take-home pay for three years. This aims to help renters and mortgage holders cope with rising living costs, potentially providing significant extra income.
ticker_line: One Nation proposes super fund diversion for households
author: Jason Morrison
heading: Superannuation

title: Students head for country as AI bites
summary: As AI reduces entry-level jobs, more young Australians like Annalise Magill are choosing careers in agriculture, which is facing a worker shortage. The sector is evolving with new technology and offers diverse roles, making it more appealing to students.
ticker_line: Young Australians flock to agriculture careers amid AI changes
author: Sally Rawsthorne
heading: AI

title: Victoria is facing a $3b-a-year debt bomb
summary: Victoria is facing a significant budget crisis with rising debt and interest costs, projected to add $3.1 billion annually as COVID-era loans are refinanced at higher rates. The state's financial situation is worsened by a downturn in the property market and increased borrowing needs ahead of the upcoming election.
ticker_line: Victoria's debt crisis deepens with rising interest rates
author: Sumeyya Ilanbey
heading: Economy

title: Medicare hack claim on dark web probed
summary: Services Australia and law enforcement are investigating claims that a hacker is selling 25 million Medicare files on the dark web. A sample of the data has been posted, but officials believe it may be recycled information from previous breaches, not directly from Medicare systems.
ticker_line: Investigation into Medicare data breach claims underway
author: Nicola Smith | Defence corresponden
heading: Health Insurance

title: Mortgage refinancing game has changed
summary: Mortgage refinancing is expected to rise as higher rates put pressure on household budgets, but banks are increasingly waiting until customers formally start leaving before offering a better deal. Experts say borrowers should compare the full costs and consider options such as extending their loan term or using an offset account, while noting these can mean paying more interest or taking on extra debt.
ticker_line: Refinancing rises as higher rates squeeze households
author: James Kirby, Associate – Wea
heading: Banking

title: Record super raid for dental work leaves holes in savings
summary: Australians withdrew $892 million from super for dental treatment in 2025-26, up 421 per cent from 2021-22, with more than half of compassionate-release approvals going to dental patients. Advisers warn withdrawals can sharply reduce retirement savings, while the ATO is targeting alleged fraud and calls are growing for stronger safeguards and better access to public dental care.
ticker_line: Dental super withdrawals surge, putting retirement savings at risk
author: Anthony Keane
heading: Superannuation

title: Australia’s data centre explosion: Why the surge in NSW, Victoria is now eclipsing the mining boom
summary: NSW and Victoria are experiencing a massive surge in data centre investments, surpassing the previous mining boom with nearly $300 billion spent in the past year. While this growth is expected to boost the economy, concerns remain about its long-term benefits and potential risks.
ticker_line: Data centre boom outpaces mining investment in Australia
author: Shane Wright
heading: Economy

title: Strata giant unmasked in secret lobbying to save insurance kickbacks
summary: PICA Group, Australia's largest strata company, secretly lobbied against a ban on insurance kickbacks, claiming it would threaten 70% of strata management firms. The government has not yet banned these kickbacks but is considering further studies on the issue.
ticker_line: PICA Group lobbies against insurance kickback ban
author: Rachael Dexter
heading: Regulation

title: AI is coming for these 82 Aussie jobs
summary: Deloitte warns that 82 Australian jobs are at high risk from AI disruption in 2026, predicting job growth will slow significantly due to economic conditions and AI advancements. While some companies have already cut jobs, overall employment in affected sectors is still growing, though at a reduced rate.
ticker_line: Deloitte warns of AI job risks in Australia
author: Heath Parkes-Hupton
heading: AI

title: Victorian teachers in class action over alleged unpaid superannuation
summary: Victorian teachers, led by Jill Perkins, are suing the Department of Education for unpaid superannuation on a salary allowance from 1995 to 2023, claiming a total loss of $400 million. The Australian Education Union argues this payment should have included superannuation contributions, which the department is currently appealing in court.
ticker_line: Victorian teachers sue for unpaid superannuation
author: story by Sacha Payne
heading: Superannuation

title: Federal government accused of AI policy retreat as US tech giants plan Australian investments
summary: The Australian government has backed away from strict AI regulations, which has raised concerns about safety as major tech companies plan significant investments in the country. Critics argue that the decision could have serious implications for consumer protection and privacy.
ticker_line: Government retreats on AI safety regulations
author: Steve Cannane, Lesley Robinson, Lar
heading: Regulation

title: Closing the AI skills gap is not just a hiring problem
summary: Australian organisations need to improve AI skills within their workforce, not just hire new talent. A more integrated approach in education and ongoing training is essential to close the skills gap and effectively implement AI solutions.
ticker_line: Australia urged to boost AI skills development
author: Andrew Foo
heading: AI

title: Labor pivots to AI intervention
summary: The Albanese government plans to impose stricter rules on data centres, requiring them to benefit local communities and add to the electricity grid. This move aims to address public concerns about AI's impact on jobs and the economy ahead of the upcoming ALP National Conference.
ticker_line: Labor to enforce new rules on data centres
author: Ronald Mizen | Political correspond
heading: AI

title: Shock inflation ranking
summary: Australia's inflation rate has reached the second-highest in the world at 3.6% for the year to May, causing concerns for homeowners facing rising mortgage rates. Experts warn that the Reserve Bank of Australia may increase interest rates in August due to ongoing inflation pressures.
ticker_line: Australia's inflation hits second-highest globally
author: Cameron Micallef
heading: Economy

title: Price tumbles spread to all capital cities
summary: House prices are falling across all Australian capital cities, with forecasts predicting a decline of up to 8% by the end of 2027. High interest rates and changes to property tax laws are discouraging first home buyers from entering the market during this downturn.
ticker_line: House prices drop nationwide amid economic uncertainty
author: Thomas Henry Noah Yim
heading: Economy

title: Bosses warn on ‘heavy-handed’ union AI role
summary: Australia's largest employer groups warn that Labor's new AI policies, influenced by unions, could harm productivity and competitiveness. They argue that union involvement in AI decisions may slow down business innovation and investment.
ticker_line: Employers warn unions may hinder AI progress
author: Noah Yim
heading: AI

title: ‘Can’t let it control us’: Taylor’s vow of AI vigilance
summary: Opposition Leader Angus Taylor has called for careful management of artificial intelligence to prevent job losses and protect Australian creators' rights. He believes AI can boost productivity and wages but warns against letting it dominate our lives.
ticker_line: Taylor calls for balanced approach to AI
author: Joseph Olbrycht-Palmer
heading: AI

title: AMP’s latest buyback signals CFS is now off the table
summary: AMP has announced a $150 million share buyback and a 3 cent interim dividend, suggesting it is not planning to acquire Colonial First State. The company continues to seek a buyer for its banking division but is facing challenges due to pricing issues.
ticker_line: AMP signals no deal for Colonial First State
author: DATA ROOM WITH BRIDGET CARTER
heading: Banking

title: Cannabis laws could make insurance high
summary: The NSW government is changing drug driving laws for medical cannabis users, which may increase car insurance costs. Critics are concerned about the lack of cost analysis and potential risks to road safety.
ticker_line: New cannabis laws may raise insurance costs
author: James O’Doherty, State Po
heading: Regulation

title: Westpac eyes Wall Street-style loan carve-up to work balance sheet
summary: Westpac is planning to sell parts of its loan book to private credit firms and super funds, aiming to free up capital and attract investors. The bank has hired former Goldman Sachs banker Rob Taylor to lead this strategy, which is inspired by successful practices in the US and Europe.
ticker_line: Westpac to sell loans to private credit investors
author: James Eyers
heading: Banking

title: CBA targeted over deforestation-linked loans
summary: Commonwealth Bank faces pressure from investors to improve transparency on loans linked to deforestation, with a resolution to be voted on at its annual meeting on October 14. The Australian Conservation Foundation reports significant deforestation associated with CBA's agricultural loans, urging the bank to adopt more sustainable practices.
ticker_line: CBA urged to address deforestation in loans
author: James Eyers
heading: Banking

title: Banks: NAB profit falls to $6.1b as recession fears grow
summary: NAB’s annual profit fell 9 per cent to $6.14 billion, while bad-debt charges rose and home loan repayments overdue by at least 30 days increased to 1.69 per cent. Chief executive Andrew Irvine said recession risks had grown and economic growth could slow to about 1 per cent next year, though mortgage stress remained low by historical standards; NAB shares fell 5.4 per cent.
ticker_line: NAB profit falls as recession and bad-debt risks rise
author: Millie Muroi
heading: Banking

title: Date centres should be built in planned precincts, inquiry finds
summary: A NSW parliamentary inquiry says data centres should be built in planned precincts with shared power and water infrastructure, rather than clustering in suburbs such as Lane Cove and Ryde. It made 23 recommendations, including stronger checks on combined impacts and community concerns, after criticising fast-track approvals; NSW has more than 60 data centres operating or being built.
ticker_line: Inquiry urges planned precincts for NSW data centres
author: Jessica McSweeney
heading: AI

title: AustralianSuper given sector's first AAA rating
summary: AustralianSuper has become the first super fund to receive a AAA credit rating from Moody’s, matching the federal government’s rating and ranking above some state governments and major banks. The $438 billion fund expects the rating to cut investment and trading costs by more than $250 million by 2035, as it grows to serve more than 5 million members.
ticker_line: AustralianSuper secures first AAA rating for a super fund
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Superannuation

title: ART super fund opens equities unit
summary: Australian Retirement Trust, a $370 billion super fund, will launch an in-house equities desk early next year to take part directly in share sales and other deals, aiming to buy shares at a discount and support Australian companies. The team will be led by John Moorhead and includes former Jarden investment banking head Dane Fitzgibbon; ART says the move is not a broader shift away from its external investment managers.
ticker_line: ART builds team to buy shares directly in deals
author: Jonathan Shapiro and Lucas Baird
heading: Superannuation

title: Big business tells Labor to get a move on with AI
summary: Leaders from Wesfarmers, Telstra and BHP are urging the Albanese government to set clear AI rules quickly, warning delays or unnecessary hurdles could cost Australia investment and competitiveness. A parliamentary inquiry is due to report by the end of November and has backed investing in data centres and changing copyright laws to help AI developers train models in Australia.
ticker_line: Business leaders urge Labor to speed up AI rules
author: Zoe Samios | Technology
heading: AI

title: ANZ’s fixed rate shock
summary: ANZ has reduced its two and three-year fixed home loan rates by up to 0.10 percentage points, with the lowest rate now at 6.29%. This move is unusual as most major banks have been increasing their fixed rates recently.
ticker_line: ANZ cuts fixed home loan rates amid rising trends
heading: Banking

title: Anthropic urges AI freeze amid fear of losing control
summary: Anthropic, the top AI company, has called for a global pause on developing powerful AI systems, warning that humanity risks losing control. They are concerned about rapid advancements that could lead to dangerous outcomes and suggest that all major AI firms should agree to slow down their work.
ticker_line: Anthropic calls for global AI development freeze
author: David Swan | Technology
heading: AI

title: Business banking on boost from AI
summary: Australian business leaders, including executives from BHP and Uber, discussed how adopting artificial intelligence (AI) could improve productivity despite some challenges. They highlighted AI's potential to prevent costly shutdowns and create new job roles, while also acknowledging the current low productivity levels in Australia since the Covid-19 pandemic.
ticker_line: AI seen as key to boosting productivity
author: Jared Lynch, Perry Williams
heading: Economy

title: The one age at which you will pay more tax than any other
summary: People aged 43 pay the most tax in Australia, averaging $59,000 a year. This age group faces high taxes due to higher incomes and family expenses, while younger and older Australians benefit more from government spending.
ticker_line: Age 43 sees peak tax burden in Australia
author: Anthony Keane
heading: Economy

title: CBA warns of new hit to Australian economy
summary: Commonwealth Bank warns that falling house prices will slow Australia's economy, with GDP growth expected at just 1.5% for 2026. However, mortgage holders may benefit as the Reserve Bank is likely to keep interest rates steady for the rest of the year.
ticker_line: CBA forecasts economic slowdown due to housing market
author: Cameron Micallef
heading: Economy

title: Watchdog’s data ‘points to uneven liability market’
summary: The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority's updated data shows an uneven liability insurance market, with Lloyd's stable market share but declining premiums, especially in the construction sector, where costs have tripled in six years. The report highlights ongoing affordability issues for small businesses in this industry.
ticker_line: Liability insurance market shows uneven trends
heading: General Insurance

title: Trade-offs required as risk protection gap widens, researchers say
summary: A report from the University of Queensland highlights the growing gap in disaster insurance coverage due to increasing natural disasters. It suggests that insurance needs to adapt by supporting risk reduction efforts to remain sustainable and effective for society.
ticker_line: Insurance must adapt as disaster risks rise
heading: General Insurance

title: How insurer transformation reshaped the smash repair sector
summary: The Australian smash repair sector has shifted from oversupply to potential undersupply due to changes in the insurance industry, leading to longer repair times and workforce shortages. The average repair time increased from 38.57 days in 2019 to 61.25 days in 2024, highlighting the industry's growing fragility.
ticker_line: Smash repair sector faces undersupply crisis
author: Ron Arnold
heading: General Insurance

title: Awards recognise life advice
summary: The Financial Advice Association Australia has added a new risk adviser category to its awards, highlighting the importance of life insurance guidance. Sponsored by Zurich Australia, the awards are open for submissions until July 30, with winners announced on November 26 in Melbourne.
ticker_line: New award for life insurance advisers launched
heading: Life Insurance

title: Nation's inflation rate is highest in developed world
summary: Australia's inflation rate has reached the highest levels among developed countries, with core inflation at 3.6% in May. Economists criticize the Reserve Bank for not acting decisively enough to control rising prices, complicating the government's efforts to manage cost-of-living concerns.
ticker_line: Australia's inflation rate hits developed world high
author: Michael Read
heading: Economy

title: Economist survey: No rate cuts 'until 2027' as fourth rise looms
summary: Economists predict no interest rate cuts from the Reserve Bank of Australia until at least 2027, with a possible fourth rate rise still on the table due to ongoing inflation concerns and global tensions. The cash rate is currently at 4.35%, and many believe it will remain unchanged for the rest of the year.
ticker_line: No rate cuts expected until 2027
author: Grace Lagan
heading: Economy

title: Judge rules AI evidence 'bordered on contempt'
summary: A judge has warned that using AI to gather evidence in dismissal cases can lead to serious legal issues, as seen in a case where a delivery driver relied on a chatbot that created false evidence, resulting in his case being dismissed and potential penalties for him.
ticker_line: Judge warns against AI misuse in court cases
author: David Marin-Guzman | Workplace corr
heading: Regulation

title: Market minds: Why Australia is the world's most underappreciated AI trade
summary: Australia is becoming an important player in the global AI infrastructure market, with significant investments in data centres and power supply expected to grow. Companies like NextDC and Macquarie Technology are leading this growth, while resources like copper will be crucial for supporting AI's energy needs.
ticker_line: Australia emerges as key player in AI infrastructure
author: Jun Bei Liu
heading: Investments

title: Privatisation of essential services driving cost-of-living crisis
summary: A study by the McKell Institute shows that the rising cost of living in Australia is largely due to the privatisation of essential services, with prices for utilities, health, and education increasing much faster than general inflation over the past 20 years. Experts argue that restoring public services and better regulating prices is essential to help everyday Australians manage these costs.
ticker_line: Privatisation linked to rising living costs in Australia
author: Nathan Schmidt
heading: Economy

title: RESERVE BANK RATE RISE TIPPED
summary: Top economists expect the Reserve Bank to raise the official cash rate by 25 basis points to 2.5% this week, as concerns about inflation ease. However, some banks believe the Reserve Bank should wait to give the economy more time to recover.
ticker_line: Reserve Bank rate hike expected this week
author: Tom Pullar-Strecker
heading: Economy

title: Superannuation: Risk assessed, AI craze fuels double-digit return for 'rational' funds
