summary: Major Australian superannuation funds report around 10% returns for the year, driven by gains in international shares and optimism around artificial intelligence. While they acknowledge risks from high valuations, they do not believe there is a bubble in the AI sector at this time.
ticker_line: Super funds see strong returns amid AI optimism
author: Clancy Yeates
heading: Superannuation

title: Beyond AI pilots, the organisations turning ambition into action
summary: Many organisations are moving from AI experiments to real change by building strong data foundations. RACQ and RMIT are examples of how connecting data and AI can improve customer experiences and business results.
ticker_line: RACQ and RMIT lead AI transformation efforts
author: Katrina Troughton
heading: AI

title: AI sway: unions steer ALP
summary: Labor's draft policy now includes stricter rules on artificial intelligence, reflecting union demands for more oversight. The changes also reaffirm Labor's commitment to renewable energy and include tax hikes from the May budget.
ticker_line: Labor tightens AI regulations amid union pressure
author: GREG BROWN, CHIEF POLITICAL CORRESP
heading: Regulation

title: Westpac taps bots to plug mortgage gap
summary: Westpac is using AI bots to speed up mortgage and credit card applications, saving 12,500 banker hours in July alone. The bank aims to improve its AI ranking and mortgage growth, competing with Commonwealth Bank and plans to launch more AI tools for customers by the end of the year.
ticker_line: Westpac boosts AI use to enhance mortgage processing
author: James Eyers
heading: Banking

title: Improved service for super? You’ll pay
summary: AustralianSuper is raising administration fees for its 3.6 million members, effective October 31. The increase will cost members up to $5.97 more per week, with the fund claiming the extra fees will improve services and security.
ticker_line: AustralianSuper raises fees for better services
author: Cameron Micallef
heading: Superannuation

title: Investment: Sovereign wealth funds bypassing Australia: Macquarie
summary: Macquarie's CEO warns that sovereign wealth funds are avoiding Australia due to slow approval processes and uncertainty, risking investment opportunities as other countries attract capital more effectively. Shemara Wikramanayake calls for faster regulatory changes to maintain Australia's appeal to global investors.
ticker_line: Sovereign funds shun Australia over slow approvals
author: Joanne Tran
heading: Investments

title: Auditing firms: Watchdog reviews 550 complaints at big four
summary: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) is reviewing over 550 complaints about misconduct at the big four auditing firms, particularly focusing on KPMG amid allegations of misuse of client information and other issues. This follows KPMG's recent crisis, which led to executive resignations and the loss of major contracts, including a $95 million deal with Macquarie Group.
ticker_line: ASIC investigates misconduct at big four auditors
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Regulation

title: Financial services: Diversa may have charged fees on 'non-existent' super balances: ASIC
summary: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) is investigating whether Diversa charged fees on superannuation balances that had become worthless after the collapse of First Guardian. Diversa's executives faced criticism for awarding a large bonus to their CEO despite the company's failures and ongoing legal issues.
ticker_line: ASIC probes Diversa over superannuation fees
author: Lucas Baird and Michael Bailey
heading: Superannuation

title: Retirement savings: 'Quite a different tax bill' for same super returns
summary: New tax rules for superannuation funds mean wealthy members could face different tax bills for similar investment returns. The Albanese government’s tax on super balances over $3 million has raised concerns about how funds will calculate these taxes fairly.
ticker_line: New super tax raises fairness concerns for investors
author: John Kehoe | Economics
heading: Superannuation

title: The fine print of banks’ travel insurance changes
summary: Major banks in Australia are changing their credit card travel insurance policies, reducing coverage and prompting consumers to review their options. Experts warn that the new terms may leave travellers underinsured, and suggest purchasing separate travel insurance for better protection.
ticker_line: Banks overhaul credit card travel insurance policies
author: Anthony Keane
heading: General Insurance

title: Affordability at new low despite house prices falling
summary: Housing affordability in Australia has hit a record low, worsened by rising interest rates despite falling house prices. A median-income household can now afford only 12% of homes sold, with South Australia becoming the least affordable state.
ticker_line: Housing affordability reaches all-time low in Australia
author: Shane Wright | Senior economics cor
heading: Economy

title: Health rebate shift reignites states-feds fight
summary: State and territory ministers are demanding more funding from the federal government due to cuts in private health insurance rebates for elderly Australians, which could increase pressure on public hospitals. Aged-care providers are also halting plans for new beds after a small increase in funding was announced, which they say is not enough to cover rising costs.
ticker_line: States push for more funds amid health rebate cuts
author: Lachlan Leeming, NSW Political Corr
heading: Health Insurance

title: China’s AI poses high risk: Hastie
summary: Liberal frontbencher Andrew Hastie warns that Australia should be cautious about using Chinese AI technology, suggesting it could pose risks to national security. He calls for Australia to develop its own AI capabilities and supports regulating AI to address these challenges.
ticker_line: Hastie warns of risks from Chinese AI technology
author: Greg Brown, Chief Political Corresp
heading: AI

title: Trust in the Reserve Bank is under strain, RBA deputy governor concedes
summary: RBA deputy governor Andrew Hauser says public trust in the bank’s ability to meet its inflation goals over the next year has fallen, although overall trust remains high, according to a survey of 12,000 Australians. He said persistent high inflation is testing confidence, while the RBA’s Monetary Policy Board has raised interest rates to 4.85 per cent, the highest level in 18 years.
ticker_line: RBA confidence weakens as inflation remains high
author: Gareth Hutchens
heading: Economy

title: Big four banks pass on rates pain
summary: Westpac and NAB will pass on the Reserve Bank’s 0.25 percentage point rate rise to mortgage customers from November 13, while Macquarie will apply it from November 19 and also lift savings rates. The increase takes the cash rate to 4.85 per cent, its fifth rise this year; a $500,000 mortgage now costs about $258 more a month than at the start of the year, and borrowers are urged to ask their bank for a better rate or support.
ticker_line: Big banks pass on fifth rate rise to borrowers
author: Cameron Micallef
heading: Banking

title: US hack into our health records
summary: A hacker using the name ‘bytetobreach’ claims to have stolen about 100,000 documents from an NSW Health website used to apply for dental vouchers, but police estimate about four gigabytes of data was taken. eHealth NSW says no patient data was involved and only a small number of third-party provider records were affected; NSW Police are investigating with help from US authorities.
ticker_line: NSW Health investigates claimed dental data breach
author: Jack Nivison and Alexandra Feiam
heading: Regulation

title: NAB backs down on Christmas redundancies
summary: NAB has delayed the departure of staff facing involuntary redundancies until January 27, five weeks later than planned, after public and political criticism of the cuts. The bank has also extended consultation by a week; about 1500 workers are affected, while staff who choose a voluntary payout will still leave on December 2.
ticker_line: NAB delays involuntary staff exits until January 27
author: Jack Derwin
heading: Banking

title: Aussies pull out $13 billion, huge super move
summary: Over the past year, Australians have withdrawn more than $13 billion from large super funds to invest in self-managed super funds (SMSFs), nearly doubling the trend from the previous year. While SMSFs offer more control over investments, they come with significant risks and responsibilities that many may not fully understand.
ticker_line: Aussies withdraw $13 billion for self-managed super funds
author: Ben Graham
heading: Superannuation

title: Treasury: No boost to growth from budget
summary: Treasury reports that the Albanese government's major tax changes won't boost economic growth or productivity, focusing instead on wealth redistribution. Despite some targeted measures for small businesses, overall forecasts for growth remain unchanged.
ticker_line: Treasury says budget won't boost economic growth
author: John Kehoe | Economics
heading: Economy

title: CBA offers staff $3000 a head to recommend private bank recruits
summary: Commonwealth Bank is offering staff $3000 for each successful referral of new hires to its private bank until June 30, as competition for skilled workers intensifies. This follows a trend of major banks, including Westpac and NAB, actively recruiting talent from each other.
ticker_line: CBA pays $3000 for staff recruitment referrals
author: Angira Bharadwaj
heading: Banking

title: 'Complacent' super giants lose $8b in a year
summary: Australians moved nearly $8 billion from large super funds to self-managed super funds (SMSFs) in the past year, highlighting a growing trend of disengagement with traditional pension funds. Major funds like AustralianSuper and Australian Retirement Trust are facing increased member losses as more people seek personalized financial advice and control over their investments.
ticker_line: Australians shift $8 billion to SMSFs
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Superannuation

title: Negative equity looms for recent homebuyers
summary: Commonwealth Bank predicts falling house prices in Sydney and Melbourne, which could lead to negative equity for recent buyers. Other cities like Perth and Brisbane are expected to see price increases.
ticker_line: House price drops may hit recent buyers hard
author: David Rogers, markets
heading: Economy

title: Jobs harder to find but AI not to blame
summary: A Deloitte report shows that finding a job in Australia will be tougher in 2026, but this is not mainly due to AI. Instead, rising interest rates and economic issues from the Middle East conflict are affecting hiring.
ticker_line: Job market tightens amid economic uncertainty
heading: AI

title: Rates are taking their toll, but don’t expect quick cuts
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia has decided to keep interest rates at 4.35% as high rates are slowing the economy. They warn that inflation may take another two years to return to target levels, and further rate hikes are possible if needed.
ticker_line: RBA holds rates steady amid economic slowdown
author: Sophie Foster
heading: Economy

title: How many home owners are in negative equity now?
summary: Fewer than 1% of Australian home owners are in negative equity, meaning their property is worth less than their loan. Most first home buyers are buying in areas that have not seen significant price drops, reducing their risk of negative equity.
ticker_line: Negative equity remains low among Australian home owners
author: Wes Mountain
heading: Economy

title: Not just upheaval: AI could deliver $120b boost and more jobs
summary: A new report by EY predicts that artificial intelligence could boost Australia's economy by up to $120 billion and create 36,000 to 44,000 jobs by the middle of the next decade. While some sectors may lose jobs, many others, especially construction and retail, are expected to see significant job growth due to increased investment and productivity from AI.
ticker_line: AI could add $120 billion to economy
author: Shane Wright
heading: Economy

title: House price drop of 10pc in major cities, says NAB
summary: National Australia Bank predicts house prices will drop by 10% in Sydney and Melbourne, with overall capital city prices falling by about 5%. This decline is driven by rising interest rates and increased property listings, leading to the sharpest downturn in 40 years.
ticker_line: NAB forecasts 10% drop in house prices
author: Lucy Slade
heading: Economy

title: Carroll cabinet to fix business links
summary: Victorian Premier Ben Carroll has reshuffled his cabinet, removing the infrastructure and Suburban Rail Loop portfolios to improve relations with businesses. New Treasurer Colin Brooks plans to engage with industry groups to address their concerns and focus on job growth as the state approaches the November election.
ticker_line: Carroll reshuffles cabinet to mend business ties
author: Sumeyya Ilanbey
heading: Economy

title: ‘Caught in a trap’: The most expensive regions for insurance on Australia’s east coast revealed
summary: Insurance costs are skyrocketing in flood-prone areas of Australia's east coast, with some regions seeing premiums rise by over 80% since 2021. Many homeowners, like Megan Vicary, are struggling to afford coverage and are left without flood insurance, raising concerns about financial security during climate disasters.
ticker_line: Flood risks drive up insurance costs dramatically
author: Caitlin Fitzsimmons and Michael Bac
heading: General Insurance

title: Tax reforms 'to change house prices forever'
summary: The Albanese government's tax reforms are expected to lower house prices by 5% permanently, with major banks predicting declines of up to 13%. Economists warn that the housing market downturn could be historically significant, influenced by multiple factors including interest rates and economic conditions.
ticker_line: Tax reforms predicted to lower house prices significantly
author: Grace Lagan
heading: Economy

title: AI doesn't need to know your race to discriminate against you
summary: Artificial intelligence can unintentionally discriminate against people by using indirect information that reflects their race or background, even if it doesn't directly include these details. This issue affects various sectors, including insurance, lending, and employment, raising concerns about fairness and legal compliance.
ticker_line: AI can discriminate without knowing your race
author: Fei Huang
heading: Regulation

title: ASIC reveals hundreds of complaints about alleged audit misconduct by big four accounting firms
summary: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) is investigating 551 complaints of audit misconduct against the big four accounting firms: KPMG, PwC, EY, and Deloitte. This follows allegations that confidential documents were misused in audit bids, prompting calls for broader investigations into these firms' practices.
ticker_line: ASIC probes misconduct claims against big four firms
author: business Nassim Khadem
heading: Regulation

title: Financial services: CBA and Westpac exploit loophole to charge overlimit fees on credit cards
summary: Commonwealth Bank and Westpac are charging long-term credit card customers $15 overlimit fees, despite these fees being banned for new accounts since 2012. Critics call this practice a 'loyalty tax' as it unfairly penalises loyal customers who exceed their credit limits.
ticker_line: CBA and Westpac face backlash over credit fees
author: Elias Visontay
heading: Banking

title: 'Everyone is feeling the pain': rate hike hits Sydney hard
summary: The Reserve Bank’s fifth rate rise this year lifted Australia’s official interest rate to 4.85 per cent, the highest since the global financial crisis. Mortgage holders in Parramatta said the increase would add about $100 a month to repayments on a $600,000 loan, forcing families to cut spending and adding pressure for property investors struggling to find tenants.
ticker_line: Fifth rate rise adds pressure on Sydney households
author: Ellie Busby
heading: Economy

title: CBA warns of record year-long 15pc price slump
summary: CBA forecasts home prices will fall 15 per cent across capital cities by late 2027, the biggest decline in its 45-year records, as higher interest rates and changes to property tax concessions weaken demand. It expects falls of up to 18 per cent in Perth and Brisbane and 16 per cent in Sydney, while the RBA has raised its cash rate to 4.85 per cent and warned it could rise further.
ticker_line: CBA forecasts record 15pc housing price slump
author: Nick Lenaghan and Lucy Slade
heading: Economy

title: Analysis: RBA's ugly outlook spells tough times
summary: The RBA raised the cash rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.85 per cent, its highest level in 18 years, saying strong domestic spending, weak productivity and wage-sensitive prices are driving inflation—not just higher fuel costs from the Middle East war. It expects slow economic growth, falling real wages until at least late 2027 and unemployment to rise, warning many households may feel as if the economy is in recession; further rate rises remain possible.
ticker_line: RBA warns of weak growth and more household pain
author: John Kehoe
heading: Economy

title: IFM Investors' staff costs go past $1b as profit surges
summary: IFM Investors more than doubled its after-tax profit to $251.5 million in the year to June 30, as higher fees from infrastructure and property investments helped lift its assets to $291 billion. Staff costs rose 10 per cent to more than $1 billion, while chief executive David Neal received $3.8 million; the results come amid scrutiny from the super funds that own IFM over its spending on overseas events.
ticker_line: IFM profit more than doubles as staff costs top $1b
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Superannuation

title: There’s one age you’ll pay more tax than any other
summary: People aged 43 pay the most tax in Australia, averaging $59,000 a year, due to high incomes and spending. Recent government budget changes are expected to increase tax burdens on younger and middle-aged Australians while benefiting older investors.
ticker_line: Age 43 sees peak tax burden in Australia
author: Anthony Keane
heading: Economy

title: New super rules spark $6bn small business cash crisis
summary: New rules for superannuation payments, starting July 1, require Australian employers to pay super at the same time as wages, potentially forcing small businesses to find an extra $6 billion and dip into personal savings due to cash flow issues from late customer payments.
ticker_line: New super rules may strain small business cash flow
author: Rishab Jain
heading: Superannuation

title: Unfair health insurance rebate cut will ripple through the generations
summary: The Albanese government plans to cut health insurance rebates for older Australians, arguing for fairness between generations. However, this decision may lead to more financial and emotional strain on families as older Australians could drop their coverage, resulting in longer public hospital waiting times and increased care responsibilities for their adult children.
ticker_line: Health insurance rebate cuts impact families deeply
author: DR RACHEL DAVID
heading: Health Insurance

title: Labor’s planned NDIS overhaul is ‘blunt and inequitable’, thinktank says
summary: The Grattan Institute criticises Labor's plan to cut funding for social participation in the NDIS by 50%, calling it unfair and poorly thought out. The government aims to reduce costs in the $50 billion scheme, but the changes may harm those with disabilities who rely on these supports.
ticker_line: NDIS funding cuts face strong criticism from experts
author: Sarah Basford Canales
heading: General Insurance

title: Unexpected AI boom contributed to RBA interest rate U-turn
summary: RBA Governor Michele Bullock says the unexpected growth in artificial intelligence (AI) has boosted the global economy, leading the Reserve Bank to change its plans on interest rates. Despite earlier expectations of an economic slowdown, strong AI investment has driven growth in Australia and its trading partners.
ticker_line: AI boom prompts RBA interest rate changes
author: Lea Jurkovic
heading: Economy

title: RBA boss says economy can weather war and avoid recession
summary: Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock believes Australia can avoid a recession despite rising oil prices due to the ongoing war. She stated that the economy is expected to grow, with strong investment in sectors like software and renewable energy.
ticker_line: RBA optimistic about economy amid rising oil prices
author: Shane Wright
heading: Economy

title: Car theft falls in every state but one and insurers are angry
summary: Car theft claims in Victoria have surged by 25%, reaching $243 million, while other states saw declines. Insurers are upset as the rise in thefts is linked to increased crime concerns in the state ahead of the upcoming election.
ticker_line: Victoria sees major rise in car theft claims
author: Patrick Durkin
heading: General Insurance

title: 20pc house price fall will open doors for investors
summary: Morgan Stanley's chief economist Chris Read says house prices need to fall by 15-20% to attract investors back into the housing market after recent tax changes. He warns that lower prices and higher rental yields are necessary for investors to regain previous returns.
ticker_line: House prices must drop to attract investors
author: DAVID ROGERS, MARKETS
heading: Economy

title: Bourse jumps as rate fears ease
summary: Australia's sharemarket rose as hopes grew that the Reserve Bank will keep interest rates steady. BHP and Rio Tinto reached record highs, while the economy showed slower growth, reducing the chance of further rate hikes.
ticker_line: Australian sharemarket rebounds on interest rate hopes
author: Cameron Micallef, Equities
heading: Economy

title: Stagflation fears rise as OECD lowers Australian forecasts
summary: Australia faces stagflation risks as the OECD lowers economic growth forecasts, predicting inflation to reach 5% and GDP growth to slow significantly. The country is experiencing its longest per-capita recession in over 65 years, driven by rising interest rates and reduced consumer spending.
ticker_line: Stagflation fears rise as OECD cuts forecasts
author: MATTHEW CRANSTON
heading: Economy

title: Mercer Super agrees to pay $10.3m fine to ASIC
summary: Mercer Super has agreed to pay a $10.3 million fine to the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) for failing to report serious issues with member services. The fund also faces $1.2 million in legal costs and has admitted to not reporting seven internal investigations between 2021 and 2024.
ticker_line: Mercer Super hit with $10.3 million fine
author: Angelica Snowden
heading: Regulation

title: Technology: 'Dangerous' AI program to hamper the hackers
summary: Australian organisations will soon access Anthropic's powerful AI model, Claude Mythos, which can identify software flaws that hackers might exploit. This move is part of a global effort to strengthen cybersecurity for critical systems, especially in sectors like finance and infrastructure.
ticker_line: Australia gains access to powerful AI for cybersecurity
author: David Swan
heading: AI

title: Industrial relations: RBA staff knock back 9.5pc wage rise offer
summary: Reserve Bank staff have rejected a 9.5% pay rise offer, pushing Governor Michele Bullock to renegotiate with the Finance Sector Union, which is demanding higher wages and work-from-home rights. The rejection highlights concerns over wages falling behind inflation and the need for competitive pay to retain skilled workers.
ticker_line: RBA staff reject 9.5% pay rise offer
author: Michael Read
heading: Banking

title: Regulation: Chalmers taps scandal-linked former KPMG partner for APRA role
summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers has appointed David Bradbury, a former KPMG partner linked to an audit scandal, as deputy chair of APRA, alongside Therese McCarthy Hockey. Both appointments aim to strengthen leadership at the regulator amid increasing complexities in the financial system.
ticker_line: Chalmers appoints scandal-linked Bradbury to APRA
author: Hannah Wootton and Edmund Tadros
heading: Regulation

title: Superannuation: AusSuper tips strong year after 9.8pc return
summary: AustralianSuper's balanced fund achieved a 9.77% return for the 2025-26 financial year, driven by strong performance in international equities, particularly in companies related to artificial intelligence. New chief investment officer Shaun Manuell is optimistic about future returns but cautious about market valuations amid rising interest rates.
ticker_line: AustralianSuper reports strong 9.77% return
author: Anthony Macdonald
heading: Superannuation

title: Retail investing: Gen Z backs ETFs as AI drives frenzy
summary: Gen Z investors are increasingly turning to ETFs as they seek to invest amid rising interest in the stock market, particularly driven by AI trends. The number of new ETFs in Australia reached a record high, with a notable gender divide in investment preferences emerging among young traders.
ticker_line: Gen Z embraces ETFs amid AI investment boom
author: Gus McCubbing
heading: Investments

title: Investment losers to avoid scrutiny as part of NRF review
summary: The Labor government's $15 billion National Reconstruction Fund is under review, but changes allowing $6 billion for low-return green energy investments will not be examined. Critics question the fund's approach and its impact on taxpayers.
ticker_line: NRF review excludes low-return investment scrutiny
author: JACK QUAIL
heading: Investments

title: How the ACT can meet its tax timetable
summary: An independent review warns that the ACT government needs major changes to its tax system to meet its goal of phasing out stamp duty by 2030. The report highlights that current tax revenue plans are unlikely to achieve this target without significant adjustments.
ticker_line: ACT faces challenges in tax reform goals
author: Jasper Lindell
heading: Economy

title: Recession risk up as prices fall
summary: Australia's property market is falling, raising concerns about a possible recession this year. Economists warn that declining house prices are hurting household confidence and spending, which could lead to slower economic growth.
ticker_line: Falling property prices raise recession fears
author: Anthony Keane
heading: Economy

title: Fighting against triple threat
summary: Hobart City Council has joined six other councils in Australia to support a federal climate compensation fund. This fund would help cover rising costs from climate change impacts, reducing the financial burden on local ratepayers.
ticker_line: Hobart Council backs federal climate compensation fund
author: Bridget Clarke
heading: Regulation

title: Labor moves to neutralise ‘widow’s tax’ and trust issues
summary: Labor is proposing changes to its tax laws to address the 'widow's tax,' which unfairly affected those inheriting property from a spouse. The changes aim to ensure that widowers, divorcees, and domestic violence victims are not disadvantaged when it comes to negative gearing on inherited properties.
ticker_line: Labor seeks to fix 'widow's tax' issues
author: Noah Yim, Matthew Cranston
heading: Regulation

title: Westpac plugs five AWS AI agents into core lending processes
summary: Westpac is using five AI agents from Amazon to speed up home loan and credit card applications by processing payslips and other documents more efficiently. This technology saves time for bankers and helps customers get quicker responses on their applications.
ticker_line: Westpac enhances lending with AI technology
author: Ry Crozier
heading: Banking

title: 'Decisively negative' time for Australian investors as 'volatile' reporting season begins
summary: Australian companies are set to report their earnings, with expectations for mixed results due to rising costs and economic pressures. Analysts warn of a negative trend in profit forecasts, particularly affecting domestic businesses and banks.
ticker_line: Volatile earnings season ahead for Australian investors
author: business David Chau
heading: Investments

title: Ben Carroll adds artificial intelligence ministry to Victorian cabinet, dumps transport infrastructure
summary: Victorian Premier Ben Carroll has reshuffled his cabinet, creating a new ministry for artificial intelligence while removing the transport infrastructure role. Key changes include Colin Brooks as Treasurer and Anthony Carbines overseeing AI and the digital economy.
ticker_line: New AI ministry formed in Victorian cabinet shake-up
heading: AI

title: AMP results set to offer clues on future strategy
summary: AMP will release its half-year results on Thursday, which may reveal its future plans, including a potential move for Colonial First State and the future of its bank. Investors are keen to see if AMP will pursue growth through acquisitions or focus on organic growth.
ticker_line: AMP's results may hint at future strategy
author: DATA ROOM with BRIDGET CARTER
heading: Banking

title: Pension trap punishes retirees who work
summary: Many retirees, like Kim Gardner, want to work part-time to boost their income but face high taxes and pension cuts that discourage them. A report highlights that the current rules penalise older Australians for earning extra money, prompting calls for changes to the Age Pension income test.
ticker_line: Retirees penalised for working part-time
author: Anthony Keane
heading: Superannuation

title: Street Talk: HSBC puts $20b in deposits up for sale amid retail banking exit
summary: HSBC is selling about $20 billion in deposits as it exits retail banking in Australia after 40 years. The bank aims to complete the sale by the end of the financial year, while focusing on corporate and private banking.
ticker_line: HSBC sells $20 billion in deposits amid exit
author: Sarah Thompson, Kanika Sood and Ang
heading: Banking

title: Australia and US aligned on AI rules: Charlton
summary: Australia and the US are working together on AI regulations that protect original work and require data centres to generate their own energy. Assistant Minister Andrew Charlton highlighted the need for balanced rules that support innovation while addressing risks, as discussions continue ahead of the G20 leaders summit in December.
ticker_line: Australia and US align on AI regulations
author: Jessica Gardner | AFR correspondent
heading: Regulation

title: States fume over Commonwealth's proposed private health insurance rebate changes
summary: State health ministers are opposing the federal government's plan to change private health insurance rebates for older Australians, warning it could increase pressure on public hospitals. The changes could lead to over 80,000 seniors in NSW alone cancelling their insurance, resulting in more surgeries needed in public hospitals.
ticker_line: States oppose federal health insurance rebate changes
author: national health Stephanie
heading: Health Insurance

title: Timing of rate hikes only doubt after hot GDP data
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia may raise interest rates again due to higher than expected inflation and strong economic growth, with a possible hike in September or November. Recent data shows GDP rose 2.1% in the June quarter, leading to increased market expectations for rate increases.
ticker_line: RBA faces pressure to hike rates again
author: David Rogers
heading: Economy

title: Super funds wary of Firmus leadership ahead of IPO
summary: Major superannuation funds in Melbourne are hesitant to invest in Firmus's upcoming IPO due to concerns about its leader, Oliver Curtis, who has a past conviction for insider trading. Despite plans for a $4 billion IPO and ambitious earnings projections, many are skeptical about the company's financial details and leadership.
ticker_line: Super funds cautious on Firmus IPO leadership
author: BRIDGET CARTER, DATA ROOM
heading: Superannuation

title: Small business cry for cyber help
summary: Small businesses are struggling to improve their cybersecurity due to government cuts and red tape, with concerns raised about the end of the Cyber Wardens program that trained over 34,000 people. Business groups are calling for renewed support to help them tackle new AI-related threats and meet compliance requirements.
ticker_line: Small businesses seek help for cybersecurity challenges
author: Noah Yim
heading: Regulation

title: Exclusive: AI giants vow remote sites for data centres
summary: Major AI companies plan to build large data centres in remote areas of Australia to avoid public backlash seen in the US. This move follows discussions with Australian officials about a $150 billion AI investment boom and aims to meet energy needs with renewable sources.
ticker_line: AI firms commit to remote data centres in Australia
author: Paul Sakkal | Chief political corre
heading: AI

title: RBA board split but majority backed raising interest rates to 18-year high
summary: The Reserve Bank raised the cash rate to 4.85 per cent, its highest level since 2008, in a 6-3 vote as it tries to curb inflation driven partly by higher oil prices and the AI construction boom. The bank now expects inflation to stay above target for longer, while warning that higher rates, falling property prices and weaker spending could slow the economy and lift unemployment.
ticker_line: RBA lifts rates as inflation pressures persist
author: Shane Wright and Millie Muroi
heading: Economy

title: Banks: Double-digit house price slump, warns Westpac boss
summary: Westpac expects Australian house prices to fall 10.9 per cent between March 2026 and March 2027, while interest rates remain high into 2027. The bank reported a $6.8 billion annual profit, down 1 per cent, and said mortgage hardship had risen slightly but remained low.
ticker_line: Westpac warns house prices could fall nearly 11 per cent
author: Millie Muroi
heading: Banking

title: Australia's economic slowdown is just beginning, economists warn, as recession risks rise
summary: Australia's economy is slowing down, with growth at just 0.3% in early 2026 and rising unemployment. Economists warn of a possible recession as inflation remains high and consumer spending weakens.
ticker_line: Australia faces rising recession risks amid economic slowdown
author: business correspondent David Taylor
heading: Economy

title: Seniors centre leak fears
summary: Mosman Council is investigating a data breach that may have exposed personal information of hundreds of residents linked to the Mosman Square Seniors Centre. The breach occurred through a third-party software system used for community services, and an external cybersecurity firm has been hired to assess the situation.
ticker_line: Data breach at Mosman Council raises concerns
author: Jim O’Rourke
heading: AI

title: Australia gains access to powerful AI amid questions about readiness
summary: Australia has gained access to a powerful AI system called Mythos, which is designed to improve cybersecurity. The government is under pressure to act faster on AI risks and opportunities as independent MPs raise concerns about the pace of its response.
ticker_line: Australia gains access to advanced AI for cybersecurity
author: chief digital political corresponde
heading: AI

title: AI may be tightening jobs market, but some roles could see stronger demand
summary: A Deloitte report highlights that while AI is changing the job market, it may not lead to widespread job losses. Some roles, especially those requiring human skills like creativity and empathy, could see increased demand as AI complements their work.
ticker_line: AI reshapes job market, some roles thrive
author: national work Bronwyn Herb
heading: AI

title: First trade deficit since 2017 opens ‘possible’ contraction
summary: Australia has recorded its first trade deficit since 2017, prompting major banks to lower their economic growth forecasts. This could lead to the first quarterly contraction in economic activity since the COVID pandemic, with concerns over rising imports and falling exports.
ticker_line: Australia faces first trade deficit since 2017
author: Noah Yim, Matthew Cranston
heading: Economy

title: Exclusive: RBA thinks reforms will help cut inflation
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) believes that Labor's tax reforms and falling consumer confidence may lower house prices and spending, which could help reduce inflation. This comes as the government faces criticism over its housing policies and prepares for a key interest rate decision on June 16.
ticker_line: RBA sees potential inflation relief from tax reforms
author: Paul Sakkal and Shane Wright
heading: Economy

title: Wages rise, rates to follow
summary: Australia's minimum wage will rise by 4.75% to $26.44 an hour from July 1, which may lead to two interest rate hikes later this year due to ongoing inflation and low productivity. Business leaders warn this wage increase could cause financial strain and a wave of insolvencies in the hospitality sector.
ticker_line: Minimum wage rise may trigger interest rate hikes
author: Jessica Wang
heading: Economy

title: Minister eases AI burden on FWC
summary: Minister Amanda Rishworth has proposed changes to help the Fair Work Commission manage its growing workload from AI-related claims. The new bill aims to speed up processes, reduce unnecessary hearings, and improve support for workers and businesses.
ticker_line: Fair Work Commission workload eased by new bill
author: EWIN HANNAN
heading: AI

title: Our super system has a new blind spot, and it could cost you thousands
summary: Australia's financial regulator, ASIC, has found serious issues with major investment platforms managing superannuation, including high fees and inadequate oversight, which could cost members thousands. Consumers are urged to be cautious and aware of their superannuation investments, especially if advised by financial planners.
ticker_line: ASIC warns of superannuation platform risks
author: Bec Wilson
heading: Superannuation

title: Super giant ART pulls back on passive strategy
summary: The Australian Retirement Trust is shifting from passive investment strategies to more active management due to concerns over market concentration, especially in technology stocks. This change aims to better protect its $207 billion portfolio against risks associated with relying too heavily on a few companies.
ticker_line: ART shifts focus to active management strategies
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Superannuation

title: Insurance overhaul to fix hospitals
summary: The Labor government plans to simplify private health insurance by reducing the number of products and improving access to maternity and mental health services. Insurers are concerned about rising premiums and the impact on affordability for families, while hospitals welcome the proposed changes aimed at improving patient care.
ticker_line: Labor proposes overhaul of private health insurance
author: Michael Smith | Health
heading: Health Insurance

title: Brokers flag first-home buyer loan slump
summary: Aussie Home Loans reports a 20% drop in first-home buyer loan applications since the government's budget changes, raising concerns about Labor's housing policies. While some brokers see a decrease in inquiries, others report stable interest, but high interest rates and market uncertainty are affecting buyer confidence.
ticker_line: First-home buyer loan applications drop 20%
author: Noah Yim
heading: Economy

title: COSTS OF NEGATIVE EQUITY
summary: Falling home values in Australia are causing concerns about negative equity, where homeowners owe more on their loans than their properties are worth. Experts advise borrowers to assess their loans and consider building cash buffers to avoid financial stress if property values continue to decline.
ticker_line: Falling home values raise negative equity fears
author: Anthony Keane
heading: Economy

title: Stress test reveals our resilient financial system
summary: The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) has reported that assets under its regulation have surpassed $10 trillion, highlighting the strength of Australia's financial system. A recent stress test showed that major banks and superannuation funds can withstand severe economic shocks, ensuring continued stability for Australians.
ticker_line: APRA reports $10 trillion in regulated assets
author: John Lonsdale
heading: Regulation

title: State makes workplace safety legally binding
summary: NSW has made workplace safety codes legally binding, requiring employers to follow specific standards or manage risks at a higher level. This change aims to improve safety and prevent workplace injuries across various industries.
ticker_line: NSW enforces new binding workplace safety laws
author: EWIN HANNAN
heading: Regulation

title: Labor senator leads call to protect workers from AI
summary: Labor Senator Tony Sheldon is leading a new group calling for stronger protections for workers as artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more common in workplaces. The group, launching at the NSW Labor conference, aims to ensure workers have a say in how AI is used, amid concerns about job losses and the need for updated regulations.
ticker_line: Labor pushes for worker protections against AI
author: Rob Harris
heading: AI

title: Worker barred from using AI in complaint against boss
summary: The Fair Work Commission has banned a worker from using AI to draft complaints against her employer, citing that AI-generated emails were lengthy and accusatory, complicating her bullying case. This decision highlights growing concerns over AI in workplace disputes as legal professionals call for stricter regulations.
ticker_line: Worker prohibited from using AI in complaints
author: David Marin-Guzman
heading: Regulation

title: Updated code may fail ASIC test, industry told
summary: The General Insurance Code Governance Committee warns that the updated insurance code may be rejected by ASIC due to weakened consumer protections. They recommend urgent changes to ensure the code meets community expectations and regulatory standards before its planned approval in late October.
ticker_line: Updated insurance code faces ASIC rejection risk
heading: General Insurance

title: ICA to launch campaign as levy debate continues
summary: The Insurance Council of Australia is starting a campaign to urge the NSW Parliament to remove the insurance tax and find a fairer way to fund emergency services. This comes as a parliamentary inquiry is ongoing, with a final report expected in November.
ticker_line: ICA pushes for removal of insurance tax
heading: General Insurance

title: CLOSING BELL: Chalmers must act on super test review
summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers is urged to reform the superannuation performance test to improve investment strategies and address market issues. A report from Treasury on proposed changes is expected soon, following consultations with super funds and stakeholders.
ticker_line: Chalmers urged to reform superannuation performance test
author: Joyce Moullakis
heading: Superannuation

title: Calls to scrap NSW emergency services levy as insurance costs rise
summary: Calls are growing to remove the emergency services levy in New South Wales as home insurance costs rise sharply, with many households struggling to afford premiums. A coalition of industry groups is urging the government to replace the levy with a property-based model before the March 2027 election.
ticker_line: Push to abolish NSW emergency services levy grows
author: business Adelaide Miller
heading: General Insurance

title: The great banking retreat: who will be next to sell up?
summary: HSBC is selling its $36 billion Australian home and personal loan portfolio to Blackstone, highlighting increasing competition in the banking sector. Other mid-tier banks may follow suit as they struggle to compete with larger banks like Macquarie, which is gaining market share with aggressive pricing.
ticker_line: HSBC sells loan portfolio amid banking competition
author: DATA ROOM with BRIDGET CARTER
heading: Banking

title: AI edge steps up cyber threat to power grid
summary: Australia's energy grid faces increased cyber threats from advanced AI models, making it easier for hackers to target critical infrastructure. The Australian Energy Market Operator warns that these risks could escalate quickly, impacting the power system and market confidence.
ticker_line: AI poses growing cyber risk to power grid
author: Perry Williams
heading: AI

title: Currencies: RBA cuts US dollar reserves in sign of hedge against Trump
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia has reduced its US dollar reserves to 45%, the lowest since 2012, as part of a strategy to diversify its assets amid global uncertainty. This shift reflects a broader trend among central banks to lessen reliance on the US dollar due to rising geopolitical risks and changing trade patterns.
ticker_line: RBA cuts US dollar reserves amid global shifts
author: Cecile Lefort
heading: Economy

title: Australia's economy grows faster than expected, raising RBA interest rate rise risk
summary: Australia's economy grew by 0.4% in the June quarter, exceeding expectations and raising the likelihood of an interest rate hike by the Reserve Bank of Australia this month. Despite strong growth, concerns about sustainability remain, with traders now seeing a 70% chance of a rate increase in September.
ticker_line: Australia's economy growth raises rate hike fears
author: business Michael Janda
heading: Economy

title: Actuaries Institute and UTS HTI publish AI risk management guidance for financial services
summary: The Actuaries Institute and UTS HTI have launched guidance to help financial services manage risks from artificial intelligence, highlighting the need for better governance as AI use grows. The framework aims to integrate with existing risk management processes and is adaptable for different organisation sizes.
ticker_line: New AI risk management guidance for finance sector
heading: Regulation

title: CBA warns more house pain on way
summary: The Commonwealth Bank warns that house prices in Sydney and Melbourne will continue to drop, with expected falls of 11% and 10% respectively this year. High interest rates and changes in property taxes are contributing to this decline, while the government struggles to meet its housing supply targets.
ticker_line: CBA predicts ongoing decline in house prices
author: Shane Wright | Senior economics cor
heading: Economy

title: Banks: CBA charged customer fees on an unactivated card for 13 years
summary: The Commonwealth Bank charged a customer annual fees for a corporate credit card that he never activated for 13 years. After the customer raised concerns, the bank acknowledged the mistake and offered a refund of $1,040, but defended its right to charge fees for unactivated cards.
ticker_line: CBA charged fees on unactivated card for 13 years
author: Elias Visontay
heading: Banking

title: Bosses embrace AI, but count the tech’s cost
summary: Australian companies are increasingly adopting AI technology, but they are facing rising costs and are now focusing on ensuring that spending leads to real productivity gains. Executives are implementing strict cost management measures to balance the benefits of AI with its expenses.
ticker_line: Australian firms embrace AI amid rising costs
author: Eric Johnston, Associate
heading: AI

title: AI is coming for office workers. How vulnerable is Brisbane?
summary: More than 40 per cent of work tasks in Brisbane are exposed to AI automation, rising to about 45 per cent in the CBD and inner suburbs, according to SGS Economics and Planning. The report says this measures tasks that could change, not jobs certain to disappear; infrastructure work ahead of the 2032 Olympics may give Brisbane time to prepare.
ticker_line: Brisbane office tasks face growing AI exposure
author: Marissa Calligeros and Matt Wade
heading: AI

title: Record super raid for dental work leaves hole in retirement savings
summary: Australians withdrew $892 million from super for dental treatment in 2025-26, up 421 per cent since 2021-22, with the ATO warning of alleged fraud and misuse for cosmetic or overseas procedures. Advisers say a $26,000 withdrawal at age 30 could cut retirement savings by almost $327,000, while industry groups are calling for stronger safeguards and a ban on predatory advertising.
ticker_line: Dental super withdrawals surge, risking retirement savings
author: Anthony Keane
heading: Superannuation

title: Westpac reveals AI cut data warehouse migration cost from $70m to $35m
summary: Westpac says AI helped it migrate St.George’s legacy data warehouse for about $35 million, half the original $70 million budget, and more than two years ahead of schedule. The new cloud-based platform is expected to deliver about $15 million in annual benefits from FY27, while the AI migration tools and methods may be reused on other projects.
ticker_line: Westpac halves data migration cost using AI
author: Ry Crozier
heading: AI

title: Big banks pour billions into India
summary: ANZ, Commonwealth Bank, NAB and Macquarie paid their Indian subsidiaries about $1.9 billion in the past year and employed 23,000 people there, with a further $200 million spent on contractors. Their fast-growing hubs, mainly in Bengaluru, handle technology and support work, helping banks access skilled workers and lower costs as they expand offshore and cut or shift some Australian roles.
ticker_line: Australian banks expand India hubs and offshore work
author: Jack Derwin
heading: Banking

title: ASIC warns super funds on service failures
summary: ASIC says it may take super fund trustees to court and seek the return of executive bonuses if funds do not improve how they handle complaints. Its review found many funds failed to spot repeated problems, including one fund that left 250,000 members unable to access documents and another that had not paid 500 members $1.3 million in retirement bonuses.
ticker_line: ASIC warns super funds over ignored member complaints
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Superannuation

title: Home values slump as RBA mulls rate increase
summary: Australian property values fell 1.2 per cent in October, their seventh monthly decline, and are down 6.7 per cent since March. Falls have spread to Brisbane and Perth, while economists expect another Reserve Bank rate rise this week that could add about $110 a month to repayments on an average mortgage.
ticker_line: Home values fall as another rate rise looms
author: Shane Wright
heading: Economy

title: Superannuation: Watchdog slams funds on customer complaints
summary: ASIC has warned superannuation trustees it may take enforcement action if they fail to properly investigate and address customer complaints. Its review found nearly a quarter of 45 trustees did not regularly check complaints for wider problems, while some blamed members; complaints across super funds rose more than 40 per cent last financial year.
ticker_line: ASIC warns super funds over mishandled complaints
author: Millie Muroi
heading: Superannuation

title: Exclusive: Inner-city workers at huge risk from AI
summary: A report by SGS Economics and Planning found that more than 45 per cent of work tasks in Sydney’s City and North Sydney council areas are exposed to AI automation, with other inner-city and knowledge-work hubs also highly exposed. The analysis measures tasks that could change, not jobs certain to disappear; the report says workers may need retraining and support as AI reshapes work.
ticker_line: Sydney’s inner-city workers face high AI exposure
author: Matt Wade
heading: AI

title: Comment: AI tech debt binge drives up global borrowing costs
summary: Major technology companies are borrowing heavily to fund AI data centres, adding to competition for money and pushing up bond yields. CBA strategist Adam Donaldson estimates this may add about 50 basis points to the yield on 10-year Australian government bonds, costing the federal budget roughly $3 billion a year in extra interest; the effect on mortgage rates, especially variable rates, remains uncertain.
ticker_line: AI borrowing binge adds to governments’ debt costs
author: Clancy Yeates
heading: AI

title: CommBank readies ‘Can’ brand evolution with new agency appointment
summary: Commonwealth Bank is changing its brand strategy by appointing a new advertising agency, Howatson+Company, to refresh its long-standing 'Can' campaign. This shift aims to strengthen its market leadership and adapt to evolving customer needs and technology.
ticker_line: CommBank evolves brand with new agency appointment
author: Danielle Long
heading: Banking

title: Exclusive: RBA rates Labor bad on homes
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) has criticized Labor's housing policies, saying they have not improved home supply and may have raised prices. Labor's plans to increase housing availability are under scrutiny as migration rates and other factors continue to impact affordability.
ticker_line: RBA criticizes Labor's housing policies and impact
author: Paul Sakkal | Chief political corre
heading: Economy

title: CEOs get AI twins as clones step up
summary: Australian CEOs are using AI to create digital versions of themselves, helping with tasks like writing memos and managing schedules. This trend is changing corporate communications, but experts warn that human skills are still needed for effective messaging.
ticker_line: CEOs embrace AI clones for corporate tasks
author: Jared Lynch
heading: AI

title: Australia’s median wealth falls almost 7% since 2020 despite the rich getting richer, report says
summary: A new UBS report shows that while Australia's average wealth rose by 19% since 2020, the median wealth fell by nearly 7%, highlighting a growing gap between the rich and the rest of the population. Over 25,000 new millionaires were created in Australia last year, reflecting a global trend of increasing wealth inequality.
ticker_line: Australia's wealth gap widens despite rising millionaires
author: Patrick Commins Economics
heading: Economy

title: $19bn in property deals done in just six months
summary: Australian commercial property transactions reached $19 billion in the first half of 2026, a 16% increase from last year. The retail sector led with $6.1 billion in sales, while domestic buyers became more active as offshore investment declined.
ticker_line: Australian property deals hit $19 billion in H1 2026
author: Ben Wilmot
heading: Investments

title: One Nation malcontents surf the RBA's inflation wave
summary: High inflation in Australia is causing voter frustration, benefiting Pauline Hanson's One Nation party. The Reserve Bank of Australia's failure to control inflation has led to economic discontent, with many Australians expecting conditions to worsen.
ticker_line: High inflation fuels support for One Nation party
author: John Kehoe
heading: Economy

title: Financial misconduct compensation scheme faces $170 million cost blow out
summary: The government's Compensation Scheme of Last Resort faces a $170 million shortfall to support victims of financial misconduct, including those affected by the First Guardian and Shield super collapses. The scheme, which helps recover losses from insolvent financial firms, currently has only $20 million available.
ticker_line: Compensation scheme faces $170 million funding gap
heading: Superannuation

title: Westpac director Nash latest KPMG casualty
summary: Westpac director Peter Nash has resigned from the bank's board to avoid distractions linked to the KPMG scandal, where he had connections. KPMG is under investigation for alleged misuse of client documents, and Nash's departure comes as the firm appoints a new independent chair.
ticker_line: Westpac director resigns amid KPMG scandal
author: David Ross
heading: Banking

title: Loan-slide: tax reforms hit housing
summary: Loan applications are dropping sharply, raising concerns about a cooling property market due to recent tax reforms and rising interest rates. The Reserve Bank warns this slowdown could impact the overall economy, with home values already declining in major cities.
ticker_line: Property market slows as loan applications drop
author: Matthew Cranston, David Ross, Noah
heading: Economy

title: ALP, Coalition line up to deny teenage super
summary: Labor and the Coalition have rejected calls to include superannuation for teenagers in new laws, which exempt businesses from paying super for young workers under 18 who work less than 30 hours a week. The Greens plan to challenge this decision again next month.
ticker_line: Labor and Coalition deny super for teenage workers
author: MATTHEW CRANSTON
heading: Superannuation

title: Watchdog eyes ALP ‘bias’ for industry super
summary: The Coalition has asked the National Anti-Corruption Commission to investigate the Albanese government's ties with industry super funds, claiming they pressured the corporate regulator to change rules that benefit these funds in property investments. Opposition spokesman Andrew Bragg argues this gives an unfair advantage to large super funds over individual investors.
ticker_line: Coalition seeks probe into ALP's super fund ties
author: GREG BROWN, CHIEF POLITICAL CORRESP
heading: Superannuation

title: Rules targeting risk reduction in critical infrastructure sectors
summary: New rules effective June 5 require Australian critical infrastructure operators to improve risk management, including stricter cybersecurity measures and supply chain checks. These changes aim to better protect vital sectors like energy, water, and communications from evolving threats.
ticker_line: New rules enhance risk management for critical sectors
author: Tim Johnston
heading: Regulation

title: No fees at new private hospital leaves doctors divided
summary: Adeney Private Hospital in Kew offers no out-of-pocket fees for patients with Bupa or Medibank insurance, sparking debate among doctors about its impact on healthcare. While some see it as a positive change for affordability, others warn it may lead to a system that prioritises healthy patients and limits doctor independence.
ticker_line: New hospital model sparks doctor debate
author: Henrietta Cook | Health
heading: Health Insurance

title: Call for action as bed block soars 60pc
summary: Hospital bed block has increased by 60% in three years, costing the health system $1.6 billion annually. Calls are being made for the government to fund 600 transition beds to help ease the crisis and improve care for older Australians.
ticker_line: Hospital bed block crisis prompts urgent funding call
author: SARAH ISON, ROSIE LEWIS
heading: Health Insurance

title: Big four lenders bankroll Blackstone’s purchase of $36b HSBC loan book
summary: Blackstone is buying HSBC Australia's $36 billion mortgage and personal loan book, with ANZ and NAB among the lenders providing over $30 billion in debt for the deal. This marks the largest sale of a bank's mortgage book globally and is expected to reshape the market.
ticker_line: Blackstone acquires HSBC's $36 billion loan book
author: Sarah Thompson and Kanika Sood and
heading: Banking

title: No action against Mineral Resources, Ellison: ASIC
summary: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) has decided not to take action against Mineral Resources and its CEO, Chris Ellison, despite previous concerns. This decision comes amid ongoing market volatility due to renewed conflict in the Middle East affecting oil prices.
ticker_line: ASIC clears Mineral Resources and CEO Ellison
author: David Rogers, Valerina Changarathil
heading: Regulation

title: APRA urges banks to bolster AI risk controls, not slow down deployment
summary: The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) urges banks to quickly adopt artificial intelligence while improving risk management practices. APRA's Therese McCarthy Hockey emphasizes the need for faster governance rather than slowing down AI deployment, following a report that provides guidance on managing AI-related risks.
ticker_line: APRA pushes banks to adopt AI faster, improve controls
author: James Eyers
heading: Regulation

title: AusSuper will admit to death benefit bungles
summary: AustralianSuper will admit to breaking financial laws by delaying death benefit payments to families of deceased members. The corporate regulator, ASIC, is finalising a settlement after an 18-month legal battle, with a court hearing set for September 9.
ticker_line: AustralianSuper admits to death benefit delays
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Superannuation

title: Cost of building a home rise by almost 30 per cent in five years, Insurance Council of Australia finds
summary: The cost to build a home in Australia has increased by nearly 30% over the past five years, with some materials rising by up to 70%. This surge in costs is mainly due to inflation and the impact of extreme weather events, leading to a competition for resources between builders and insurers.
ticker_line: Home building costs soar nearly 30% in five years
heading: General Insurance

title: Treasurer is mowed down over inflation
summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers faces criticism for high inflation and government spending, with inflation rising to 4% in August. Economists warn of potential interest rate hikes as early as November 3, while Chalmers insists global oil prices are the main cause of inflation.
ticker_line: Chalmers criticized over rising inflation concerns
author: Ellen Ransley
heading: Economy

title: Stablecoins could put Australia's $24 billion digital finance opportunity within reach
summary: Australia could unlock up to $24 billion in annual economic gains from digital finance by adopting stablecoins, which offer faster and cheaper payment options. However, regulatory uncertainty and infrastructure challenges need to be addressed to realise this potential.
ticker_line: Stablecoins could boost Australia's digital finance sector
heading: Economy

title: Banking: Mortgage pain grows as big banks pass on rate rises
summary: Commonwealth Bank, Westpac, and ANZ will raise home loan rates by 0.25% from October 9, following the Reserve Bank's decision. Despite this increase, overdue mortgage rates remain low, and offset account balances are near record highs, indicating some resilience among borrowers.
ticker_line: Big banks raise mortgage rates again
author: Nick Bonyhady
heading: Banking

title: APRA warns of private credit risk to super pot
summary: The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) has raised concerns about risks in private credit affecting Australia’s $4.5 trillion superannuation sector. APRA is reviewing super trustees' investments and proposing new rules to improve oversight and accountability after recent failures in the sector.
ticker_line: APRA warns of risks in superannuation investments
author: Cliona O’Dowd
heading: Superannuation

title: Libs flag fight on health rebate
summary: Victorian Opposition Leader Jess Wilson plans to confront Prime Minister Anthony Albanese over cuts to the private health insurance rebate for older Australians, which could force many to pay more and increase pressure on public hospitals. The Albanese government expects to save nearly $3 billion over four years with this change, starting in April 2027.
ticker_line: Libs challenge Albanese on health rebate cuts
author: Anthony Galloway, Victorian politic
heading: Health Insurance

title: Suncorp has held preliminary talks with suitor
summary: Suncorp is in early talks with Tokio Marine about a possible buyout, with no formal proposal yet made. Suncorp, Australia's second-largest insurance firm valued at $20 billion, is seen as an attractive target for Tokio Marine's expansion plans.
ticker_line: Suncorp discusses potential buyout with Tokio Marine
author: DATA ROOM with BRIDGET CARTER
heading: General Insurance

title: Top chef Scott Pickett faces court grilling over collapse of super fund
summary: Chef and restaurateur Scott Pickett is expected to be questioned by liquidators about First Guardian’s $13 million investment in his joint business with fund boss David Anderson, Rogue Traders, and a decision to waive repayment. Pickett is not accused of wrongdoing and is not a defendant in the regulator’s case; First Guardian’s 2025 collapse wiped out $512 million in savings for about 6000 investors, while liquidators have so far recovered only $8 million from investments listed at $118.38 million.
ticker_line: Liquidators to question Pickett over First Guardian funds
author: Sarah Danckert
heading: Superannuation

title: AI trade claims casualties but the boom is far from over
summary: Nanuk Asset Management’s Tom King says the AI boom may bring failures, especially among heavily indebted operators renting out computing power, but electricity shortages and ongoing demand make a broad collapse unlikely. He advises investors not to bet everything on one AI company or abandon the theme, while noting it remains unclear who will pay for the projected growth in AI use.
ticker_line: AI boom faces failures, but demand remains strong
author: David Rogers
heading: AI

title: In an unstable world super-charged by AI, hacking is the new war front
summary: Cyber attacks on systems that control physical infrastructure are increasing, with recent incidents affecting water, hospitals, supermarkets and Australian sugar production. Experts warn that ageing equipment is becoming more exposed as it connects to the internet, while AI could help hackers find weaknesses faster; past attacks such as Stuxnet show the potential for serious damage.
ticker_line: AI and rising tensions raise risks to critical infrastructure
heading: Regulation

title: Treasury sets out industry’s APRA levies
summary: Treasury plans to collect about $27.2 million from the general insurance industry to support the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) in the next financial year. The overall levy for APRA is estimated at $297.3 million, which includes costs for life insurance as well.
ticker_line: Treasury outlines APRA levies for insurance sector
heading: Regulation

title: Beware knock-on effects of mental health reform: EML
summary: A report from EML warns that changes to mental health support in workers' compensation could lead to more claims in income protection insurance. It calls for better coordination across Australia's support systems to prevent financial vulnerability and improve recovery outcomes.
ticker_line: EML warns of mental health reform impacts
heading: Life Insurance

title: Ombudsman slams icare over wage adjustment delays
summary: The NSW Ombudsman has criticized icare for delays in processing wage adjustments for workers' compensation, which caused financial issues for employers. The Ombudsman recommends icare apologize, offer flexible payment plans, and improve its processes.
ticker_line: Ombudsman criticizes icare for wage adjustment delays
heading: General Insurance

title: NSW confirms workers’ comp premiums
summary: NSW employers will soon get workers' compensation renewal notices, with icare confirming premium settings. The minimum premium stays at $240, and the cap on premium increases for some employers will drop from 30% to 25%.
ticker_line: NSW confirms workers' comp premium changes
heading: General Insurance

title: Perils lifts November storms loss tally
summary: Storms in Queensland and NSW last November caused insured losses of $2.94 billion, according to Swiss data company Perils. The updated figure shows an increase from the previous estimate of $2.66 billion, with most losses coming from Queensland.
ticker_line: November storms cost $2.94 billion in losses
heading: General Insurance

title: Insurers to revisit storm-hit Clifton
summary: Insurers will hold support sessions in Clifton, Queensland on June 8-9 for residents affected by a hailstorm last November. Policyholders can meet with insurer representatives to get help with claims and recovery.
ticker_line: Insurers offer support for storm-hit Clifton residents
heading: General Insurance

title: Industry profit down amid investment slump
summary: The life insurance industry reported a profit of $121 million for the March quarter, a significant drop from $332 million a year earlier, due to lower investment returns and increased claims. Underwriting profits also fell, with individual disability insurance performing best among product classes.
ticker_line: Life insurance profits decline amid investment slump
heading: Life Insurance

title: Housing price slump in Melbourne continues
summary: Melbourne and Sydney are seeing significant drops in housing prices due to high interest rates and new tax changes. In May, Sydney house values fell to $1.58 million, while Melbourne's median house price dropped to $958,000.
ticker_line: Housing prices continue to fall in Melbourne and Sydney
author: Shane Wright and Matthew Knott
heading: Economy

title: Retirement anxiety grows
summary: Many Australians are delaying retirement by up to four years due to rising living costs, with most expecting to work until 66 instead of their desired 62. A new report shows that people now believe they need over $1 million in superannuation for a comfortable retirement.
ticker_line: Australians delay retirement amid rising costs
author: Cameron Micallef
heading: Superannuation

title: Australia:APRA publishes findings of inaugural System Risk Stress Test
summary: APRA's first System Risk Stress Test shows that Australia's banks and superannuation funds can handle severe financial shocks. However, it also reveals vulnerabilities that need addressing as the superannuation sector grows.
ticker_line: APRA stress test shows financial system resilience
author: Jimmy John
heading: Banking

title: Super balances would drop 25pc in a time of severe stress: APRA
summary: The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) warns that in a severe economic crisis, superannuation funds could sell nearly $100 billion in shares and bonds, leading to a 25% drop in average member balances. This stress test highlights the risks posed by the concentration of power among a few large funds in the superannuation sector.
ticker_line: APRA warns of super fund risks in crisis
author: Lucas Baird
heading: Superannuation

title: The main tax, super and other financial changes that start today
summary: Starting July 1, 2026, tax cuts, increased super contribution limits, and changes to parental leave and Medicare thresholds take effect, benefiting workers and families. Key changes include a tax cut for those earning over $45,000, higher super caps, and a boost in paid parental leave to 130 days.
ticker_line: Major tax and super changes effective July 1
author: Rebecca Pike
heading: Economy

title: Stand up to US on AI, says Turnbull
summary: Former Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull urges Australia to demand access to advanced AI models from the US, especially after OpenAI appointed his former adviser Peter Anstee to lead its national security policy in the Asia Pacific. This comes as the US restricts AI access for allies, prompting concerns over cybersecurity and regional technology independence.
ticker_line: Turnbull calls for AI access from US
author: Paul Smith | Technology
heading: AI

title: Cost of comfortable retirement reaches a record high
summary: The cost of a comfortable retirement has risen to $80,000 a year for couples, prompting the government to assist over 2.5 million Australians planning to retire in the next decade. New superannuation reforms aim to help retirees manage their savings better as many fear their funds won't last.
ticker_line: Retirement costs soar, government steps in to help
author: Nina Hendy
heading: Superannuation

title: Super boost for teens
summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers may allow over 500,000 teenagers to receive up to $1 billion in superannuation, as the Greens push to stop companies from avoiding super payments for under-18s working less than 30 hours. Critics say this loophole has cost teens around $405 million in super contributions last year.
ticker_line: Teenagers could gain $1 billion in superannuation
author: Ria Pandey
heading: Superannuation

title: APRA - Response to NCPD non-confidentiality and publications consultation
summary: The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) will move forward with a non-confidentiality determination for the National Claims and Policies Database (NCPD), allowing for a new publication format that includes separate data for cyber insurance and management liability. The first updated publications will include data up to December 2024, with further improvements in usability and timeliness expected.
ticker_line: APRA updates NCPD publication format and data
publication: Australian Government News and Documents via PUBT
heading: Regulation

title: Minutes point to another RBA rate rise in August
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia is likely to raise interest rates in August to control inflation, which is currently at 4%. The RBA has already increased rates three times this year and expects inflation to remain above target for the next two years.
ticker_line: RBA hints at August rate hike to curb inflation
author: Duncan Evans
heading: Banking

title: WIPEOUT OF JIM’S ‘TINY TAX’ RELIEF
summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers' new tax cut of $268 a year is overshadowed by rising mortgage costs and inflation, with rates expected to increase again soon. Homeowners are feeling the squeeze as property values in Sydney drop significantly, raising concerns about affordability and market confidence.
ticker_line: Tax relief overshadowed by rising mortgage costs
author: Jessica Wang, Aidan Devine & Duncan
heading: Economy

title: Financial services: HSBC winds down retail banking
summary: HSBC will close its Australian retail banking after selling $36 billion in loans to Blackstone, marking the end of its 40-year presence in the country. The bank will continue corporate and private banking while winding down retail operations over the next 18 months.
ticker_line: HSBC exits Australian retail banking market
author: Jonathan Shapiro
heading: Banking

title: A challenging year as some super funds go backwards
summary: Some super funds in Australia had a tough year, with Hesta's sustainable growth fund returning only 3.3%, below cash rates and inflation. Other funds performed better, with many achieving returns between 8% and 10%.
ticker_line: Hesta's super fund struggles with low returns
author: Cliona O’Dowd
heading: Superannuation

title: Health rebate cut a stitch-up, says Taylor
summary: Health Minister Mark Butler is cutting private health insurance rebates for older Australians, which could push many out of the system. The opposition argues this will shift costs to state health departments and harm lower-income seniors, while Butler claims it will help fund aged care services fairly across all income levels.
ticker_line: Health rebates for seniors face major cuts
author: NOAH YIM, RICHARD FERGUSON
heading: Health Insurance
